The event begins with an online idea screening and culminates in an offline final round at Karpagam Academy of Higher Education in Coimbatore.

details_text: HackSprint 3.0 — Build Bold. Ride Beyond. About the Event HackSprint 3.0 is a national-level, 36-hour hackathon organized by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Karpagam Academy of Higher Education (KAHE), Coimbatore, in collaboration with the Metaverse Association. HackSprint 3.0 brings together passionate developers, designers, problem-solvers, and innovators from across India to transform creative ideas into impactful, technology-driven solutions. It provides a platform to experiment with emerging technologies, collaborate with like-minded innovators, and tackle real-world challenges. Mode: Online Preliminary Round + Offline Final Round Final Venue: Karpagam Academy of Higher Education (KAHE), Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu Final Hackathon Duration: 36 hours Application Deadline: 28 December 2026 PPT Submission Template: Will be announced soon! How It Works Round 1: Online Idea Submission & Screening The first round will be conducted online. Interested teams must submit a PowerPoint presentation (PPT) outlining their proposed project idea before the application deadline. The presentation should explain: Problem Statement: What real-world problem are you addressing? Proposed Solution: How will your idea solve the problem? Innovation: What makes your approach unique? Feasibility: How can the solution be implemented? Expected Impact: Who will benefit from your solution? Team Portfolio: Relevant projects, technical skills, and previous work, where available. The organizing team will evaluate submissions based on innovation, problem relevance, feasibility, technical approach, potential impact, and relevant portfolio experience. Following the evaluation, selected teams will be shortlisted for the final round. Important: Submitting an application does not guarantee participation in the final hackathon. Only shortlisted teams will be invited to the offline round. Round 2: Offline Final Hackathon Shortlisted teams will participate in the 36-hour offline hackathon at Karpagam Academy of Higher Education, Coimbatore. Participants will develop their proposed solutions, build prototypes, test their implementations, and present their projects to the judging panel. Final evaluation will focus on innovation, technical implementation, functionality, feasibility, problem-solving, and overall impact. Final-round dates will be announced once confirmed. HackSprint 3.0 Tracks 1. Agrotech Leverage technology to address agricultural challenges through smart irrigation, precision farming, AI-enabled agriculture, resource optimization, and sustainable farming solutions. 2. MedTech Develop technology-driven healthcare solutions focused on diagnostics, remote healthcare, medical accessibility, patient monitoring, and improved healthcare delivery. 3. EduTech Reimagine education through digital learning platforms, adaptive learning systems, skill-development tools, inclusive education, and innovative teaching technologies. 4. WildVisionTech Explore AI- and ML-powered solutions for wildlife conservation, anti-poaching intelligence, environmental monitoring, and biodiversity protection. 5. Open Innovation Think without boundaries. Build creative, technology-driven solutions to meaningful real-world problems across any domain. What Awaits You? An opportunity to showcase your creativity and technical skills. A platform to transform ideas into practical solutions. Collaboration with passionate developers, designers, and innovators. An opportunity to present your work and receive feedback from the judging panel. Recognition for outstanding innovation and problem-solving. Prize details, partners, and additional opportunities will be announced through official HackSprint 3.0 communication channels. Rules & Regulations Idea Submission: Teams must submit their project proposal as a PPT before the first-round deadline. Screening: Teams will be shortlisted based on their ideas and relevant portfolios. Final-Round Eligibility: Only shortlisted teams may part

title: Agents that act. Systems that answer. | Free Virtual Agentic-AI Hackathon
description: This free 3-day virtual hackathon challenges student builders to create agentic AI systems designed for real-world tasks. Rather than just building for success, you will focus on how your AI handles failure modes, human oversight, and error reversibility.
eligibility: Students worldwide, working solo or in teams of up to 4.
requirements: No experience required; must build a working agentic AI system for a specific person's task.
details_text: About the Hackathon: Anyone can build an AI demo that works once. Agents that act. Systems that answer. is about what happens when it goes wrong. It's a free, 3-day virtual hackathon for student builders, hosted by StudentChakra and co-hosted by Priyanshu Agarwal (founder of NextMove, organiser of Hackorizon). What You'll Build: An agentic AI system for a real person with a real task. Start with a person, not an industry: who are they, what do they hate doing, what does your agent do for them, and where does it break? Solo or in a team of up to 4. No experience required. How Projects Are Judged: We judge how your project behaves when things go wrong: Failure modes: how does it break? Human oversight: who stays in the loop? Intervention: can someone stop it? Reversibility: can a mistake be undone? Plus usefulness to a real person and the quality of your working build. Prizes: $680 in prizes: 1st place about $500 in Apify credits; 2nd and 3rd place Cursor subscriptions. Judges: Experts from AI governance, cybersecurity, venture and OpenAI, including Dr. Esona Fomuso (formerly VP of Technology, JPMorgan Chase), Dr. Aleem Khalid Alvi (Professor of Cybersecurity & Software Engineering, Sheridan College), Kunal Kapoor (Venture Continuity, Katha) and Priyanshu Agarwal (ChatGPT Lab, OpenAI India). Key Dates: Registration closes: Nov 27 Hackathon: Nov 28–30 (virtual) Final results: Dec 8 Who Can Join: Students worldwide, solo or in teams of 1–4. Free.

title: AI BuildFest 2026
description: AI BuildFest 2026 is a 48-hour online hackathon where you can build custom AI solutions to tackle real-world challenges. Instead of just using existing APIs, you will use the Adaption platform to prepare datasets and train your own unique models. It is a hands-on opportunity to develop a functional prototype and showcase your model-building skills.
eligibility: Teams of 2–4 members, including students, developers, and AI enthusiasts.
requirements: Must use the Adaption platform for dataset preparation and model training to build a functional AI application.
details_text: Overview 48-Hour Online AI Hackathon Organized by Frontend Arena | In collaboration with Adaption Event Dates: December 10–12, 2026 Format: Online Duration: 48 hours Team Size: 2–4 members About AI BuildFest 2026 AI BuildFest 2026 is a 48-hour online hackathon focused on building AI-powered solutions for real-world challenges. It brings together students, developers, and AI enthusiasts to explore how custom-trained AI models can be developed and applied to practical problems. Participants will work in teams to understand a challenge announced during the hackathon, prepare or generate a suitable dataset, train their own model using Adaption’s platform, and build a working solution that demonstrates its capabilities. The event emphasizes practical model development, problem-solving, experimentation, and the creation of useful AI applications. Hackathon Theme Own Your AI: Train a Model That Solves a Real Problem Participants will be challenged to build an AI solution in which a trained model plays a meaningful role in addressing a real-world problem. The official problem statements and challenge requirements will be announced to registered participants during the hackathon. Teams will then have the event period to understand the challenge, develop their approach, train a model, and implement their solution. Challenge Format AI BuildFest will follow a challenge-based format. No specific tracks or problem statements are being published in advance. Official problem statements will be revealed during the hackathon. Teams will select or be assigned a challenge according to the instructions announced by the organizers. The challenge will require participants to develop an AI-based solution using the Adaption platform. Detailed requirements, deliverables, and submission instructions will be communicated when the challenge is announced. Teams should be prepared to work with data, train a model, and demonstrate a functional solution within the 48-hour period. Required Use of Adaption Adaption is the technology partner for AI BuildFest. Teams must use Adaption’s platform as part of their model-development workflow. Dataset Preparation or Generation Teams will use Adaptive Data to transform raw files into a training dataset, or Invent-a-Dataset to generate a dataset suited to their challenge. Model Training Teams will use AutoScientist to train their own model for the selected task. Solution Development Teams will build a functional application or prototype that uses their trained model to address the announced challenge. Demonstration Teams must demonstrate their solution and explain how the dataset and trained model contribute to solving the problem. Participants retain their trained model weights and may publish them on platforms such as Hugging Face or Kaggle, subject to applicable platform terms and data or licensing restrictions. Core requirement: Projects must demonstrate meaningful use of Adaption for dataset preparation or generation and model training. Simply integrating an existing third-party AI API without training a model through the required Adaption workflow will not satisfy this requirement. Technical Workshop A technical workshop led by an Adaption representative is planned before the hackathon. It will help participants become familiar with the platform and its model-development workflow. Planned workshop topics: Introduction to Adaption’s platform Preparing or generating datasets Training models using AutoScientist Technical guidance and participant Q&A Workshop date and time: To be announced Format: Online The confirmed schedule and joining details will be shared with registered participants. title: RedStone Rush 12 Hour Open Innovation Hackathon
organiser: Madan Mohan Malaviya University of Technology (MMMUT), Gorakhpur
description: Continuum 2026 is a two-round open innovation hackathon hosted by NEXSUS at MMMUT, Gorakhpur, focusing on solving real-world problems. Student teams can develop software, hardware, or hybrid solutions, starting with an online idea submission followed by an offline grand finale. It is an opportunity to showcase innovation and technical implementation to a panel of industry experts.
eligibility: Student teams interested in software, hardware, or interdisciplinary technology solutions.
requirements: An online idea submission (Abstract or PPT) for Round 1, and physical attendance at MMMUT, Gorakhpur for the offline Round 2 build sprint.
details_text: Continuum 2026 Hackathon is a two-round Open Innovation competition by NEXSUS at Madan Mohan Malaviya University of Technology (MMMUT), Gorakhpur. The hackathon invites student teams to identify meaningful real-world problems and develop innovative solutions that may be software-based, hardware-based, or hybrid/interdisciplinary . The competition consists of an online idea-submission round followed by an offline grand finale at MMMUT, Gorakhpur . Round 1 — Online Idea Submission Participants must submit either an Idea Abstract or Idea Presentation (PPT) explaining: Problem statement and relevance Proposed solution Innovation and originality Technical approach Feasibility Expected impact Scalability A completed prototype is not mandatory for Round 1. Round 2 — Offline Grand Finale Shortlisted Teams Will Report Physically at Mmmut, Gorakhpur For: Team Verification Orientation Preliminary Idea/technical Presentation Technical Interaction Verification of Existing/baseline Work The 12-Hour Build Sprint schedule Will Be Released Later. Final Evaluation — 100 Marks Problem Understanding & Relevance — 10 Innovation & Originality — 20 Technical Implementation — 25 Functionality / Working Prototype — 15 Feasibility & Scalability — 10 Impact / Practical Utility — 10 Final Demonstration & Presentation — 10 Ai Usage AI-Assisted Tools Are Permitted for Coding, Debugging, Research, Ideation, Documentation, Design and Development Assistance, Provided They Are Used Responsibly. Teams Must Be Able to Explain, Defend, and Demonstrate Every Major Component of Their Solution. Copying Another Team's Solution or Submitting Someone Else's Code/product as One's Own Is Prohibited. Open-Source Libraries, Frameworks, APIs, Models, and Public Development Resources May Be Used Where Permitted, with Relevant Use Disclosed. Previously Developed Personal Components Must Also Be Disclosed. Hardware & Hybrid Projects Hardware and Hybrid Projects Are Welcome. Teams Will Be Evaluated Fairly on Demonstrated Engineering Progress. Working Subsystems, Circuits/prototypes, Simulations, Architecture, Integration Progress and Demonstrated Functionality May Be Considered Where a Fully Fabricated Product Is Not Feasible Within the 12-Hour Sprint. Final Submission Teams Must Provide: Project / Solution Title Concise Project Description Project Repository or Relevant Source/design Files Working Prototype or Demonstrable Implementation, Where Applicable Technology Stack Architecture / Implementation Summary Declaration of Major Pre-Existing, Open-Source and Ai-Assisted Components Final Presentation and Required Backup Demonstration Material Jury Evaluation Will Be Conducted by A Panel Comprising Industry Experts, Working Professionals, Domain Specialists and Experienced/senior Faculty Members . The Decision of The Authorized Jury and Organizing Committee Regarding Evaluation-Related Matters Shall Be Final. Who Should Participate? The Hackathon Is Designed for Student Teams interested in Solving Real-World Problems Through Technology, Innovation and Engineering. Projects Can Be Software, Hardware, Hybrid or Interdisciplinary. Join Whatsapp Group for further updates : https://chat.whatsapp.com/GVzZSCjYIr4Bero0fqzJiE

details_text: Overview Are you ready to explore Full Stack Python Development and Generative Artificial Intelligence? What Will You Learn? Explore the fundamentals of Full Stack Python Development and understand how Generative AI can support modern application development. Workshop highlights include: Introduction to Python programming and its real-world applications Python fundamentals, data types, functions, modules, and object-oriented programming Front-end development concepts using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript Introduction to web development using Python frameworks such as Django or Flask Understanding databases, SQL, and database integration Fundamentals of front-end and back-end application development Introduction to APIs and connecting different application components Understanding Generative AI and its applications in software development Exploring AI-assisted coding, code explanation, debugging, and productivity workflows Introduction to building intelligent applications using Python and AI APIs Understanding project development workflows and industry-relevant technical skills Exploring career pathways in Python Development, Full Stack Development, and Generative AI Why Attend This Free Workshop? Python is widely used in web development, automation, data science, and artificial intelligence. Generative AI is also creating new opportunities for developers to improve productivity, explore innovative solutions, and build AI-enabled applications. By attending this workshop, you can understand the relationship between Full Stack Python Development and Generative AI, identify the skills you may want to learn, and explore how these technologies are used in modern software projects. Quality Thought conducts software training programs and workshops designed to help learners explore technical concepts and emerging IT technologies. Register for the Free Workshop by Quality Thought and discover the technologies, skills, and learning pathways that can help you prepare for a career in software development. title: AI Problem-Solving Workshop: Turn Real Problems into Practical Solutions
description: Turn a real-world problem into a clear, practical solution with UPSC ZONE AI. This online workshop focuses on choosing the right problem, understanding who faces it, and exploring how applied AI can help. What you will…
details_text: Turn a real-world problem into a clear, practical solution with UPSC ZONE AI. This online workshop focuses on choosing the right problem, understanding who faces it, and exploring how applied AI can help. What you will explore • Define a specific problem and the people affected by it. • Explain why the problem is worth solving and how it is handled today. • Develop an AI-assisted solution idea and identify its limitations. • Describe a simple prototype and a practical way to test your idea. Who can participate Participate individually or in a team of up to 10 members under the listed team-participation settings. Bring curiosity, creative thinking, and an interest in problem-solving and AI. Prepare your idea Choose a problem you understand. Summarise the target users, current difficulty, proposed solution, and expected benefit. Clearly identify any assumptions and explain how you would check whether the solution works. How to participate Register on Unstop before the displayed deadline. Review the Rounds & Stages section for the session and submission instructions. Submit your own work and acknowledge any sources or AI tools used. Ready to build a stronger idea? Register and bring a problem that matters to you.

title: Master in Management (MiM) Decision: What It Is, What It Takes, and What You Get
description: The MiM session: Most Master in Management (MiM) advice comes from school marketing or one stranger's forum post. This is the version GradBrew gives paying clients. Who leads it: Led by a GradBrew mentor who: Did a…
details_text: The MiM session: Most Master in Management (MiM) advice comes from school marketing or one stranger's forum post. This is the version GradBrew gives paying clients. Who leads it: Led by a GradBrew mentor who: Did a Master in Management Has spent 8+ years in strategy and finance across six countries Has mentored MiM applicants across the US, Europe and Asia Has been on both sides of this decision, so can tell you what the brochures leave out What the hour covers: Eligibility: whether you are still eligible, which is not about your age and is the question that catches most people out MiM vs MBA vs specialised master's: how they differ, and which your situation actually calls for Programme length: why programmes run anywhere from one to three years, and what a gap year really is Where it is taught: the US and Europe, and why almost no American programme is called a MiM Rankings: how to read one properly, including why most major US programmes are missing from the table and why that has nothing to do with quality Outcomes: what you actually do afterwards, named concretely rather than described aspirationally Your application: what a strong CV, essay, letter and interview look like AI: where it helps you, where it quietly sinks you, and the completely honest mistake that gets applicants flagged as dishonest Who it is for: Anyone considering a MiM in the US or Europe Whether you are a year out or midway through a shortlist If you applied before and did not get in, come Format: 45 minutes of content, then live Q&A, hands or chat Everyone who attends gets the Profile Evaluation Workbook by email afterwards Brew your best. Team GradBrew.

details_text: Note: Mandatory Registration on : https://techfest.org/workshops/prompt-engineering All further updates will be  from Techfest website only ,its mandatory to register in the website . All that you need to know about Techfest Prompt Engineering Workshop Prompt Engineering Workshop: Prompt Engineering is the practice of turning a raw AI model into a precise, reliable tool  structuring instructions well enough to get accurate, consistent, and usable output every single time. It sits at the intersection of human intent and AI systems, going far beyond "how to talk to ChatGPT" to cover grounding prompts in real data, multimodal inputs, and prompt security  the exact standards enterprise AI teams work with in 2026. Today, this skill is being demanded across every function, not just tech roles: software, finance, healthcare, marketing, legal, and education are all pairing domain expertise with the ability to drive AI effectively, a combination that pays a premium over either skill alone. From building multi-step reasoning chains to structuring content so AI search engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Claude actually cite it (Generative Engine Optimization, the AI-era equivalent of SEO), businesses now run on well-engineered prompts, not lucky guesses  and this workshop teaches you to build them. Across two intensive offline days at IIT Bombay, you'll go from foundational prompt structures to a real, evaluated prompt system you'll design, test, and refine yourself  no prior AI or coding background required. Workshop Content Foundations of Prompt Engineering Prompt Structuring & Response Shaping Context, Memory & RAG Domain-Specific & Multimodal Prompting Zero-Shot & Few-Shot Learning Advanced Prompting: Chaining & Reasoning Patterns Adaptive & Self-Optimizing Prompt Systems Prompt Security & Evaluation AI Search & GEO Capstone: Build & Test Systems + Certification

description: Event Title: 2-Day Offline Workshop on Agentic AI & Autonomous Systems Registration: Complete the process at https://techfest.org/workshops/agentic-ai Venue & Format: Lecture Hall Complex, IIT Bombay Campus | Offline…
details_text: Event Title: 2-Day Offline Workshop on Agentic AI & Autonomous Systems Registration: Complete the process at https://techfest.org/workshops/agentic-ai Venue & Format: Lecture Hall Complex, IIT Bombay Campus | Offline (Concept Sessions, Live Demos & Hands-On Practice) Limited Seat available: About the Workshop Agentic AI represents the biggest paradigm shift in applied artificial intelligence since basic chatbots. Modern enterprise solutions are rapidly evolving from simple single-turn systems to fully autonomous, tool-using agents capable of planning, deciding, and acting. This intensive 2-day hands-on workshop covers the entire agent lifecycle—from core reasoning loops and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to multi-agent orchestration, safety guardrails, and real-world deployment. Participants will build functional agents from scratch using industry-standard frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen. Why You Should Attend: Master Next-Gen Tech: Deep-dive into the Model Context Protocol (MCP)—the open standard for connecting models directly to enterprise tools and data. Hands-On Experience: Build, evaluate, and deploy end-to-end agents with real-world execution. Framework Mastery: Gain direct technical exposure to LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and vector database integrations. Production-Grade Design: Learn memory management, Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) checkpoints, system safety, and token-cost optimization. Workshop Syllabus & Core Topics: Agentic Foundations & Architectures: Transition from chatbots to autonomous agents, master the Sense-Think-Act-Reflect loop, explore operational autonomy levels, and identify failure mitigation strategies. LLM Integration & Prompting: Optimize context windows, implement function calling with JSON schema structured outputs, design production-grade system prompts, and analyze model speed/cost trade-offs. Reasoning & Planning Patterns: Implement multi-step reasoning patterns including ReAct, Reflexion, and Tree-of-Thought alongside automated task decomposition and Orchestrator-Worker routes. Tool Execution & Safety Checkpoints: Design robust tool schemas for deterministic APIs, handle errors with auto-retries, optimize execution (parallel vs. sequential), and integrate Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) safety checks. Model Context Protocol (MCP): Build, connect, and sandbox custom MCP servers using standard Host/Client/Server architecture, primitives, and transport mechanisms (stdio vs. HTTP/SSE). Memory Management & RAG Pipelines: Architect dynamic short-term context and persistent long-term memory using vector databases, context engineering, dynamic session state, and high-retrieval RAG. Multi-Agent Systems & Frameworks: Construct peer-to-peer and hierarchical agent topologies using state handoffs, while comparing leading frameworks: LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen. Capstone Build & Deployment: Hands-on experience building, debugging, benchmarking, and applying guardrails to deploy a production agent as an API, Web App, or Chat Interface.

details_text: About: The National Aeromodelling Challenge is presented by Techfest, IIT Bombay, for students passionate about aerospace and engineering. Teams design, build, and fly their own fixed-wing electric RC aircraft that carries golf-ball payloads. They first prove their aircraft can carry and land a payload safely, then complete a timed two-trip delivery mission. Ready-made models are not allowed. Bring your aircraft to life at Techfest, IIT Bombay, Asia’s largest science and technology festival. Structure: The competition has an abstract screening stage, followed by a Qualifier Round and a Main Round at Techfest, IIT Bombay. Eligibility: Open to school, UG, and PG students. Teams can include students from different colleges or schools. Participants must carry a bona fide certificate signed by their HoD/Dean/Principal and a valid ID card. Team Size: 2 to 4 members. A participant can be part of only one team. Problem Statement: Design, build, and fly a fixed-wing aircraft that carries golf-ball payloads (45 g, 43 mm diameter, supplied by organizers) and completes the tasks in each round. Abstract Submission (Online): Submit an abstract of under 15 pages (A4, 1.5 line spacing) in the official Aeromodelling 2026 Abstract Form format. The abstract should cover the aircraft’s basic design (dimensions, wing area, velocity, etc.) and how it suits the problem. Attach a zip file of 5-10 photographs taken while building the aircraft. Abstracts not following the format will not be evaluated. Round 1 - Qualifier Round: Carry one or more golf balls inside the aircraft, fly for at least 30 seconds within a 3-minute window, and land with the payload inside the designated area. Score = (payload weight x 100) / aircraft weight without payload. Each team gets two attempts, and the best counts. The top 30 teams advance to the Main Round. Round 2 - Main Round: Complete a round trip of payload delivery within 3 minutes: load, take off, fly at least 30 seconds, land, unload, reload, take off again, fly at least 30 seconds, land, and unload. Loading must be hands-free, using transmitter-operated compartment doors. Score = E1 + E2 - C1 - C2 - C3. Each delivered golf ball earns 10 points per trip, and each second spent on the ground during loading and unloading costs 1 point. Each team gets two attempts, and the best counts. Overall Score = 0.25 x Normalized Qualifier Score + 0.75 x Normalized Main Round Score. Ties are broken by a separate round framed by the judges. Design Constraints: The aircraft must be designed and built by the team (no RTF/ARF/BNF models). Maximum weight is 1 kg without payload. Thrust-to-weight ratio must not exceed 1 without payload. Wingspan is up to 1.2 m, with no tolerance. Propeller diameter is up to 13 inches, and metal propellers are not allowed. Electric motors only. Gyroscopes, programmed mission steps, FPV, and any flying support are prohibited. Timeline: Registration Deadline: 25th November 2026 Abstract Submission Deadline: 25th November 2026 Abstract Result Announcement: 1st December 2026 Qualifier Round: 15th-16th December 2026 Main Round: 17th December 2026 Rules: Register online to receive a Team ID. No late entries are accepted. The same aircraft described in the abstract must be used in both rounds. Damaged aircraft can be repaired but not replaced. No modifications to the aircraft are allowed after the thrust-to-weight ratio is measured. A 2.4 GHz radio is required. Any other frequency must be informed to the organizers in advance. Landing must be within the inner boundary, otherwise a 20% penalty applies. Touching or crossing the outer boundary disqualifies the attempt. Teams must be ready at their turn, or they lose it. Teams must not share aircraft components with other teams. Safety violations or misconduct will lead to penalties or disqualification. The judges’ and organizers’ decisions are final and binding. Updates will be posted on the Techfest website and sent to registered teams. For official announceme

title: VIT Bhopal University to Host Health Hackathon 3.0 in January 2027
description: Health Hackathon 3.0 is an innovation challenge hosted by VIT Bhopal in collaboration with Johns Hopkins University to develop solutions for global healthcare access. Students can propose ideas in areas like AI, mental health, and low-cost healthcare tools to solve real-world medical challenges. It is a unique opportunity to present high-impact projects and compete for a ₹2 Lakh prize pool.
eligibility: Innovators, students, and researchers.
details_text: VIT Bhopal University will host Health Hackathon 3.0 on 28 and 29 January 2027. A pre-event workshop will take place on 27 January 2027. VIT Bhopal is collaborating with the Whiting School of Engineering at Johns Hopkins University for this event. Its full title is “Health Hackathon 3.0: Global Health Access Innovation Challenge – Next Generation.” New Ideas for Better Healthcare The event has a clear aim: it seeks innovative ideas that can improve healthcare accessibility for more people, reduce costs, and enhance overall efficiency. Participants are invited to propose actionable solutions to real-world healthcare challenges. Key focus areas for submissions include: Low-cost tools and technologies for healthcare delivery. New ways and platforms to support mental health. Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare solutions. Tools leveraging health data analytics to identify and predict health risks. A Chance to Share and Build Ideas Health Hackathon 3.0 invites innovators, students, and researchers to present their concepts and refine them further. The emphasis is on practical, high-impact solutions designed to reach underserved communities and individuals facing healthcare access barriers. Event Overview & Key Dates • Pre-Event Workshop: 27 January 2027 • Main Hackathon: 28 & 29 January 2027 • Venue: VIT Bhopal University, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh • Total Prize Pool: ₹2 Lakh Registration & Submission Registration is now open. Interested teams and individuals must submit their project proposals by 31 October 2026 . To learn more, view participation guidelines, and complete registration, please visit the official Health Hackathon 3.0 event website

details_text: About DOOMFORGE DOOMFORGE is a two-round business and engineering hackathon that challenges participants to combine strategic thinking, market analysis, and practical software engineering. The competition is designed to take participants beyond conventional coding challenges. It begins with identifying real-world business problems and market opportunities, followed by hands-on engineering challenges involving existing codebases and open-source development. Participants will have the opportunity to demonstrate their analytical thinking, technical expertise, creativity, and ability to build practical solutions. Eligibility and Team Formation Open to college students. Team size: 1 - 3 members. Inter-college teams are allowed. Participants from different academic specialisations are welcome to collaborate. Each participant can be part of only one team. All team members must complete the registration process. Competition Structure Round 1: Market Analysis Duration: 4 December – 6 December 2026 Round 1 focuses on business strategy, market research, and problem identification. Participants will be presented with a business-oriented problem or scenario. They must analyse the problem, understand the market landscape, identify opportunities, and propose a feasible solution. What participants need to cover: Problem identification and understanding. Target audience and market analysis. Competitor research and existing solutions. Identification of market gaps and opportunities. Proposed solution, its feasibility, and potential impact. Submission Format: Teams must submit a one-minute video explaining their market analysis, identified opportunity, and proposed solution through Unstop. Evaluation Criteria: Depth of market research. Understanding of the problem. Originality and innovation. Feasibility of the proposed solution. Clarity and effectiveness of presentation. Based on their submissions, selected teams will qualify for the second round. Round 2: Engineering Arena – Open-Source Development The second round is a hands-on engineering challenge in which shortlisted teams will work on one of four dedicated GitHub repositories. Each repository represents a distinct engineering track with its own technical problem space. Participants will be expected to understand the existing codebase, identify areas for improvement, and implement meaningful technical contributions. Potential engineering challenges include: Developing new features and functionalities. Identifying and fixing bugs. Improving application performance and scalability. Implementing security enhancements. Writing automated tests and improving test coverage. Integrating AI/ML-based capabilities. Improving code quality, maintainability, and documentation. Submission Format: All development contributions must be submitted through GitHub Pull Requests (PRs) to the respective repositories. Evaluation Criteria: Functional correctness and completeness. Code quality and maintainability. Technical implementation. Security and reliability. Testing and validation. Innovation and practical impact. Engineering Tracks DOOMFORGE features four specialised engineering tracks, each backed by a dedicated GitHub repository. Participants will work on the repository and technical challenge specified by the organising team. Further details regarding the repositories, technical requirements, and challenges will be communicated to qualified participants. Rules and Regulations Teams must consist of a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 3 members. Inter-college participation is permitted. Each participant may register as part of only one team. Round 1 submissions must be submitted within the specified deadline, from 4 December to 6 December 2026. Round 1 submissions must follow the prescribed one-minute video format. description: About Goa Buildathon ’27: GOA BUILDATHON ’27 is a 36-hour offline hackathon planned for January 2027 in Goa, India. It aims to bring together developers, designers, AI enthusiasts, problem-solvers and innovators from…
details_text: About Goa Buildathon ’27: GOA BUILDATHON ’27 is a 36-hour offline hackathon planned for January 2027 in Goa, India. It aims to bring together developers, designers, AI enthusiasts, problem-solvers and innovators from colleges and communities to turn ideas into working solutions. This is where ideas move beyond discussions and become prototypes. Whether you're exploring AI agents, developing web applications, automating everyday workflows or experimenting with emerging technologies, GOA BUILDATHON ’27 is designed to give you the space to build, collaborate and challenge yourself. Our vision is to create an environment where students can experiment with new technologies, solve meaningful problems, learn from experienced builders and connect with people who share the same passion for creating. Not just another hackathon. A place to turn ideas into reality. What To Expect: 36 hours of offline building in Goa Collaboration with developers, designers and innovators Hands-on experimentation with AI, AI agents and automation Web development, software engineering and emerging technology Teamwork, rapid prototyping and practical problem-solving Opportunities to connect with mentors, judges and technology communities Project showcases and opportunities to present your ideas Community partnerships and potential sponsor-led challenges An environment focused on learning, creativity and building real solutions Who Can Participate?: GOA BUILDATHON ’27 welcomes students, aspiring developers, designers, AI builders and technology enthusiasts who want to learn by building. Whether you're an experienced hackathon participant or attending your first hackathon, the focus is on curiosity, collaboration and the willingness to create something meaningful. Bring your skills, find teammates, explore unfamiliar technologies and turn your ideas into something people can experience. What Can You Build?: We encourage projects across a range of technology areas, including: Artificial Intelligence & AI Agents: Build intelligent assistants, agentic workflows and practical AI-powered applications. Web Development: Create websites, platforms and full-stack applications that address real problems. Automation: Develop tools that reduce repetitive work and improve everyday processes. Data Science & Analytics: Turn data into insights, useful tools and better decisions. Software & Developer Tools: Build products that improve workflows, productivity and collaboration. Electronics & Emerging Technology: Explore innovative solutions that connect software with the physical world. The goal is not simply to present an idea, but to make meaningful progress towards a working solution within the hackathon. Why Goa?: Goa offers a distinctive setting for bringing people together to learn, collaborate and create. GOA BUILDATHON ’27 aims to combine the energy of a technology-building event with a community-driven experience where new connections and ideas can grow. We want participants to leave with more than a project: new skills, valuable connections, practical experience and the confidence to keep building. Event Details: Event: GOA BUILDATHON ’27 Format: 36-hour offline hackathon Location: Goa, India Whatsapp: https://chat.whatsapp.com/KEaIIsIqZhxElIHvivnFDT Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/goabuildathon27 Website: https://goabuilds.com/ Contact: hello@goabuilds.com The event dates, venue, registration details, prize pool and other final arrangements will be announced through official channels once confirmed. Be Part Of The Build: We're bringing together people who don't just want to talk about ideas — they want to build them. If you have an idea worth exploring, a problem worth solving or simply the curiosity to create something new, GOA BUILDATHON ’27 is your opportunity to get started. Build > Collaborate > Create real impact Let's build something that matters.

title: Code Conquest
description: About: An engaging mix of algorithmic strategy, autonomous decision-making, and competitive resource management, this event puts participants in command of programmable rover fleets competing for dominance on an…
details_text: About: An engaging mix of algorithmic strategy, autonomous decision-making, and competitive resource management, this event puts participants in command of programmable rover fleets competing for dominance on an unpredictable battlefield. Participants must design intelligent controllers to explore unfamiliar terrain, gather resources, defend their territory, and outmanoeuvre rival teams. With mechanics ranging from hidden hazards and tactical combat to resource-driven upgrades and enemy vault raids, every decision can shift the balance of the game. The event tests participants' programming skills, strategic thinking, adaptability, and ability to make optimal decisions under uncertainty. The event will unfold in two stages . Prelims (Online): Format: Submission-based programming round hosted on Unstop. Description: Participants develop and submit autonomous rover controllers to compete in a head-to-head, turn-based strategy game. The round challenges participants to explore a simulated environment, gather resources, and outmanoeuvre their opponents through intelligent decision-making. Algorithmic thinking, tactical planning, and efficient resource management are key to advancing. Finals (Offline): Format: On-site interactive competition conducted at IIT Madras. Description: Shortlisted participants compete in a live, turn-based rover strategy game featuring a free-for-all format. Participants must program their rovers to explore the map, mine resources, raid enemy vaults, engage in combat, and manage upgrades to maximise their score. The finals also introduce a dynamic in-game market, adding an economic dimension where participants must make strategic decisions about resource allocation, purchases, and upgrades. Adaptability, tactical thinking, and intelligent resource management will be crucial to securing victory. Date: To be held during Shaastra 2027 at IIT Madras. The event follows a team-based format, with 2–3 participants per team, encouraging collaboration in algorithm design, strategic planning, and resource management. Participants must combine their analytical abilities and technical skills to develop competitive rover controllers and devise effective strategies.

title: Boeing Aeromodelling Competition
description: Event Description Abstract Submission Round Participants must submit an aircraft abstract in A4 format, with 1.5 line spacing and a maximum of 15 pages, along with a ZIP file containing 5–10 construction photographs.…
details_text: Event Description Abstract Submission Round Participants must submit an aircraft abstract in A4 format, with 1.5 line spacing and a maximum of 15 pages, along with a ZIP file containing 5–10 construction photographs. The abstract should cover the aircraft design, including dimensions, wing area, estimated flight speed, reservoir and mounting, release mechanism, leakage prevention, centre-of-gravity management, and safe operation. The prescribed format must be downloaded from the respective IIT website and submitted by email at least 20 days before the competition. Shortlisted teams will be announced 15 days before the competition. If multiple teams participate from the same institution, their aircraft designs must be distinct, with at least a 2.5% difference in wingspan, chord, and fuselage length; otherwise, the teams will be disqualified. Qualifier Round The Qualifier Round aims to select the top 30 teams with lightweight aircraft capable of safe, controlled flight carrying a 1,000 mL water payload. The aircraft must fly safely for at least 30 seconds with the full payload, with no water release required. The water must be stored in a sealed, securely mounted, removable reservoir, with the reservoir and release mechanism included in the aircraft’s empty weight. Judges will inspect the system before takeoff, and there must be no visible leakage. Each attempt must be completed within 3 minutes. Failure to maintain 30 seconds of safe flight or any visible leakage before landing results in a zero score. Each team gets two attempts, with the higher score counted, and only teams that safely complete the loaded flight can advance. The top 30 teams qualify for the Main Round and receive ₹5,000 towards material costs, subject to providing the bank details of one designated team member. Main Round In the Main Round, the aircraft must carry 1,000 mL of water in an inspected, sealed, removable reservoir and release it while flying over the designated simulated fire/release zone. The aircraft must fly safely for at least 30 seconds before release, which must be manually triggered by the pilot using a single transmitter channel; automatic or programmed release is not allowed. Judges will verify that the release begins within the marked zone, which is approximately 40 m from the take-off/landing area, though its location and dimensions may be adjusted based on venue and wind conditions. The amount of water released will be determined by weighing the reservoir before and after the attempt; if leakage before the commanded release cannot be distinguished from the actual release, the attempt scores zero. Each team gets two attempts, with the better score counted, and each attempt must complete the release and landing within 3 minutes. Rules and Regulations The same aircraft must be used throughout all rounds and must match the submitted design; repairs are allowed, but replacement aircraft are not. Teams should carry spare components and be ready when called, or risk losing their attempt or flight time. A 2.4 GHz radio is required unless another frequency is approved in advance, receivers must remain in receiver mode only, and metal propellers are prohibited. All systems will be inspected before the competition, and non-functional equipment can lead to dismissal. Teams must carry their own equipment and cannot share components with other teams. Aircraft may use powered take-off with landing gear or manual launch. A team member cannot participate in more than one team. Teams must be ready to fly after the 120-second interval following the previous attempt or lose their turn. Reimbursement will only be made to a registered team member whose bank account name matches the registration details. Flying outside the designated zone will result in disqualification, and the aircraft must immediately return and land safely. title: Pixels To Prognosis
description: About the Event Gliomas are among the most aggressive brain tumours, and outlining them accurately on MRI is central to diagnosis, surgical planning and treatment monitoring. Doing it by hand is slow, and different…
details_text: About the Event Gliomas are among the most aggressive brain tumours, and outlining them accurately on MRI is central to diagnosis, surgical planning and treatment monitoring. Doing it by hand is slow, and different radiologists often draw the boundaries differently. Pixels to Prognosis asks you to build an AI system that does this automatically. Using multimodal brain MRI scans, your model has to locate a glioma and separate it into its three subregions: active (enhancing) tumour, necrotic core, and surrounding edema. The event combines neuroscience, MRI physics and computer vision. You’ll need more than a model with a good leaderboard score. You’ll also need to understand what the scans show, why models fail, and how to make one that holds up on real clinical data. Who Can Participate Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from any college and any stream Especially suited to students in Biotechnology & Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, and AI & Data Science Teams of 1 to 3 members . Cross-disciplinary teams are encouraged. Competition Structure Round 1: Online Quiz (Screening) This is a case-based quiz on: How MRI machines work and the basics of MRI imaging The biology of brain gliomas and how they appear on MRI scans Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning and Image Processing The questions reward reasoning over memorisation. The quiz is meant to sharpen your problem-solving for the later rounds. Round 2: Model Submission Round Shortlisted teams train a segmentation model on a curated glioma dataset we provide. Each patient has four MRI modalities: T1-weighted, post-contrast T1-weighted (T1ce), T2-weighted and T2-FLAIR. Your model must segment three regions: Whole Tumour, Tumour Core and Enhancing Tumour. Models are ranked on a hidden patient-level test set . Rules: Train only on the dataset provided. No external data. All learnable parameters must start from random initialisation . Pretrained weights are not allowed. You may use published architectures such as U-Net variants. The Colab notebook runtime must be 9 hours or less . Submission requirements: Complete source code (.py / .ipynb) Final trained weights (.pt / .keras) Training logs, including loss and validation curves, config and seed used (.csv) A technical report (.pdf) covering your thought process, pipeline, architecture details and the compute you used Evaluation: Segmentation quality is measured with the Dice score and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance for each tumour region. Scoring also covers anatomical consistency, false-positive control, and the quality of your technical report. Finals: Offline Round at IIT Madras Finalists come to campus and receive a new set of MRI scans with real-world problems. These can include motion artefacts, missing modalities, or pathologies your model has never seen. Each team must: Work out what is wrong with the data and why it happened Adapt the model through preprocessing, retraining or other corrective strategies Present the problems they found, the medical reasoning behind them, and how they handled them Evaluation criteria: Problem identification and medical reasoning Model adaptation strategy and outcome Clarity of presentation and understanding Knowing when your model should not be trusted counts in your favour. Flagging an unreliable case for expert review is part of good clinical AI. Prizes & Recognition Cash prizes for the top 3 teams [prize pool: ₹35000] Special Awards for Best Robust Model and Best Diagnostic Reasoning Certificates of Merit for the winners(Hard Copy) Certificates of Merit for all finalists(Soft Copy) Certificates of Participation for all Round 2 participants Important Dates Registration closes: 28th December, 2026 Round 1 (Online Quiz): 5th December, 2026 Round 2 submission window: 9th - 16th December, 2026 Finals at IIT Madras: 4th January, 2027

details_text: About the Event: Slay CTF is a thrilling, jeopardy-style Capture The Flag competition designed to test your offensive security skills, analytical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. Whether you are a beginner looking to break into the world of cybersecurity or a seasoned hacker hunting for complex challenges, Slay CTF offers a dynamic environment to exploit vulnerabilities, crack ciphers, and trace digital footprints. Put your skills to the test, climb the global leaderboard, and prove your mettle in the ultimate battle of bits and bytes! Eligibility & Registration Guidelines: Target Audience: Open to all students (UG/PG/Diploma), early-career professionals, and self-taught security enthusiasts. Inter-College Teams: Allowed and highly encouraged. Inter-Specialization Teams: Allowed (Open to all branches and backgrounds). Team Size: Participate individually or in teams of [1 - 3 members] . Prerequisites: Eagerness to learn. Challenge Categories (Topics) The CTF will feature a diverse set of challenges scaled from beginner to advanced difficulties across the following domains: Web Exploitation: Uncover vulnerabilities in web applications (e.g., SQLi, XSS, IDOR, SSRF). OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence): Track down hidden information and piece together digital trails across the public internet. Cryptography: Break encryption schemes, decode ciphers, and analyze cryptographic protocols. Digital Forensics: Analyze memory dumps, network packet captures (PCAPs), and hidden file metadata. Reverse Engineering: Deconstruct compiled binaries and understand their underlying logic. Miscellaneous / Sanity: Brain-teasers, scripting challenges, and out-of-the-box puzzles. Event Format & Process Format: Hybrid (Online + JGEC Campus), Jeopardy-Style CTF. Platform: Challenges will be hosted on our dedicated infrastructure ( CTFd). Duration: The competition will run continuously for 3 hours . Scoring System: Dynamic scoring will be implemented (the point value of a challenge decreases as more teams solve it). Process: Once registered on Unstop, team leaders will receive the platform link and credentials via email 24 hours prior to the event kickoff. Rules & Code of Conduct No Flag Sharing: Sharing flags or solutions with other teams is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate disqualification of all involved parties. No Brute-Forcing: Automated brute-forcing of the flag submission platform or challenge infrastructure is forbidden unless explicitly mentioned in the challenge description. No Attacking the Infrastructure: Do not launch Denial of Service (DoS/DDoS) attacks or attempt to compromise the hosting servers. Collaboration: You are free to use Google, AI tools, and public documentation, but collaboration is strictly limited to your own team members. Final Decisions: The organizing team's decisions regarding scoring, disputes, and disqualifications are final and binding. Prizes & Perks Cash Prize, Certification Vouchers and goodies. [NOTE: Cash Prizes and Goodies exclusively for offline participation] Official Certificate of Participation for those who solve at least one challenge.

title: AETHOS - Day Zero
description: If civilization had to begin again tomorrow, what would humanity build first? Unlike conventional hackathons that ask participants to build products around a technology, DAY ZERO challenges teams to engineer the…
details_text: If civilization had to begin again tomorrow, what would humanity build first? Unlike conventional hackathons that ask participants to build products around a technology, DAY ZERO challenges teams to engineer the foundations of an entirely new civilization. Participants are encouraged to think beyond applications and incremental improvements. Every project should solve a meaningful challenge that contributes to rebuilding society—whether through communication, energy, healthcare, infrastructure, education, resilience, exploration, or entirely new approaches that redefine the future. This is not about recreating yesterday. It is about engineering tomorrow. The Mission: Design and develop an innovative solution that would help humanity rebuild after the collapse of modern civilization. Your project may be software, hardware, embedded systems, IoT, AI, robotics, communication systems, cybersecurity, biotechnology, space technology, sustainable engineering, or any interdisciplinary solution aligned with the mission. Projects should focus on solving real-world problems with practical engineering, long-term scalability, and meaningful societal impact. Civilization Pillars: Every project belongs to one of the official Civilization Pillars that represent the essential functions required to rebuild society. The detailed descriptions of all pillars are provided separately. Choose the pillar that best represents the purpose of your solution, not simply the technologies you use. Who Can Participate? Students from any recognized institution are welcome. Participants from all engineering, science, technology, design, management, and interdisciplinary backgrounds are encouraged. Teams must follow the team size specified on the registration page. Innovation thrives when diverse disciplines work together. What Can You Build? We welcome projects across a wide range of domains, including but not limited to: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Embedded Systems & Electronics Internet of Things (IoT) Robotics & Automation Wireless Communication Systems Healthcare & Medical Technologies Renewable Energy Smart Infrastructure Disaster Management Cybersecurity Space & Aerospace Technologies Sustainability Human-Centered Design Frontier & Moonshot Innovations If your solution contributes meaningfully to rebuilding civilization, it belongs here. Submission Requirements: Teams should be prepared to submit: Project presentation Technical documentation Source code repository Prototype or proof of concept Demonstration video (if applicable) Additional submission guidelines and templates will be shared with registered participants. Evaluation: Projects will be assessed on their overall contribution toward rebuilding civilization, including: Innovation Engineering excellence Technical feasibility Scalability Societal impact Resilience Quality of presentation The complete judging rubric is available in the attached documentation. General Rules: All submitted work must be original. Open-source libraries, frameworks, APIs, and development tools may be used with proper attribution. AI-assisted development is permitted unless otherwise specified. Plagiarism or intellectual property violations will result in immediate disqualification. Participants are expected to maintain professionalism and uphold the event's code of conduct. Decisions made by the organizing committee and judging panel will be final. A comprehensive rulebook is available in the attached resources. Why Participate? DAY ZERO is more than a competition. It is an opportunity to think like the engineers who would shape the first generation of a new civilization. Challenge assumptions. Collaborate across disciplines. Build technologies that matter. Engineer systems that could redefine humanity's future. Tomorrow Begins Here. History remembers the civilizations that were built. The next one starts with your idea.

details_text: Business Analytics Workshop: Business Analytics is the practice of turning raw business data into clear, actionable decisions. It sits at the intersection of business thinking and data tools - using spreadsheets, databases, and visualization platforms to spot patterns, forecast trends, and answer real business questions. Today, this practice is being reshaped by AI: natural-language queries, auto-generated insights, and AI-assisted dashboards are changing how analysts work, making the skill faster to learn and more powerful to apply. From sales and marketing to operations and finance, businesses now run on dashboards, not gut feeling - and this workshop teaches you to build them. Across one intensive day, you'll go from raw, messy data to a real dashboard and a business recommendation you'll actually present - no prior coding or analytics background required. details_text: ANAVARAN, presented as part of XAVIESTA 5.0 – KAALCHAKRA, is an immersive sustainability investigation and strategy competition that challenges participants to uncover the gap between corporate sustainability claims and ground realities. Teams of four step into the roles of Sustainability Investigators and Corporate Strategists, investigating Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd., a fictional organisation whose green image may not reflect its actual environmental and social impact. Across three challenging rounds, participants will identify greenwashing, investigate hidden contradictions, assess business risks and develop commercially viable sustainability strategies under real-world-inspired crises. From questioning environmental claims to defending strategic decisions before a jury, ANAVARAN tests critical thinking, ESG awareness, analytical ability and the power to build a genuinely sustainable future. ROUND 1 – GREEN OR GREENWASH? Spot the Illusion Teams will receive a collection of fictional ESG claims, advertisements, sustainability statements, corporate announcements and certification claims made by Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd. regarding its proposed Hooghly Data Park in West Bengal. Participants must critically examine each of the 10 claims and classify them into one of three categories: Genuine Sustainability Greenwashing Misleading Communication Each classification must be supported by a short justification explaining what is being promised, whether the claim is verifiable, what important information is missing and whether the communication creates an exaggerated positive impression. Round Details: Mode: Online on Unstop. Format: ESG Claim Classification + Justification Brief. Case: Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd. – Hooghly Data Park. Number of Claims: 10. Submission: Each claim must include its classification and a justification of 3–6 lines. Qualification: Top 12 Teams advance to Round 2. Evaluation Criteria: Classification Accuracy – 50% Quality of Justification – 40% Clarity of Expression – 10% ROUND 2 – THE GREENWASH FILES Uncover the Truth The qualifying teams will receive a comprehensive investigation dossier containing public statements, internal technical documents, employment projections, renewable energy plans, community partnership updates and environmental assessments relating to Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd. Teams must investigate the contradictions between the company's public sustainability commitments and its internal operational realities. Participants must identify instances of greenwashing, uncover misleading disclosures, assess environmental and social implications, and evaluate the financial, regulatory and reputational risks arising from these gaps. Teams will present their investigation findings and risk assessment before the jury. Round Details: Mode: Offline. Timing: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM (as specified in the event brochure). Format: Case Investigation + Jury Findings Presentation. Case: Detailed investigation of Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd.'s Hooghly Data Park. Qualification: Top 6 Teams advance to Round 3 (Grand Finale). Key Areas of Investigation: Water consumption, groundwater stress and water-positive claims. Renewable energy commitments and net-zero targets. Employment claims and actual local job creation. Farmer partnerships and treated wastewater utilisation. Green certifications and environmental compliance. Financial, regulatory, reputational and social risks. Victory belongs not to the highest spender, but to the team that makes the smartest decisions. Assemble your team, bid strategically and build your empire! details_text: KaalDrishti, presented as part of XAVIESTA 5.0 – KAALCHAKRA, is a business analytics competition that challenges participants to step into the role of Data Investigators and uncover the truth behind a company's crisis. Teams of four will work with fragmented financial records, internal communications, customer data and other business information to identify hidden patterns, detect anomalies and establish the real cause of a problem. Across three challenging rounds, participants will investigate an unsolved business crisis, tackle analytical challenges and defend their conclusions through hypothesis testing and a live boardroom presentation. The event tests analytical thinking, data interpretation, statistical reasoning, problem-solving and the ability to convert data into meaningful business decisions. ROUND 1 – THE CRIME SCENE: FIND THE STORY Project Mirage – Uncover the Hidden Truth Participants will receive a business scenario, problem statement and relevant datasets. The case file will contain fragmented information such as financial records, internal communications, customer data and other business evidence. Teams must independently understand the situation, identify relevant patterns and anomalies, determine the root cause of the crisis and develop a hypothesis explaining what went wrong and why. Based on their analysis, teams must propose feasible business solutions while complying with the given constraints. Round Details: Mode: Online on Unstop Format: Open-Ended Data Investigation + Written Hypothesis Brief Submission: PDF deck of maximum 10 pages, excluding the Introduction and Closing slides. Qualification: Top 12 Teams advance to Round 2. Evaluation Criteria: Understanding of the problem and root cause analysis. Analytical rigour specific to the dataset. Methodology adopted. Feasibility and quality of the proposed business solution. ROUND 2 – THE LOCKED DATA: UNLOCK THE EVIDENCE Xcelerate – Excel E-Sports The qualifying teams will enter an analytical challenge where they will be provided with a dataset and a problem statement. Participants must analyse the given information and develop an optimised solution or analytical model according to the requirements. Teams will be required to demonstrate their analytical capabilities using Microsoft Excel. They can use Excel charts, VBA, Macros and other Excel plugins to develop and present their solutions. However, the final solution must be presented entirely in Excel. The methodology adopted and the plugins used must be explicitly mentioned. Round Details: Mode: Offline Format: Dataset-Based Analytical Modelling and Excel Challenge. Tools: Microsoft Excel, Excel Charts, VBA, Macros and other Excel plugins. Submission/Presentation: The solution must be presented in Excel only. Qualification: Top 5 Teams advance to Round 3. Evaluation Focus: Analytical reasoning. Data interpretation and modelling. Problem-solving ability. Efficiency and accuracy of the solution. Methodology and effective use of Excel tools. ROUND 3 – THE FALSE TRAIL & THE BOARDROOM TRIAL: DELIVER THE VERDICT Find the Real Cause. Defend It Under Fire. The finalists will be presented with multiple plausible explanations for the company's crisis, each supported by a different set of evidence. Only one explanation will represent the actual cause. Teams must test each hypothesis against the evidence collected in the earlier rounds, identify explanations based on bias, false correlation or manipulated data, and trace the crisis back to its Point of No Return — the exact past decision that set the crisis in motion. Participants will then present their final verdict and business recommendations before a jury acting as the company's Board, which will cross-examine their assumptions and conclusions. Round Details: Mode: Offline – Live Defence, Grand Finale. Format: Hypothesis Testing + Live Verdict Presentation + Jury Cross-Examination. details_text: Overview YUGANTAR, presented by FINNOVATION as part of XAVIESTA 5.0, is an immersive marketing strategy competition that challenges participants to rewrite the destiny of a fictional Indian footwear brand. Through three interconnected rounds, teams will investigate the brand's history, uncover the strategic decision behind its downfall, rewrite a defining moment in its journey, and navigate the consequences of their choices. From analysing fragmented evidence and developing revised marketing strategies to tackling real-time marketing crises, participants must demonstrate their consumer understanding, analytical thinking, creativity and strategic decision-making. Here, every decision shapes the future, and every consequence tells a story. Round 1 – The Archive Decode the Brand Teams will receive a fragmented case archive containing old advertisements, consumer reviews, sales data, competitor movements, internal memos and market research relating to Kadam Footwear, a fictional Indian footwear brand. Participants must reconstruct the brand's timeline, identify the single strategic decision that changed its destiny and support their conclusions with evidence from the provided documents. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Online on Unstop Format: Fragmented Evidence Reconstruction + Written Hypothesis Brief Submission: One PDF containing: Reconstructed timeline of 8–12 events in chronological order. Hypothesis brief of maximum 500 words. Supporting evidence with document references. Qualification: Top 12 Teams Evaluation: Timeline accuracy, identification of the turning-point decision, evidence-based analysis and critical thinking. Round 2 – The Butterfly Effect Rewrite the Past The qualifying teams will get an opportunity to change one defining decision from Kadam Footwear's history. They must analyse how this single intervention could have altered the brand's journey, considering its impact on brand equity, market share, profit margins, competitive positioning and consumer perception. Based on their revised historical scenario, teams must develop a coherent marketing strategy and justify the consequences of their chosen intervention. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Offline Format: Single-Decision Rewrite + Revised Strategy Brief Challenge: Rewriting one historical decision and analysing its consequences. Submission: Revised strategy brief. Qualification: Top 6 Teams Evaluation: Strategic coherence, consequence analysis, marketing strategy, positioning and decision-making. Round 3 – The Present Break & Break the Chakra Survive 2027, Then Choose the Future The final round brings the consequences of each team's revised decision into the present. Each finalist will face a team-specific marketing crisis shaped by the changes introduced in Round 2. Teams must allocate a limited marketing budget across digital marketing, influencers, product, retail, partnerships and consumer research to respond to the crisis. They will then face a CEO-level dilemma, choosing whether to Accept, Alter or Reset the brand's future direction. The challenge concludes with a live boardroom presentation and jury cross-examination, where teams must defend their strategy and decisions. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Offline – Live Defence Format: Crisis Budget Allocation + CEO Dilemma + Jury Presentation & Cross-Examination Challenge: Team-specific marketing crisis and strategic decision-making. Finalists: Top 6 Teams from Round 2 Evaluation: Crisis management, resource allocation, consumer understanding, creativity, brand vision and strategic defence. details_text: Eligibility: Open to all undergraduate, postgraduate, and high school students, as well as working professionals and stock market enthusiasts. Fundamental Analysis & Stock Screening: Decoding financial statements (P&L, Cash Flow), key ratios (P/E, ROE, Debt-to-Equity), and building screener filters. Technical Analysis & Chart Reading Basics: Dow theory, dynamic support/resistance, trendlines, and core candlestick patterns (Hammer, Engulfing, Doji). Key Indicators & Trading Signals: Moving averages (SMA vs. EMA), momentum indicators (RSI, MACD), and volume breakout validation. Trading Strategies & Market Psychology: Swing trading, momentum investing, long-term value selection, and emotional discipline. Risk Management & Capital Protection: Position sizing rules, risk-to-reward ratios, stop-loss strategy, and capital allocation. AI Tools for Smart Investors: Leveraging AI assistants (ChatGPT/Claude) for fast quarterly earnings summaries and news breakdown. details_text: All that you need to know about CyberPeace Foundation ISR Innovation Hackathon | Defence Intelligence Summit 2027 Are you ready to build solutions that strengthen the future of digital intelligence and security? Shaastra 2027, the annual technical festival of IIT Madras, in collaboration with the CyberPeace Foundation , invites innovators, developers, AI/ML enthusiasts and content creators to participate in the ISR Innovation Hackathon , a flagship competition of the Defence Intelligence Summit 2027. The competition aims to tackle emerging challenges surrounding AI-generated disinformation, deepfakes and digital manipulation through technology and public awareness. About the Competition The hackathon features two tracks: Track 1: Agentic AI Tools (High Complexity) Build the agent that catches the fake. Develop an autonomous AI agent that monitors simulated social media, messaging and video feeds to detect deepfakes and AI-generated disinformation. Your solution should integrate multiple verification techniques, analyse evidence and generate explainable verdicts with confidence levels. Teams of up to 4 members. Submit a PPT/PDF abstract outlining your proposed solution. Shortlisted teams will demonstrate their working agents at the finale. Track 2: Creator Content (Creative Challenge) Make the reel that teaches the trick. Create an original 30-90 second reel, video or carousel that educates audiences on identifying digital manipulation and misinformation. Choose one theme: Emotional Manipulation Fake Experts Impersonation Manufactured Outrage Forward Before You Think Open to individuals or teams of up to 4 members. Entries can be submitted in any Indian language. Shortlisted participants will take on a surprise live creative brief at the finale. Competition Structure Round 1: Online Preliminary Round Submit your AI agent abstract (Track 1) or original social media content (Track 2). Entries will be evaluated on creativity, originality, accuracy and technical feasibility. Round 2: Offline Finale at IIT Madras The top 10 teams from each track (20 teams in total) will be shortlisted and invited to the IIT Madras campus for the finale. Track 1: Shortlisted teams will demonstrate their AI agents live against a fresh simulated multi-platform feed. Track 2: Shortlisted teams will take on a surprise live creative brief on stage. The finalists will showcase their solutions before a distinguished panel of judges from the CyberPeace Foundation and the defence and technology ecosystem. Key Dates Registrations Close: December 7, 2026 (6:00 PM IST) Doubt Clearance Session: December 10, 2026 Round 1 Submission Deadline: December 13, 2026 (6:00 PM IST) Offline Finale: January 3, 2027 Prizes & Recognition A total prize pool of ₹90,000 is up for grabs! 1st Prize: ₹45,000 2nd Prize: ₹30,000 3rd Prize: ₹15,000 Resources & Guidelines Track 1 participants will work with a simulated multi-platform feed. Live platform scraping and real personal data are not permitted. All submissions must be original. Track 1 solutions must operate within the provided sandbox. Track 2 must not use synthetic media depicting real, identifiable people. AI-generated media must be labelled. Political-party content and material unsafe for general audiences are prohibited. Participants below 18 must provide verified guardian consent. Winning technical systems may be required to be open-sourced. Ready to Make an Impact? Whether you're building an AI agent to detect digital deception or creating content to help people recognise manipulation, this is your opportunity to contribute to a safer digital ecosystem. details_text: Moneyball is a football-themed strategy and management event that combines football knowledge, player auctions, squad building, tactical planning, financial management and negotiation. Round 1 (League Stage): All 10 teams compete in a round-robin league format , where every team plays against every other team. Qualification: The Top 4 teams based on their league-stage performance qualify for the knockout stage. The remaining 6 teams are eliminated from the championship. Transfer Market: After Round 1, a transfer market opens. The Top 4 teams can bid for players belonging to the eliminated teams. Best Negotiator Award: Among the eliminated 6 teams, the team that finishes the transfer market with the highest remaining purse wins the Best Negotiator Award. The Top 4 teams after Round 1 will qualify for the knockout stage. The remaining 6 teams will be eliminated from championship contention but will remain eligible for the Transfer Market and Best Negotiator Award . During the Transfer Market, qualified teams may bid for players belonging to eliminated teams. Eliminated teams have the right to negotiate and decide which offer provides the best value for their player. All transfers must be approved and recorded by the organizing committee before being considered official. Once the Transfer Market closes, no further player transfers will be permitted. The Top 4 teams will use their updated squads for the knockout stage. The knockout stage will consist of two semi-finals followed by a Grand Final . details_text: Overview The Glideator is a newly ideated event introduced for the first time at Shaastra 2026, the annual technical festival of IIT Madras. This exciting challenge is designed to test the stability, maneuverability, and control precision of RC gliders as they precisely navigate through a challenging obstacle course. Participants must rely solely on aerodynamic efficiency and pilot skill — without the aid of powered propulsion — to complete the course with maximum accuracy and control. Competition details: Round 0 - Preliminary Submission: 1) Video Demonstration Each participating team must submit a demonstration video showing : The Glider's control surfaces along with their movement while the glider is at rest. The glider has to be thrown from 3 - 5 metres height without any usage of the control surface and is expected to land safely after at least 10 metres distance. Land safely after a designated spot in a square of radius 2m. The video should consist of measuring the vertical and horizontal distance before and after the launch of the glider. This video demonstrates that the glider possesses sufficient control, maneuverability, and has appropriate range. 2) Technical PDF Submission A detailed technical document must be submitted containing: Glider dimensions and total weight along with a photo of the glider. (The dimensions of any other physical components that are used (like a carbon rod used as a spar) are to be mentioned.) Power source and other electronic components' specifications. Control surface dimensions. Thickness of the balsa wood used for the glider Place the photographs as proofs for each aspect mentioned. A hollow chamber of sufficient size should be arranged in the glider for adding weights in round 2. Round 1 — Glide ratio: Launch: Gliders should cover the greatest horizontal distance possible showcasing their aerodynamic efficiency. Teams must ensure their glider maintains a steady, level flight without erratic movements or stalls. In this round the glide ratio of each team's respective glider would be noted when released from a fixed spot. Round 2 — Obstacle Navigation: In this round, the glider should travel as far as it can and Specified landing zones were positioned at 2-meter intervals from the point of release. Teams were awarded additional points based on the zone in which the glider landed, with the condition that the entire glider must be contained within the designated zone to qualify for the corresponding points. Points were given for distance they travelled and also for landing in the specified zones. Additionally, teams were allowed to add weights (About 5gm each) provided by the organizing team to the glider, earning bonus points based on the number of weights successfully added. Rules and Guidelines Type: Glider(Without any propellor) only. Control System: Manual operation using a remote controller. Autonomous flight is not permitted. Dimensions: Wing span should be 70 - 75 cm and the other dimensions should be based on the wing span and aerodynamic parameters. Material to be used: Balsa wood of minimum thickness 3mm and maximum thickness 5 mm. Placing of foam or any other material between the balsa wood at wings or the body for strength or extra weight is strictly restricted. Stability & Maneuverability: The glider must demonstrate stable flight, precise low- altitude flight, and agile directional control. The weight of the glider should range between 350g and 500g. A hollow chamber of sufficient size should be arranged in the glider for adding weights in round 2. Important Dates: Registration Start: 28-10-2026 Registration Deadline: 10-12-2026 Main Event on: 03-01-2027 Venue: Student Activity Center (SAC), Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Madras Please go through the Problem statement attached below for all the details regarding the competition and for the submissions.

details_text: ROBO OCEANA 2027 – Amphibious Rescue & Recovery Event Overview Robo Oceana 2027 challenges participants to design and operate a self-powered hovercraft capable of navigating land and water to complete a simulated flood-rescue mission.
