Water Navigation: Avoid floating obstacles and navigate simulated currents while maintaining stability and control. Rescue & Recovery: Collect standard payloads (table tennis balls) and heavy payloads (golf balls). Evacuation: Return to land and deposit each payload in its designated rescue zone. Arena Specifications Land zone with smooth and rough surfaces. Sloped land-to-water transitions. Water zone with floating obstacles and simulated currents. Two entry routes: a short, narrow route with bonus points and a long, broad route. Designated payload collection and evacuation zones Technical Requirements Maximum dimensions: 50 × 40 × 40 cm Maximum weight: 4.5 kg Power: Completely self-powered. Battery: Insulated and securely enclosed. Control: RC operation permitted; physical tethers and external steering assistance prohibited. Collisions, incorrect sorting, payloads falling outside designated zones, excessive instability, and exceeding payload limits may attract penalties. title: Aerofloat Shaastra 2027
description: About the Event AeroFloat is an indoor lighter-than-air (LTA) vehicle competition held under the AeroFest vertical of Shaastra 2027 at IIT Madras. Teams design, build, and fly a remotely controlled blimp. Because blimps…
details_text: About the Event AeroFloat is an indoor lighter-than-air (LTA) vehicle competition held under the AeroFest vertical of Shaastra 2027 at IIT Madras. Teams design, build, and fly a remotely controlled blimp. Because blimps operate in a slow, buoyancy-dominated regime that is highly sensitive to control input, the competition tests both piloting precision and real-time combat strategy. Team & Venue Details * Team Size: Up to 3 members per team. * Participation Model: Open registration with an online qualification round. * Venue: Indoor venue at SAC Main Hall, IITM. * Event Duration: 1 day. * Prize Pool: INR 5,000. Competition Stages 1. Online Qualification Round * Every registered team must submit a single continuous, unedited video (maximum 3 minutes, minimum 720p) through Unstop by 10th December 2026. * The video must show controlled climb and descent, controlled yaw (left and right), and an unassisted altitude hold of at least 5 seconds with the vertical-thrust motor switched off. * This round is evaluated on a pass/fail basis to grant an on-site Day 1 slot. Teams may resubmit once before the deadline. 2. Round 1: Precision Navigation * All blimps must pass a Day 1 technical check: the envelope must fit in a box of 1 m x 0.5 m x 0.5 m, helium is the only lifting gas, and the gondola must be custom-built by the team. * Teams pilot their blimp through a 3D course of up to 10 suspended hoops within a 3-minute time limit, scoring 10 points per gate passed in sequence. * The top 6 teams on the leaderboard advance to Round 2 and are seeded 1 to 6. 3. Round 2: Aerial Combat * The top 6 teams compete in a knockout bracket of single duels inside a netted arena, ending in the Grand Final. * The objective is to puncture the opponent's envelope with a team-supplied, removable pin (protruding less than 10 cm from its mount) while protecting your own. * A duel is won when the opponent's envelope is punctured or damaged and visibly loses lift. * Envelope repairs are not permitted. If both envelopes burst before the Grand Final, both teams are eliminated. Key Rules & Requirements * Build Rules: Envelopes must be commercially purchased, while the gondola and electronics must be built from scratch by the team. * Propulsion & Control: The blimp must use electric motors with propellers and be manually controlled by a human pilot, via an RC transmitter or an Arduino/microcontroller linked to a phone or laptop over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth. Autonomous flight is not permitted. * Safety: Helium is the only permitted lifting gas; the use of hydrogen will result in strict and immediate disqualification. Teams must bring their own helium cylinders. * Combat Conduct: Deliberately ramming with the gondola or contacting an opponent's electronics during combat is prohibited and, as judged by the referee, leads to immediate disqualification.

title: Embedded Programming Challenge
description: Embedded Programming Challenge (EPC 2027) The Embedded Programming Challenge is the flagship embedded systems event of Elecfest, IIT Madras, conducted under the Events and Workshops vertical of Shaastra 2027. It tests…
details_text: Embedded Programming Challenge (EPC 2027) The Embedded Programming Challenge is the flagship embedded systems event of Elecfest, IIT Madras, conducted under the Events and Workshops vertical of Shaastra 2027. It tests your expertise across digital design, low-level programming, microcontroller architecture, real-time systems and hardware interfacing, rewarding sharp problem-solving and clean implementation. Every participant will receive a certificate from Shaastra, one of India's premier annual technical festivals! Who Can Register/Participate: Anyone can participate, irrespective of their college or academic background. Intercollegiate and interdisciplinary teams are welcome. Each team can consist of 1 or 2 participants. A participant cannot be part of multiple teams. A laptop is mandatory for both rounds. Syllabus: Digital Logic & Verilog Low-Level Embedded C Microcontroller Assembly & ISA RTOS (FreeRTOS on ESP32) Peripherals & Communication Protocols Sensors & Interfacing Note that the above list is not exhaustive. It is meant to give an idea of what to expect from the event and the areas it will focus on. Event Structure: The competition consists of two rounds. Round 1 is an online qualifier that tests theoretical knowledge of embedded systems. Round 2 is held on campus at IIT Madras and focuses on practical implementation and debugging. Round 1: Duration: 1.5 hours Format: Online proctored quiz with MCQs, fill-in-the-blanks, error detection/missing-code and comprehension-based questions Qualification: Top 25 teams advance to Round 2 Details about the quiz platform and access link will be emailed to all registered participants 24 hours before the event. Marking Scheme: MCQs: +3, −1 Fill in the Blanks: +3, 0 Error Detection/Missing Code: +4, 0 (partial marking applicable) Comprehension: +1 per correct subpart Round 2: Duration: 3 hours Mode: Offline at IIT Madras (Old IE Lab) Qualified teams will be contacted soon after Round 1. Teams will tackle 3–4 mandatory engineering challenges and one elective challenge of their choice. Datasheets and documentation for the components used will be shared beforehand. Participants must bring their own laptops. Instructions for installing the required software will be shared with qualified teams before the round, and all software must be installed and working before arriving. Solutions will be evaluated on functionality, component efficiency, optimisation, creativity and edge-case handling. Rules and Guidelines: Ensure a stable internet connection and a functional laptop/PC for Round 1. Tab switching, communication with others, or use of external assistance or AI tools will result in immediate disqualification. Responses must be submitted before the timer ends; late submissions will not be accepted. Individual qualifiers may pair up before Round 2; two merged qualifiers will be treated as one team. Ties will be resolved using the published round-specific tie-breaker criteria. Participants must strictly follow all instructions and deadlines set by the coordinators and maintain basic etiquette in all interactions with the organisers. Keep checking Unstop and the Shaastra website for updates. Further information will be communicated via groups formed after registration. The decision of the event coordinators will be final in case of any dispute. Certificates: Winners: Hard-copy certificates Finalists: Soft-copy certificates Participants: Soft-copy certificates, awarded only upon attending Round 1 Join Now and Showcase Your Skills!

details_text: Overview: Are you interested in stock markets, trading strategies, and financial research? Here's your opportunity to put your knowledge to the test! Stocks Sena AlphaQuest 2026 is a pan-India competition designed for students passionate about financial markets, trading, and investment research. Organized by Stocks Sena, the competition challenges participants to test their knowledge, explore financial research tools, and experiment with trading strategies. About Stocks Sena: Stocks Sena is a stock market research platform built to make financial research more accessible and comprehensive. It brings together company financials, market-related news, portfolio tracking, and research tools to help users explore listed companies and financial markets. Discover Backtest Lab: One of the key features of Stocks Sena is Backtest Lab , which allows users to define trading strategy parameters and generate backtest reports showing how those strategies would have performed over a selected historical period. Participants can experiment with different parameters, evaluate historical strategy performance, and gain practical exposure to systematic trading strategy analysis. Competition Structure: The competition consists of three rounds: Round 1: Financial Markets Quiz Test your understanding of financial markets, fundamental analysis, valuation, technical analysis, and investing concepts. Round 2: The Stocks Sena Advantage Challenge Explore Stocks Sena's features and demonstrate your understanding of how the platform can support financial research and market analysis. Round 3: Backtest Lab Challenge Use Stocks Sena's Backtest Lab to test a trading strategy over a specified historical period and submit your results for evaluation. Cash Prizes: Compete for a total national cash prize pool of ₹15,000. All-India Rank 1: ₹10,000 All-India Rank 2: ₹3,000 All-India Rank 3: ₹2,000 Potential Internship Opportunities: The competition also offers an opportunity to stand out beyond the leaderboard. National podium finishers may be considered for potential internship opportunities with Stocks Sena , based on their performance, skills, and the company's requirements. This is an opportunity to showcase your understanding of financial markets, analytical abilities, and interest in financial research and technology. Who Can Participate? Students from colleges and universities across India who are interested in stock markets, financial research, investing, or trading strategies are encouraged to participate. Whether you're beginning your journey in financial markets or already have experience analyzing companies and trading strategies, AlphaQuest offers an opportunity to learn, experiment, and compete. Certificates: Participants who meet the competition's participation requirements will receive a digital participation certificate. Join the Challenge: Explore the markets. Test your strategies. Compete with the best student talent across India.

details_text: Immuno Case Files is a case-study-based scientific competition designed to challenge participants to investigate complex immunological mechanisms underlying disease. Focusing on ocular inflammation and autoimmune uveitis, participants will explore the factors contributing to disease progression and analyze scientific datasets to uncover the mechanisms behind disrupted immune regulation. Their task is to interpret the available evidence, formulate research hypotheses, and propose scientifically justified strategies to investigate the underlying causes of ocular inflammation. Guidelines: Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students Inter-college team members are allowed . Inter-specialization team members are allowed. Students will be provided with ONE Problem Statement. Round 1: Screening round(online) Submission of Case Study Report and 2 minute Video in a 4 day window. Round 2: Final Round(Offline) Shortlisted teams will further develop their research proposals and present their findings before a panel of judges. Presentation: 15-20 mins Q&A : 10 mins Rules: Participants must follow the prescribed format, word limit, file format, and submission procedure The judges' decisions will be final, subject to the competition's announced procedures. late submissions are not accepted. However, AI must not replace their independent scientific reasoning, dataset interpretation, hypothesis development, or research design. Participants must verify AI-generated information, cite relevant sources, and ensure their submissions reflect their own understanding and original thinking. AI use must be disclosed wherever required by the organisers. Explicitly state that only winner certificates will be provided as hard copies. Participation and finalist certificates will be issued as soft copies only.

title: Call for Papers: The Arthniti 2026-27
description: About: The Arthniti (ISSN: 2277-1344) is the official peer-reviewed research journal of the Department of Economics at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai. The journal features research papers and articles written by…
details_text: About: The Arthniti (ISSN: 2277-1344) is the official peer-reviewed research journal of the Department of Economics at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai. The journal features research papers and articles written by undergraduate students of economics and related disciplines. Every year, the journal publishes research on a specific theme, enriching the scope and suggesting a refreshing strand of thought to pick upon by the students every year across the disciplines of Economics, Finance, Political Science, Psychology, Technology, inter alia, and this year The Arthniti invites abstracts on the theme ‘Emergence’. Theme: Emergence is the process by which interactions among simple underlying components can give rise to complex behaviours and structures. Often, the ultimate outcome observed is neither intuitive nor reducible to those individual components. This theme looks at interdisciplinary ideas as emerging concepts that rarely respect the boundaries of a single field. Emergence therefore, is not merely change, but it further examines what change produces. An understanding of these processes is therefore imperative to not only navigating uncertainty but also building systems that are resilient to adapting for what comes next. This year, The Arthniti tries to capture the essence of its theme, ‘Emergence’ through diverse research papers. Instructions: This post is a call for paper submissions, that is, a complete research paper of up to 6000 words (excluding References and the Appendix) has to be submitted for the entry to be considered. The paper submissions have to adhere to the following guidelines: All in-text citations, references, tables figures, and depictions to be in the American Psychological Association (APA) 7 format and accurately numbered. The font must be Times New Roman with font size as 12. The paper must follow the following structure: • Abstract: A summary of the entire study, including the methods, findings and future outlook under 300 words. • Introduction: A brief overview of the background of your research study, a brief outline of the various fundamental elements that constitute the phenomenon you seek to explain. • Literature Review: A comprehensive review of literature surrounding the chosen subject, using any method of review. • Objectives: The various steps/methods/processes used as part of the study in answering the research question, in brief. • Hypothesis: The primary and secondary research questions that the author of the study seeks to answer, including the hypothesised relationship between the variables of the study. • Methodology: An exhaustive overview of the methods, datasets, models, processes that have been utilised in your research paper. • Policy Recommendations (if applicable): Actionable and empirical policy implications of your study. • Limitations: A transparent declaration of the pitfalls that you encounter in the process, or any information that hampers the validity or scope of the claims being made by the study. • Conclusion: A brief summary of the study. Since the journal is ISSN-indexed, all submissions made must be exclusive to The Arthniti, and any duplicate papers will be regarded as plagiarism. The journal maintains stringent academic standards, and any plagiarism or AI-generated textual usage will lead to disqualification of the submission. Note: Please submit your entries through this form link.

title: MindShift - The Science of Decisions
description: Overview: Why do we remember some things and forget others? How does the brain shape our perception, behaviour and decisions? MindShift is a three-round competition exploring neuropsychology, cognition and human…
details_text: Overview: Why do we remember some things and forget others? How does the brain shape our perception, behaviour and decisions? MindShift is a three-round competition exploring neuropsychology, cognition and human behaviour. Through application-based challenges, scientific research and problem-solving, participants will investigate how cognitive processes influence the way we think and interact with the world. Designed for curious minds across disciplines, MindShift encourages scientific reasoning, critical thinking and evidence-based decision-making. No prior specialisation in neuroscience or psychology is required. Eligibility: Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from all academic disciplines. Participants may register individually or in teams of 1–4 members. Competition Rounds Round 1: Brain Basics | Online Quiz An application-based quiz covering foundational concepts in memory, attention, perception, learning, cognitive biases and decision-making. Questions will focus on applying concepts to real-world scenarios rather than relying solely on factual recall. A preparatory reference document will be provided before the round, making it accessible to beginners. Round 2: NeuroDesign | Submission Round Shortlisted participants will receive a challenge brief requiring them to approach an unfamiliar neuropsychological problem through scientific reasoning, research and creative problem-solving. Teams must develop a structured response, justify their approach and consider its feasibility within the given constraints. The challenge will run over two days, with detailed instructions, deliverables and evaluation criteria released at the start of the round. Final Round: Offline Finale | IIT Madras The finalists will participate in an interactive, research-driven neuropsychology challenge at IIT Madras on 2 January 2027 . Teams will investigate a neuropsychological condition, explore its underlying mechanisms using credible scientific literature, and develop an evidence-informed solution or intervention concept. Teams will submit their research and proposed approach with appropriate citations and present their findings to a judging panel. Detailed task requirements and evaluation criteria will be shared with the finalists. Evaluation Criteria: Participants will be evaluated on scientific understanding, analytical reasoning, research quality, creativity, feasibility, problem-solving and communication. Detailed, round-specific judging criteria will be communicated to participants. Prizes Total Prize Pool: ₹35,000 The prize pool of ₹35,000 will be distributed among the top three teams, with ₹18,000 for the 1st place, ₹10,000 for the 2nd place, and ₹7,000 for the 3rd place. Winner certificates will be provided in hard copy. Finalist and participation certificates will be provided digitally. Why Participate? Explore the science behind human cognition, engage with scientific research and tackle challenging problems that go beyond conventional quizzes. Develop skills in research, critical thinking, scientific communication and teamwork while investigating the fascinating relationship between brain function and behaviour. Think critically. Investigate the evidence. Discover the Science of Decisions.

title: Petri Dish Challenge
description: Overview: Beyond the naked eye lies a universe of chaos, beauty, and hidden potential. Are you ready to decode it? The Petri Dish Challenge invites budding microbiologists to identify an unknown bacterial culture using…
details_text: Overview: Beyond the naked eye lies a universe of chaos, beauty, and hidden potential. Are you ready to decode it? The Petri Dish Challenge invites budding microbiologists to identify an unknown bacterial culture using standard microbiological techniques. Participants will explore bacterial isolation and culture, Gram staining, biochemical tests and antibiotic susceptibility testing. They must analyse experimental data, draw scientific conclusions and present their findings clearly. The event consists of an online quiz round followed by an offline laboratory round at IIT Madras. Participants will be shortlisted for the final round based on their performance in the online round. Target Audience: Students interested in: Microbiology and microbial identification Biotechnology and biomedical sciences Wet-lab techniques, bacterial culture and biochemical analysis Experimental reasoning and scientific interpretation Eligibility: Undergraduate and postgraduate students from all disciplines, including engineering, science, medical, arts, commerce, management and law. Format: Round 1: Online Quiz Platform: Unstop Format: Online quiz covering biotechnology, microbiology and microbiology laboratory techniques Structure: Approximately 30–40 questions Dates: December 12-13,2026 Participants must attempt at least one quiz to be considered for qualification to the offline final round. Final Round: Offline at IIT Madras Location: UG Labs, IIT Madras Dates: January 4–5, 2027 Participants will receive an unknown bacterial sample and conduct laboratory investigations, including: Staining and cell morphology, including cotton blue staining Cell count and viable cell determination Antibiotic susceptibility testing and Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) Lactose fermentation and extracellular enzyme activity/synthesis Motility testing and biochemical characterisation The final round includes hands-on experiments, lab report preparation, live presentations and a viva. Evaluation Criteria: Selection and execution of appropriate laboratory tests Accuracy of observations, recordings and interpretation Scientific reasoning and evidence supporting bacterial identification Quality and clarity of the lab report and presentation Performance during the viva examination

title: NITRO GP
description: NITRO GP is an adrenaline-fuelled, nitro-powered RC car racing championship hosted at Shaastra, bringing together hobbyists, students, and professional racers from across India to enjoy the thrills of navigating…
details_text: NITRO GP is an adrenaline-fuelled, nitro-powered RC car racing championship hosted at Shaastra, bringing together hobbyists, students, and professional racers from across India to enjoy the thrills of navigating challenging turns, ramps, and rugged terrain in a test of speed, precision, and control. The competition celebrates creativity, engineering expertise, technical craftsmanship and sharp reflexes, pushing both the machines and their drivers to their limits. Competition details: VIDEO SUBMISSION: Each team must submit a clear video showcasing their car's composition, functionality, and performance on a test track. The video should highlight that it is a 1:8 Nitro fuel-based RC car which is functional.It must be submitted before the deadline for evaluation and shortlisting. QUALIFIERS: All teams have to go through a 3-lap time trial round. Each driver’s fastest time in this qualifying round will be considered. The Top 16 proceed to the next round and are slotted according to their positions in this round. ROUND ROBIN: The teams are split into 4 groups and race among themselves in the group. The top 2 of each group directly proceed to the next stage, whereas the third-place team of each group goes into a revival round. REVIVAL: The 3rd-place teams race each other where the first-place team also advances to the semifinals. QUARTER-FINALS: 9 teams are seeded and race out of which 6 teams head to the semifinals. SEMI - FINALS: 2 high-stakes races of 3 cars each; the top 2 of each race proceed to the finals. FINALS: Teams that qualify from the semi-finals will advance to the final race. The final race will be of longer duration.Pit stops are available. Grid positions for the final will be based on the number of laps completed in the semi-final (in the given time). Rules & Guidelines: Open only to Nitro fuel-based 1:8 RC buggies; further specifications regarding the cars are mentioned in the PS. Further rules and guidelines are available in the Problem Statement.

details_text: Overview – Trust No One. Question Everything. AUDACIA 2026 | 11th Integrity & Ethics Conclave | Symbiosis Centre for Information Technology (SCIT), Pune Description In a boardroom where everyone has an agenda, can you really trust the person sitting next to you? Welcome to THE UNSEEN HAND, an exciting offline corporate social-deduction challenge inspired by the popular game Among Us, where business strategy meets mystery, deception, and unexpected twists! Imagine stepping into a corporate boardroom where critical decisions must be made, challenges arise without warning, and every individual appears to be working toward a common objective. But appearances can be deceiving. Behind professional conversations and convincing arguments, hidden motives and conflicting interests may be at play. As situations evolve and uncertainty grows, participants must rely on their observation, strategic thinking, communication, and decision-making abilities to navigate the boardroom. Will you recognize the warning signs before it's too late? Can you distinguish a genuine ally from someone quietly influencing the outcome? In this boardroom, every decision matters, every conversation counts, and trust might be your greatest strength or your biggest vulnerability. Get ready for a game where corporate intelligence meets psychological strategy, and nothing is quite as straightforward as it seems! Eligibility Mode: Offline Registration Platform: Unstop Team Composition Team Size: 3-4 with a twist Team Allocation: Final playing teams will be determined by the organizers on the event day. Important: Participants registering or arriving together may be assigned to different teams. Pre-registered groups are not guaranteed to play together. Be prepared to collaborate with unfamiliar faces, build new alliances, and adapt to an unpredictable boardroom environment. Competition Format Mode: Offline Venue: SIC Campus, Pune Enter the Boardroom The Unseen Hand places participants in a simulated corporate environment where they must navigate business challenges, interpret information, collaborate with others, and make decisions under uncertainty. The competition combines elements of: Corporate Strategy and Decision-Making Social Deduction and Observation Communication and Persuasion Logical and Critical Thinking Teamwork and Adaptability Crisis Response and Problem-Solving Participants will encounter evolving challenges that test their ability to balance strategy, judgment, and trust. Expect the Unexpected! In the corporate world, the most important developments are not always announced in advance. The Unseen Hand embraces this uncertainty through unexpected scenarios, shifting circumstances, and challenges that demand quick thinking. There's more to this boardroom than meets the eye! Certain aspects of the gameplay will remain confidential until the event to preserve fairness, suspense, and the element of surprise. The organizers will explain the applicable rules, instructions, and evaluation process before the relevant gameplay stages begin. Remember: The most dangerous move might be the one you never saw coming. What Will the Challenge Test? Participants should be prepared to demonstrate: Strategic Thinking & Decision-Making: The ability to evaluate situations, consider alternatives, and make informed decisions under pressure. Observation & Analytical Reasoning: The ability to recognize inconsistencies, interpret information, and identify important details in complex situations. Communication & Persuasion: The ability to communicate ideas, question assumptions, and present convincing arguments. Adaptability & Collaboration: The ability to work with unfamiliar participants, respond to unexpected developments, and navigate changing circumstances. Specific scoring mechanisms and challenge-wise evaluation criteria will be communicated by the organizers as applicable. Important Dates & Timeline Registration Opens: 19th October, 2026 Registration Closes: 28th November

description: AdVenture: Brand. Buzz. Boom. AdVenture is a three-round marketing and brand strategy competition at Strategia’27. You play an advertising and marketing agency: you develop, defend and adapt a campaign for a real…
details_text: AdVenture: Brand. Buzz. Boom. AdVenture is a three-round marketing and brand strategy competition at Strategia’27. You play an advertising and marketing agency: you develop, defend and adapt a campaign for a real product from a real brand. The competition tests how well you understand consumers, spot market opportunities, think creatively and make strategic decisions under pressure. Across three rounds, your team builds a campaign strategy, responds to a marketing crisis affecting the same brand, and defends every decision in an undisclosed live finale. Focus areas: consumer insight, brand and market relevance, creative thinking, strategic thinking and problem diagnosis. Who can participate: any UG or PG student currently pursuing their education. Team size: exactly 2 members (no solo entries). Round 1: Pulse Check, The Brief (Online) Submission deadline: 5 Jan 2027 The real product and brand for the case are announced at the start of the round [on date]. Your team develops a campaign concept for the brand and submits either a slide deck (PPT/PDF) or a single poster, strictly following the format in the round brief. The highest-performing teams advance to Round 2. Round 2: The Red Alert, Crisis (Online) Submission deadline: 25 Jan 2027 Your team receives a marketing crisis or product problem connected to the same brand and case as Round 1. It may be a PR setback, declining relevance, a repositioning requirement or a failed launch. You diagnose the problem and develop a revamped marketing brief containing the problem diagnosis, a fresh strategic direction, key messaging and a proposed course of action. This round tests how you respond to the unexpected, rethink a campaign and stay aligned with the brand. Round 3: The Full Throttle (Offline) Date: 16 Feb 2027 | Venue: Loyola College, Chennai The final round is an undisclosed surprise challenge, revealed only when the round begins. Finalists think on their feet and defend the campaign from Round 1 and the crisis response from Round 2 before the judging panel. It tests strategic clarity, adaptability, confidence and your ability to justify marketing decisions under pressure. Key Rules Submit only in the official format given in each round’s brief. Late or unofficial submissions will not be considered. [The use of AI tools, chatbots or automated assistants is strictly prohibited in every round.] Submissions must be original. Plagiarism, impersonation or any other malpractice leads to immediate disqualification. Carry a valid institutional ID, which may be checked at any stage. The decisions of the judges and the Organising Committee are final and binding.

title: FrAudit
description: FrAudit: Where the Numbers Never Lie, But People Do FrAudit is Strategia’s flagship auditing and forensic accounting competition, designed to take participants beyond textbook learning and into the real-world work of a…
details_text: FrAudit: Where the Numbers Never Lie, But People Do FrAudit is Strategia’s flagship auditing and forensic accounting competition, designed to take participants beyond textbook learning and into the real-world work of a statutory auditor and forensic investigator. Instead of testing memorised theory, it simulates a professional audit engagement with incomplete information, conflicting evidence, financial statement risks, internal control weaknesses, fraud scenarios and time pressure. Across three progressively challenging rounds, you move from an online audit knowledge qualifier, to an intensive forensic investigation, and finally to a live “Cook & Catch” finale, where one team creates a realistic financial manipulation and another team must detect it. Who can join: any UG or PG student currently pursuing their education. Familiarity with Indian audit standards and regulations is preferred, but not mandatory. Team size: 2–3 members (no solo entries). Round 1: Audit IQ, Concept and Case Challenge (Online) Date: 29 Jan 2026 | Duration: 30 minutes | Platform: official online examination portal This round tests your understanding of auditing concepts and your ability to apply them to practical business situations. The focus is on application, reasoning and professional judgment rather than memorisation. Part A, Audit Concepts: audit planning and risk assessment, internal controls, audit evidence and documentation, procedures and assertions, materiality and professional skepticism, fraud risk, ethics and auditor independence, substantive testing, vouching and verification, analytical procedures, revenue, inventory, receivables and payables, and basic forensic audit awareness. Part B, Audit Case Studies: practical scenarios on financial statement risks, internal control weaknesses, fraud risks, audit evidence, and revenue, inventory, receivables, purchases and payroll, including choosing the right audit procedures and auditor responses. The test has 40 objective questions , about 60% conceptual or application-based and about 40% case-based. Difficulty progresses from basic to challenging professional-judgment scenarios. The round is strictly timed, and the portal auto-submits when time expires. The top teams advance. Round 2: The Red Flag Files, Forensic Investigation Round (Offline) Date: 15 Feb 2027 | Duration: 60 minutes Each team receives a sealed audit file for a fictional company: a realistic mix of routine and manipulated records such as purchase orders, tax invoices, GST returns, salary registers, bank statements, ledger extracts, inventory records, vendor master, emails, delivery challans, payment vouchers, journal entries, fixed asset register, audit trail, cash book and trial balance. Fraud is rarely contained in one document, so you must cross-reference the records and build an evidence trail. You will: Trace transactions across multiple documents. Identify numerical, date and authorisation inconsistencies. Detect suspicious transactions and potential fraud schemes. Explain why each item is suspicious. Recommend audit procedures such as vouching, confirmation and physical verification. Submit a structured Audit Observation Sheet. You are evaluated on red flag identification, cross-referencing quality, reasoning and explanation, recommended audit procedures, and presentation and documentation. The top 10 teams advance to the Finale. Round 3: Crooked Books, The Cook & Catch Finale (Offline) Date: 15 Feb 2027 | Format: live two-phase forensic simulation The top 10 teams are divided into two groups, Fraud Accountants and Auditors, and paired head-to-head. Each pair gets the same business scenario. Phase 1, The Cook (90 minutes): the Fraud Accountants receive a genuine, internally consistent set of books and deliberately introduce believable manipulation, such as window dressing, premature revenue recognition, inflated expenses, inventory inflation, shell vendors, payroll manipulation, backdated journal entries, concealed liab

title: CaseQuest
description: CaseQuest is a business strategy and case-study competition, in Strategia'27 that brings together sharp analytical thinking, decision-making under pressure, and live presentation skills, testing participants across a…
details_text: CaseQuest is a business strategy and case-study competition, in Strategia'27 that brings together sharp analytical thinking, decision-making under pressure, and live presentation skills, testing participants across a series of progressively challenging rounds. The competition begins with a two-part online qualifier , followed by a live branching case-study round, and concludes with a Grand Finale where the top teams present a brand-new case before a judging panel. Participants will be evaluated on: Depth of analysis Clarity and structure of explanation Quality of decision-making Awareness of Trade-Offs and Risks Ability to adapt strategy Consistency of decisions Guidelines: Open to all registered UG/PG students. Every round is played in teams of exactly 2 members - individual participation is not allowed at any stage. Both members register together, and the same two-member team continues across all rounds; changes are allowed only in exceptional cases, at the Organizing Committee's discretion. Carry a valid institutional ID card at all times - it may be checked at any stage. Use of AI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, etc.), internet search, or unauthorized notes/textbooks is strictly banned unless a round specifically allows it. Teams may only communicate with their own teammate - contact with other teams or outside help is not permitted. Only the materials explicitly permitted for a round may be used; all other devices and references are prohibited. Only responses submitted in the official format/portal are evaluated - loose sheets or unofficial submissions are not considered. Once submitted, responses are final and cannot be edited or resubmitted. Violations such as AI use, plagiarism, impersonation, or unauthorized assistance lead to immediate disqualification. Decisions of the Judges and Organizing Committee on evaluation, rules, and disputes are final and binding - no re-evaluation requests are entertained after results are declared. The Organizing Committee may revise rules, format, or schedule if required, and will inform all participants in advance. Stages & Timelines: Stage 1: Online Qualifier (Jan'26) Date: 27th & 28th January, 2027 Duration: TBA Platform: Unstop Guidelines : A two-part quiz that narrows the full field of registered teams down to the 50 teams who advance to Stage 2. Part A - General Round (Current Affairs & Business Awareness): Open to all registered teams . Questions cover general current affairs together with foundational business and economic awareness. All registered teams compete in Part A. Each part includes a mix of regular questions and Star Questions - Star Questions carry bonus/higher marks than regular questions. Scored on total marks earned (regular + Star Questions); the top teams (by cumulative score) advance to Part B. Ties are broken by time taken to complete the round - the faster team is ranked higher. Part B - Advanced Business Round: A more in-depth quiz restricted to the top teams who cleared Part A, testing deeper business, finance, and industry knowledge. Open only to the teams that qualify from Part A. As in Part A, a mix of regular questions and higher-value Star Questions is used; Star Questions carry bonus marks. Scored on total marks earned (regular + Star Questions); the top 50 teams (by cumulative score) advance to Stage 2. Ties are broken by time taken to complete the round - the faster team is ranked higher. Stage 2: The Case Study Round (15 Feb'27): The centrepiece of the event. Teams work through a live, branching business case and are evaluated on the judgment behind every decision - not just the decisions themselves. The Stage 2 case is released to the qualifying teams only once Stage 1 (Parts A and B) has concluded and the qualifying teams are confirmed. Format: Each case presents a company facing a real-world business challenge. Each case consists of four sequential decision points. At every stage, participants choose one of the available strategic option

details_text: Official Competition Guidelines Theme: The Things We Don’t Question Organized Collaboratively by: D-LAB, Design Community (IISER Berhampur) with Art Clubs of Other IISERs Overview & Thematic Brief: We navigate daily life governed by unexamined habits, systemic norms, invisible social defaults, and unquestioned cultural agreements. ARTICULATE invites designers to interrogate the familiar challenging viewers to pause, reflect, and ask critical questions about the everyday realities we take for granted. The Theme: The Things We Don't Question: The Things We Don’t Question: Use the medium of graphic design to explore an assumption, belief, behaviour, practice, or system that has become so familiar that we rarely stop to question it. Your poster should make the familiar feel unfamiliar, something that makes people pause, think, and question what they usually take for granted. ARTICULATE invites thinkers, illustrators, graphic designers, and creative minds across India to disrupt this visual complacency. Your artboard is an analytical instrument to surface hidden paradoxes, challenge accepted defaults, and construct visual metaphors that make viewers reconsider their everyday assumptions. Thematic Scope & Satirical Commentary / Critiques: Prohibition on Use of Direct Personalities & Real-World Entities’ Identities. Critique must remain systemic, structural, and conceptual. Use allegory, generic archetypes, visual metaphors, and symbolic representation rather than literal real-world identities. Submissions must maintain ethical design standards, completely avoid personal attacks, hate speech, or defamation, and channel their visual commentary into universal, thought-provoking ideas. Design Specifications & Technical Requirements: Format & Dimensions: Submissions must be exactly A4 size (portrait orientation recommended). Quantity: One original poster submission per registered participant. Thematic Alignment: Every submission must demonstrate a rigorous, creative, and critical interpretation of the theme, The Things We Don't Question. Submission Deliverables: Participants must compile and submit all three mandatory deliverables via the official registration portal: High-Resolution Poster Image: One export in JPG, JPEG, or PNG format (minimum 300 DPI recommended). Source / Editable Design File: The original editable working file in PSD, AI, SVG, or other industry-standard formats. For designs authored in Canva, an unrestricted editable or template share link must be provided. Portfolio & Concept Document (PDF): A single PDF containing: A full-page high-resolution preview of the poster. A structured written rationale (up to 250 words) articulating the conceptual premise, creative methodology, design iterations, and social or moral values reflected within the artwork. Mandatory Social Engagement & Verification: To ensure transparent public exhibition and complete validation of participation, entrants must fulfill all of the following steps prior to the deadline: Follow @design_iiserbpr on Instagram. Post the finalized poster on Instagram as a Collaborator Post with @design_iiserbpr. Include the concept rationale / artist statement within the post caption or in the post itself. Tag the following institutional and partner accounts in the caption: @design_iiserbpr @artclub_iisertirupati Note: Collaboration acceptance and tagging of all partner entities are compulsory requirements for jury review. Prizes & Rewards (Total Prize Pool: ₹10,500) The competition offers a comprehensive prize pool valued at ₹10,500, distributed across direct cash rewards, Amazon gift vouchers, and official honors: Overall Prize Pool: ₹10,500 (inclusive of Cash Prizes & Amazon Gift Vouchers). 1st Place (Winner): ₹3,000 + Amazon Vouchers / Certificate of Excellence 2nd Place (First Runner-Up): ₹2,000 + Amazon Vouchers / Certificate of Excellence 3rd Place (Second Runner-Up): ₹1,000 + Amazon Vouchers / Certificate of Excellence Special Mentions (3 Positions): ₹500 eac

title: Molequest Case Challenge
description: MOLEQUEST Case Challenge is a competition for people who love to read, think and connect the dots. Teams (1-4 members) will dive into biological puzzles, work out what’s happening at the molecular level, and build…
details_text: MOLEQUEST Case Challenge is a competition for people who love to read, think and connect the dots. Teams (1-4 members) will dive into biological puzzles, work out what’s happening at the molecular level, and build solutions that hold up when the evidence takes an unexpected turn. The event is structured in three rounds, each one testing a progressively deeper layer of scientific competence: conceptual knowledge, analytical depth and real-time adaptability. The theme is Epigenetics. So, think like scientists and find what the epigenome is hiding. Eligibility: Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students Target Audience: Students interested in Epigenetics and Genomics Molecular Biology Biotechnology Biochemistry Biomedical Engineering Plant and Agricultural biotechnology Competition Rounds: Round 1: Online Quiz This quiz will test grasp of basic molecular biology and epigenetics fundamentals, the toolkit you will need to crack the cases ahead. Be prepared to think fast and be sharp to earn your place in the next round. Round 2: Submission Round In this round, teams will be given a set of cases. Teams pick one of the cases, study the data provided, and submit a written report, answering the questions given in the case document. Finals at IIT Madras: Offline Round Teams arrive with a prepared PPT based on their Round 2 work and will be given a sealed envelope revealing new findings. They are then given 1 hour to rework their PPT adding any changes in their reasoning. They should then defend their Round 2 report and explain what changes and doesn’t change in their reasoning because of the new information to a panel of judges.

details_text: All that you need to know about Robo Run Guidelines: A team shouldn't contain more than 5 members. Bot Dimensions:  Smaller than 20 * 20  cms. Participants are required to build an autonomous (not to be operated by a remote controller) line follower Bot, which can reach the end point of a maze in the shortest possible time. ( The line thickness will be 3-4 cm) Video submission round: This will be a submission round! You will have to prepare a small maze with two curves and show your line-following bot running on it. Shoot a video clip and attach the file. Round -1: In round 1, every team will be given a chance to run through the maze. The top set of teams will be qualified to final round. Shortlisting will be done based on the points you acquire. Refer to the problem statement for scoring criteria. Round -2: In round 2, the maze will additionally contain yellow blocks (10cm*10cm*10cm) directly placed on top of yellow squares. These yellow blocks are to be displaced from the square. The sqaures will act as a checkpoint only if the block is displaced completely. The maze and scoring pattern will be different between the two rounds. Robo Run Description: A Bot shall not be larger in length or width than 20 cm. There are no restrictions on the height of a Bot. A Bot should essentially comprise a drive motor to move it; a steering and turning method; sensors to detect the maze turns; sensors to ignore the action of the rest Bots and a source to provide power. A Bot shall be self-contained (no remote controls). A Bot shall not use an energy source employing a combustion process. Required sensors may be used for identifying the block and the maze line. A Bot shall not leave any part of its body behind while navigating the maze. A Bot shall not jump over, fly over, climb, scratch, cut, burn, mark, damage, or destroy the line of the maze. Judges can debar any machine if it is likely to cause damage to the maze in any way. title: BREAKING BID : Presented by MARG The Management Society of Ram Lal Anand College
description: Competition Description Step into the world of strategy, business, and decision-making, where every choice has consequences and every move can create an opportunity. This competition challenges participants to think…
details_text: Competition Description Step into the world of strategy, business, and decision-making, where every choice has consequences and every move can create an opportunity. This competition challenges participants to think critically, understand market dynamics, and make strategic decisions under pressure. Combining a knowledge-based quiz with an immersive bidding and brand-building challenge, it tests both conceptual understanding and practical business acumen. Participants will progress through two rounds, moving from testing their knowledge and reasoning to applying their skills in a competitive business simulation. Think strategically. Bid wisely. Build intelligently. Round 1: Online Quiz The first round is an elimination-based online quiz designed to assess participants' knowledge, logical reasoning, analytical thinking, and decision-making abilities. The quiz will feature a diverse mix of questions covering business and economics concepts, marketing psychology, consumer behaviour, logical reasoning, and real-world business scenarios. Participants will be required to go beyond theoretical knowledge, interpret situations, identify patterns, and choose appropriate solutions under time constraints. Format: 20 questions 30-minute duration Multiple-choice, logical reasoning, and scenario-based questions No negative marking One attempt per team Performance in this round will determine qualification for the next stage. Round 2: The Bidding Challenge The second round takes participants into a competitive business simulation where strategic thinking, resource allocation, and calculated decision-making become essential. Teams will receive a fixed amount of virtual capital and compete to acquire business assets through a bidding process. Each asset offers distinct advantages and trade-offs, requiring participants to balance their ambitions with their available resources. Using their acquired assets, teams must develop a viable business, establish their market positioning, and demonstrate how their resources work together to create a competitive advantage. The challenge extends beyond bidding, requiring teams to justify their decisions, manage constraints, and respond strategically to unexpected market developments. The objective is not simply to acquire the most expensive assets, but to make intelligent investments and build a business capable of succeeding in a competitive market. Teams will be evaluated on their strategic decisions, resource management, business viability, adaptability, and overall performance. Rules and Regulations Participants must register in teams of 3–4 members. Each participant may be part of only one team. Qualification for the offline round depends on performance in the online quiz. Each team is permitted one quiz attempt, submitted by a designated team member. The online quiz must be completed within the stipulated time and in a single sitting once started. No negative marking will apply to the online quiz. Shortlisted teams must participate in the offline round according to the instructions provided by the organisers. During the bidding challenge, teams must operate within their allocated virtual capital. Borrowing and transferring credits between teams are not permitted. Teams must comply with the bidding rules, asset-acquisition requirements, and evaluation criteria communicated before the offline round. Any misconduct, plagiarism, or use of unfair means may result in disqualification. Participants must carry a valid college ID for the offline round. The organisers' and judges' decisions regarding evaluation and competition outcomes will be final and binding.

title: Aven Journal by Kartexa — Call for Research Papers
description: Have a research idea, an innovative solution, or findings worth sharing with the world? Aven Journal by Kartexa invites research paper submissions across multiple disciplines. A nonprofit publishing initiative by…
details_text: Have a research idea, an innovative solution, or findings worth sharing with the world? Aven Journal by Kartexa invites research paper submissions across multiple disciplines. A nonprofit publishing initiative by Kartexa, Aven Journal aims to make scholarly publishing more accessible by offering a platform where contributors can share their research and readers can access published work for free. Whether you are a student writing your first research paper, an independent researcher exploring a new idea, a professor advancing academic knowledge, a teacher sharing educational research, or an organization presenting research findings, we welcome your contribution. Our vision is simple: make research accessible, encourage knowledge sharing, and give ideas a platform to grow. Who Can Participate? The call for papers is open to: School and college students Undergraduate and postgraduate students Research scholars Independent researchers Professors and academic faculty Teachers and educators Colleges, universities and academic institutions Research organizations and other eligible organizations Institutional affiliation is not mandatory for independent researchers. Research Areas: We welcome original research and scholarly contributions in relevant disciplines, including: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Computer Science and Information Technology Engineering, Robotics and Emerging Technologies Natural and Applied Sciences Mathematics and Statistics Education and Learning Sciences Business, Economics and Management Social Sciences and Humanities Environmental Studies and Sustainability Agriculture and Interdisciplinary Research Submissions must fall within the journal's scope and comply with its editorial and publication policies. Types of Submissions: Depending on subject suitability and the journal's editorial policies, contributors may submit: Original research papers Review articles Interdisciplinary research Case studies Applied research Research-based technical papers Why Submit to Aven Journal? Free Publication There are no manuscript submission or publication fees. Free Public Access Published articles are available to readers without subscription or access charges. Inclusive Research Community Students and independent researchers can participate without requiring a university affiliation. Cross-Disciplinary Knowledge Sharing Contribute research across science, technology, education, humanities and other relevant disciplines. Accessible Research Records Published articles can have dedicated article pages with author attribution, abstracts, keywords and citation information, according to the journal's publication workflow. Submission Guidelines: Before submitting: Prepare an original manuscript relevant to the journal's scope. Include the title, abstract, keywords, author details and references. Ensure that all listed authors have approved the submission. Include applicable research ethics approvals and conflict-of-interest information. Follow the official author guidelines. Submit your manuscript through the official journal submission process. All submissions are subject to editorial screening and the journal's applicable review process. Submission does not guarantee acceptance or publication. Read the author guidelines and current publication policies before submitting.

details_text: About the Opportunity: Idea to Income: 50K is an entrepreneurship challenge by the InteractUP Startup Committee that gives selected teams the opportunity to turn their business ideas into revenue-generating ventures. Selected teams can receive ₹10,000 per month for 5 months, amounting to up to ₹50,000 in funding, to build, execute, and validate their ideas. Unlike a traditional business plan competition, this challenge focuses on execution, revenue generation, and measurable business outcomes. What Is the Challenge? Pitch a practical and scalable business idea . Explain how you will start and operate the business. Show how you will use the ₹10,000 monthly funding . Generate real revenue and profits through execution. Track your business performance every month. Demonstrate how you can recover the investment and generate profit . This isn't just an idea-pitching competition. Your idea will be tested through execution and numbers. Make sure you are part of the following group for regular updates: https://chat.whatsapp.com/HrgxdxPQEn9DAlp4PFH6d0 Round 1 - 90-Second Business Pitch Submit a 1 to 1.5-minute video covering: Business Idea - What are you planning to build? Problem - What problem or need are you addressing? Launch Plan - How will you start the business? Outline the expenses you expect to incur and the revenue you aim to generate, month by month, over the five-month period. Detailed 1st month description Capital Plan - How will you use the ₹10,000 received each month? Revenue Model - How will you generate revenue? What will your costs, revenue and expected profits look like? 5-Month Plan - How will you grow and improve the business? Investment Recovery - How will you recover the investment while generating profit? Your video should demonstrate a clear, practical, and financially viable plan. We are more interested in the numbers and execution strategy than just the business idea. Explain how you will acquire customers, what you will pitch to them, your expected ticket size, and who your target customers are. If you are proposing a product, explain the per-unit cost, sourcing or manufacturing process, pricing, and expected profit margin. The interview will evaluate: Practicality of the business idea Financial viability Execution strategy Revenue potential Scalability Understanding of the target market Ability to use limited capital effectively Round 2 dates will be announced soon. Based on the interview evaluation: Final teams will be selected. Profit sharing will continue as per the terms agreed with the selected teams until the applicable recovery/profit objective is achieved. Detailed terms will be communicated to shortlisted/final teams. What Can You Build? You are not restricted to a particular industry. Some areas you can explore: Healthy Food: Healthy snacks Meal concepts Beverages Nutrition-focused products Experiences & Events: Stranger meets Cultural events Community experiences Curated social gatherings ️ Travel & Experiences: Strangers' trips Weekend experiences Local tours Curated group activities These are only examples. Your idea can come from any sector, provided it has a practical path to execution and profitability. Preferred Location: Delhi NCR is the preferred location for execution. title: EO Mumbai Global Student Entrepreneur Awards 2026
description: The EO Global Student Entrepreneur Awards (EO GSEA) is the premier event for student entrepreneurs worldwide. Student entrepreneurs compete against their peers from around the world in a series of local competitions to…
details_text: The EO Global Student Entrepreneur Awards (EO GSEA) is the premier event for student entrepreneurs worldwide. Student entrepreneurs compete against their peers from around the world in a series of local competitions to qualify for the EO GSEA Global Finals. EO GSEA is an Entrepreneurs’ Organization (EO) program. EO Mumbai chapter is bringing this opportunity to the student community in India. Structure: Application-based screening: The applications received will be filtered out on the basis of the information provided and the top shortlisted individuals will move ahead for the further rounds. EO Mumbai Finals: Shortlisted student entrepreneurs will be participating in the EO Mumbai Finals. Global Finals: All the Finalists from different clusters will then compete in the Global Finals for the ultimate battle. Prizes and Rewards: EO Mumbai Round: INR 5,75,000 EO Global Finals: USD 100,000 (plus a Paid International Trip for all finalists) Eligibility criterion to compete in the Global Student Entrepreneur Awards (GSEA): You must be enrolled for the current academic year in a university/college as an undergraduate or graduate student at the time of application. Full-time enrollment is not required; part-time enrollment is acceptable. You must be the owner, founder or controlling shareholder of your student business. Each company can be represented by only one owner/co-founder - studentpreneur. Your student business must have been in operation for at least six consecutive months prior to the application. Your business must have generated US $500 or received US $1000 in investments at the time of application. You should not have been one of the final round competitors from any previous year’s GSEA Global Finals Competition. The competitor must be 18-30 years of age. Note : Graduate students are eligible to apply only if they have continually enrolled in a university following their undergraduate degree and have not left school to work on their business or to seek other employment. Exceptions can be made for students who have taken up to one academic year off before beginning their postgraduate education.

description: Continuum 2027 Ideathon is an innovation and pitching challenge for students who can identify meaningful real-world problems and transform them into original, practical and scalable ideas . Participants will move from…
details_text: Continuum 2027 Ideathon is an innovation and pitching challenge for students who can identify meaningful real-world problems and transform them into original, practical and scalable ideas . Participants will move from problem identification → solution structuring → live pitching → jury Q&A . A working prototype is not mandatory . The focus is on the quality of the problem, originality of the solution, feasibility, impact, scalability and the ability to communicate and defend the idea. The Ideathon is part of CONTINUUM 2026 , the technical festival organised by NEXSUS at Madan Mohan Malaviya University of Technology, Gorakhpur . The festival brings together students, builders, problem-solvers and emerging-technology enthusiasts. Eligibility: Open to eligible college/university students. Participants from colleges/universities outside MMMUT may also participate. Individual and team participation may be permitted as per the final registration configuration. Only registered participants/teams will be considered for the competition. Competition Format Stage 1 — Problem & Idea Identify a meaningful real-world problem and define a focused solution. Ideas may address technology, sustainability, education, healthcare, mobility, finance, social impact, campus innovation, business/process innovation or other relevant domains. Stage 2 — Structure the Solution Develop a concise pitch covering: Problem statement Target users/stakeholders Key insight Proposed solution Innovation/originality Implementation approach Feasibility Expected impact Scalability/sustainability Stage 3 — Live Pitch & Q&A Teams present their idea before the jury at MMMUT, followed by a Q&A session. Participants must be able to defend their assumptions, solution choices, feasibility and expected impact. Evaluation — 100 Marks Criterion Marks Problem Understanding & Relevance 15 Innovation & Originality 25 Feasibility & Practicality 20 Impact & Value Creation 15 Scalability / Sustainability 10 Pitch Clarity & Communication 10 Response to Jury / Q&A 5 Total 100 AI & Originality Policy AI tools may be used for research, ideation, analysis, design and presentation preparation. However, participants remain responsible for the originality and accuracy of their submission and must understand and defend their major claims, assumptions and solution choices. Copied ideas, plagiarised presentations, false ownership claims or deliberate misrepresentation may result in penalty or disqualification. General Rules The idea must be original and meaningfully address a real problem. External research and existing products may be referenced for learning and comparison but must not be presented as the team's own work. Participants must follow the instructions of the organising team and jury. Jury decisions regarding evaluation and ranking will be final. Organisers reserve the right to disqualify submissions violating competition rules, originality requirements or participant conduct standards. Final event instructions, pitch duration and other operational details will be communicated by the organisers. Tagline: Turn a real problem into an idea worth building.

title: Pixel2Path 2027
description: Event Description: Pixel2Path is an autonomous robotics competition where teams build a robot that turns digital images into physical drawings on paper, with no human intervention. It combines Machine Learning, Computer…
details_text: Event Description: Pixel2Path is an autonomous robotics competition where teams build a robot that turns digital images into physical drawings on paper, with no human intervention. It combines Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Path Planning, Robotics, and Mechatronics. Online Submission: The teams have to submit the 'Documentation', 'BOM', and 'Video-Demonstration' of the bot. (Non-Eliminatory Round) Round 1 : The robot receives an unseen image (PNG/NPY), processes it, plans an optimized path, and draws it on an A3 sheet within the allotted time. Round 2 (Draw) : Each team gets an image with 40% of its strokes randomly removed. Their trained AI model predicts the missing strokes, and the robot draws the completed image (visible and predicted strokes) on A3 sheet. Round 2 (Predict) : Teams get 10 unseen masked images and predict the originals. Each is scored by SSIM. Teams get 100 image pairs two weeks before the event. On event day they get the full 5,000-pair dataset and a 60-minute window to train their model on Kaggle. Rules: Teams must have 3 to 5 members, with one designated Team Lead for official communication. Teams must bring a fully assembled and tested robot (no on-day mechanical builds), a laptop with all software pre-installed, the trained model weights file, a 12V DC power supply, and a USB cable for Arduino. It must be a 3-axis plotter (X, Y, and a Z pen-lift) with independent control of each axis. The robot must have an Emergency Kill Switch that completely stops all motion. Training must be done in a Kaggle Notebook on event day with GPU acceleration, with Internet toggled OFF. Training must be from scratch, using only the provided 5,000-image dataset. Data augmentation is allowed.

title: goSTOPS Marketing Case Study | The Road Less Booked | ₹30,000 Prize Money + Internship Opportunity
description: goSTOPS Marketing Case Study – The Road Less Booked ₹30,000 prize pool | Internship opportunities | Real-world marketing challenge What would it take to get young travellers to book a place they wouldn't normally…
details_text: goSTOPS Marketing Case Study – The Road Less Booked ₹30,000 prize pool | Internship opportunities | Real-world marketing challenge What would it take to get young travellers to book a place they wouldn't normally consider? At goSTOPS, we're tackling two real business challenges: driving demand for a mountain-view hostel outside Kasol's main market, and turning Alibaug into a more accessible destination for budget travellers beyond the weekend. In The Road Less Booked , you get to choose one of these challenges and build a marketing strategy around it. The challenge Option 1: goSTOPS Kasol PLUS The property is located outside Kasol's main market, away from the route most travellers typically follow. How would you turn its offbeat location and mountain views into a reason to book? Option 2: goSTOPS Alibaug Alibaug is often seen as a destination for villa stays and premium weekend trips. How can goSTOPS make it more appealing to budget-conscious young travellers, especially from Monday to Friday? Choose one property and build your solution around its specific business problem. What you'll work on This isn't just a campaign-ideas exercise. Your solution should be grounded in consumer behaviour and practical business thinking. Consumer research: Survey young travellers aged 20–35 to understand their travel preferences, barriers, brand awareness and stay choices. Present your key insight. Marketing strategy: Define your priority audience, positioning, channels and scalable marketing ideas, supported by a campaign cost breakdown. Campaign execution: Develop a campaign concept and show 2–3 sample executions across your chosen channels. We want to see original thinking, real consumer insights and ideas that could work in the real world. Who should participate? If you're interested in marketing, brand strategy, consumer behaviour, travel, growth or business problem-solving, this is your opportunity to put those skills to work. Team size: 1–3 members Format: Online Registration deadline: 30 November 2026, 11:59 PM IST Rewards A total prize pool of ₹30,000, along with internship opportunities. Refer to the official competition details for confirmed reward terms and eligibility. Ready to take on the challenge? Choose your property, understand the traveller, and build a strategy that gets them to take The Road Less Booked. Register on Unstop before 30 November 2026. At goSTOPS, we believe that some of the best ideas come from people who are willing to question the obvious, look at problems differently, and turn challenges into opportunities. Through this case competition, participants will get a chance to showcase exactly that — their ability to think critically, collaborate effectively, and build solutions that are both creative and practical. Bring your ideas. Bring your curiosity. Bring your problem-solving mindset and get ready to see how far you can take your solution!

details_text: About the event: Building India Case Study Competition is the largest undergraduate case study competition in India engaging students to solve challenging governance problem statements on Education, Sports, Public Health etc. Selected students get the opportunity to present their solutions in front of subject matter experts and government stakeholders. The theme of the fourth edition is "Substance Use". The problem statement is “How can India strengthen demand-side interventions to prevent and reduce substance use among youth by 2030?" Participants are required to submit a scanned copy of their college ID at every round of the competition for verification purposes. Participants can register individually or in teams of two. Participants are expected to develop implementable and scalable approaches that strengthen prevention, encourage early intervention, mobilise communities and leverage existing institutional mechanisms to create healthier environments for young people. Platforms like LinkedIn and Instagram are no longer just social media platforms . LinkedIn has become a powerful space for professional networking, recruitment, thought leadership, and career opportunities, while Instagram has evolved into an important platform for personal branding, content creation, community building, and showcasing your personality, skills, and interests. Your resume may get you a foot in the door, but your digital presence can determine whether people remember you, trust you, and want to connect with you. Whether you are a student looking for internships, a fresher searching for your first opportunity, or a professional building industry connections, having a strong and authentic personal brand can significantly strengthen your professional journey. LinkedIn Launchpad is designed to help participants understand the importance of social media in today's professional ecosystem and express ideas, build credibility, and express your POV. The competition will challenge you to think about real-world issues, form your own opinions, and communicate those opinions effectively through LinkedIn. Responses must maintain professional and respectful language. Participants must repost the given problem on LinkedIn along with their own thoughts and perspectives, as instructed. Judging Criteria Participants will be judged on the quality and originality of their thoughts, creativity, clarity of communication, relevance of their perspective, professional presentation, and overall effectiveness of their content and personal branding. title: BRICS 2026 (Online): Operation De-Dollarization | Along with Friendly Networking Track
description: BRICS 2026: The De-Dollarization Summit A Pan-India Diplomatic Simulation What happens when the world's emerging economies come together to reshape the global financial order? Step into the world of international…
details_text: BRICS 2026: The De-Dollarization Summit A Pan-India Diplomatic Simulation What happens when the world's emerging economies come together to reshape the global financial order? Step into the world of international diplomacy, economics and strategic decision-making with BRICS 2026: The De-Dollarization Summit , a pan-India mock BRICS competition designed to test your understanding of global affairs while putting your negotiation, public speaking, strategy and teamwork skills to the ultimate test. Participants from across India will come together and be divided into teams representing different BRICS member countries. Each participant/ team will be assigned a country and will be expected to research its economic interests, geopolitical priorities and international position over the given agenda. The teams will then enter a simulated BRICS summit where they will negotiate, collaborate, debate and defend their country's interests around one central idea: Can BRICS reshape the global financial system through de-dollarization? Teams will be required to negotiate and work towards a common agenda or action plan that addresses the central issue. The summit will conclude with the teams attempting to reach consensus and pass a final resolution with the required majority of participating countries. This isn't just a debate. It is a simulation of international diplomacy where every decision, alliance and negotiation can influence the final outcome. We will also conduct one networking track so that all participants can connect with each other and make new friends and connections. What Will You Do? Represent a BRICS member country and understand your country's economic and geopolitical interests Develop a position on de-dollarization and negotiate with other countries Build strategic alliances/Defend your country's interests Participate in diplomatic discussions and negotiations and Present your final strategy and proposed framework Respond to challenges and developments introduced during the simulation What Skills Will You Test? Go beyond textbooks and experience how geopolitics, economics and diplomacy come together in the real world. Develop your strategic thinking, negotiation, research, public speaking and leadership skills while representing a country and making high-stakes decisions. Walk away with a deeper understanding of international relations, global finance and diplomatic decision-making, along with practical experience in teamwork, persuasion and problem-solving. Why Participate? Because this is more than a conventional competition; it is a global competition, where you compete with partipants from different geographies and challenge yourself to upscale. You won't simply answer questions or prepare a presentation. You will step into the role of a country and experience how international diplomacy actually works. Whether you are passionate about economics, finance, international relations, public policy, geopolitics, debating or simply looking for an intellectually engaging experience, this competition gives you a platform to think, negotiate, strategize and lead . title: Custom Paper Bags: How Small Brands Can Get Better Packaging
description: Custom Paper Bags That Make Sense for Growing Brands: Custom paper bags should work for your product, your customers, and your budget. Whether you're selling candles at a local market, shipping beauty products, or…
details_text: Custom Paper Bags That Make Sense for Growing Brands: Custom paper bags should work for your product, your customers, and your budget. Whether you're selling candles at a local market, shipping beauty products, or preparing for retail shelves, the right bag can make your brand feel more considered without forcing you into an expensive packaging order. The Cheapest Bag Isn't Always the Smartest Choice: Generic paper bags cost less upfront, but they can leave your branding looking disconnected. A coffee shop with premium products and a thin, poorly printed bag sends a mixed message. That doesn't mean you need luxury finishes. You need the right balance of paper quality, size, handles, and printing. Before ordering, check: Does the bag support the actual product weight? Is the size right, or are you paying to ship space? Will the print match your approved brand colors? Can the supplier handle your order quantity without surprise charges? I've seen small brands order thousands of bags before testing one with their actual products. That's an easy mistake to avoid. Choose Paper Bags That Fit Your Selling Channel: Your packaging needs change depending on where customers receive the product. A boutique beauty brand may need sturdy bags with twisted paper handles. A candle company should consider the weight and shape of glass jars. A retail brand preparing for store shelves needs consistent sizing and printing across different product lines. Keep Your First Order Manageable: Here's what actually works for early-stage brands: start with a quantity you can reasonably use, then scale when demand becomes predictable. Alora Packaging: Supports this approach with low MOQs, free design support, and free structural samples. That gives founders room to test a bag before committing to a large production run. No die or plate charges also help avoid costs that weren't part of the original budget. Alora Packaging has shipped for more than 10,000 brands, but the practical lesson is simple: get the size right, test the strength, and make sure the final cost works for your business. If you're planning a new bag order, start with your product dimensions and budget. A quick conversation with Alora Packaging can help you figure out what makes sense before you commit.
