description: Mandatory Registration at: techfest.org/competitions/thetashift ThetaShift is a high-octane robotics challenge held as part of Techfest 2026-27 . Participants must design and construct a manually controlled, wireless…
details_text: Mandatory Registration at: techfest.org/competitions/thetashift ThetaShift is a high-octane robotics challenge held as part of Techfest 2026-27 . Participants must design and construct a manually controlled, wireless spherical robot built to navigate dynamic terrain, clear precision-based obstacles, and handle surprise course features . The top 5 teams from the Zonals round will qualify for the Grand Finale at the IIT Bombay campus from December 16–18, 2026 Key Rules & Technical Specifications: Bot Dimensions & Drive: Must be a wireless spherical bot with a diameter between 4 and 10 inches . Control Mechanism: Controlled manually via a joystick/remote or a mobile phone using 2.4GHz WiFi or Bluetooth . SSID format must follow TeamName_TF . Power Constraints: Onboard power supply only (≤ 24V DC for electric setups) . A physical power-disconnect switch is mandatory . Build Constraints: No ready-made Lego parts (ready-made gear assemblies permitted) . Spikes, abrasive materials, or adhesives damaging the track cause immediate disqualification . Arena & Challenge Breakdown: The 3x3m arena features 12 distinct terrain obstacles designed to test control, traction, and task execution : Terra Firma: Rock and sand path (50 Points) The Slalom Ridge: Triangular zig-zag barriers (30 Points) Sawtooth Ridge: Contiguous triangular speed bumps (30 Points) Infinity Circuit: Figure-8 path (60 Points) Domino Planks: Unevenly spaced rectangular planks (40 Points) Incline Overdrive: 10-degree incline ramp (40 Points) The Razor’s Edge: Elevated 7-inch wide track without side barriers (60 Points) Freefall Hairpin: Downhill slope ending in an immediate 90-degree turn (70 Points) The Gridlock: Alternating block grid path (30 Points) The U-Turn: Strict U-turn maneuver (20 Points) Bulldozer Drive: Pushing a block across a line and exiting in reverse (50 Points) Surprise Obstacles: Confidential obstacles introduced during the Grand Finale . Gameplay, Scoring & Time Limit: Time Limit: 6 minutes (360 seconds) per run . Each team gets 1 run . Scoring Formula: $\text{Total Score} = A + T - P$ A: Task Points earned (Max 480 Points) T: Time Bonus = 240 - Time in seconds (for runs under 4 minutes; Max 100 Points) P: Penalties (10 points per arena violation or extra pause time) Pauses & Resets: Two 45-second and one 30-second technical pauses allowed . Off-track bots reset to the start of the current obstacle with a 10-point penalty . Timeline & Rewards: Grand Finale: December 16–18, 2026 at IIT Bombay Campus . Certificates: Certificates of Excellence for the top 5 teams per zonal city and top 3 finale winners . Participation E-Certificates for teams crossing the benchmark score .

title: One Day workshop on Advanced Ensemble Learning Techniques for Supervised Machine Learning using Python 2026
description: This Workshop aims at providing a forum for members of the research and academy community. The Workshop enables the participants to understand the recent technologies in ML Foundations, ensemble techniques such as…
details_text: This Workshop aims at providing a forum for members of the research and academy community. The Workshop enables the participants to understand the recent technologies in ML Foundations, ensemble techniques such as Boosting, Voting, and Stacking, along with their practical implementation using Python. The One-Day Workshop on Advanced Ensemble Learning Techniques for Supervised Machine Learning aims to provide participants with a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental concepts, advanced methodologies, and practical applications of ensemble learning. The workshop will introduce the principles of ensemble modeling and explain how combining multiple base learners can enhance the accuracy and reliability of predictive models. Participants will explore major ensemble techniques, including Bagging, Random Forest, Boosting, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Voting Classifiers, and Stacking.The workshop will emphasize the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of these techniques, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and suitability for different supervised learning tasks. Participants will gain insights into model selection, hyperparameter tuning, feature importance analysis, and performance evaluation using appropriate metrics for classification and regression problems. A hands-on session using Python and machine learning libraries such as Scikit-learn will enable participants to implement ensemble algorithms, experiment with real-world datasets, and compare the performance of individual models with ensemble-based approaches.

title: 4th Edition of Winter School on Biomedical Optics (4th WiSBO)

description: Biomedical optics has become one of the most inevitable field in the recent research in clinical diagnosis and treatment. In this course, we will learn about the fundamentals of biomedical optics, starting from how the…
details_text: Biomedical optics has become one of the most inevitable field in the recent research in clinical diagnosis and treatment. In this course, we will learn about the fundamentals of biomedical optics, starting from how the photon interacts with a single atom, to a diatomic species, and then with polyatomic species such as haemoglobin. You will learn the basics of spectroscopy and different imaging modalities such as fluorescence, UV-Vis-NIR, diffuse optics, polarization, Speckle contrast, and multimodal imaging. You will also learn about fundamental and advances in the field of optical biosensors and various plasmonic resonances. We will also discuss the principles and details along with demonstration of various microscopic imaging such as brightfield, phase contrast, fluorescence and polarization-based microscopy.The Department of Electronics and Communication, IIITDM Kancheepuram is organizing the 4th Edition of Winter School on Biomedical Optics (WiSBO ’26-27) at IIITDM Kancheepuram-Chennai, India between 27th December to 30th December. The participants (about 40 to 50) will be PhD students, Faculty members, and Industry participants working in the field of biomedical optics throughout India.

Stand out from the crowd in job applications by showcasing your certificate from Shaastra, IIT Madras! Gear up to excel in competitions by building strong fundamentals! Learn from the masters of the trade who have proved their mettle. About the Workshop In this workshop, you will explore the fascinating real-world applications of quantum communication and quantum sensing. The first session explores why current encryption methods used in apps like WhatsApp are at risk. It introduces the fundamental principles of photons and quantum states through live demonstrations. You will participate in interactive games and Python simulations to learn how to share secret keys using the BB84 method, identify digital hackers, and understand the future of the quantum internet and India's National Quantum Mission. The second session focuses on quantum sensing, explaining how the extreme sensitivity of quantum particles powers highly accurate atomic clocks for GPS and uses tiny flaws in diamonds for medical brain scans and GPS-free navigation. Through hands-on simulated sensor data, you will see these concepts in action before concluding with an exciting team challenge to design your own futuristic quantum gadget. For further details related to the workshop, please refer to the Content Doc . Requirements Participants should bring their laptops. Install KiCad in advance. Bringing a mouse is recommended. details_text: Building on the legacy of MDI’s National Management Convention, Delphique proudly presents MDI's Knockout Parliamentary Debate . title: British Parliament
description: Overview British Parliament is a three-day Model Parliament that simulates the United Kingdom Parliament. Participants debate, draft and decide legislation as it is done at Westminster. Sixty delegates serve as Members…
details_text: Overview British Parliament is a three-day Model Parliament that simulates the United Kingdom Parliament. Participants debate, draft and decide legislation as it is done at Westminster. Sixty delegates serve as Members of Parliament in the House of Commons and, once the Bill passes, take on new roles as peers in the House of Lords. Ten further participants represent the International Press, who question and report on the proceedings. The Journey: Day 1, Day 2 and Day 3 Day 1 (Round 1): The House of Commons. Members take the oath, address the House on the agendas and vote for the motion to be taken forward. They then draft the Bill together, while the International Press faces a surprise press conference. Day 2 (Round 2): Commons to Lords. The Commons debates the Bill and its amendments and decides them by vote. Members are then ennobled, take on their Lords personas and begin the Lords’ reading of the Bill. Day 3 (Round 3): The House of Lords and the Close. The Lords examine the Bill clause by clause and vote on amendments. The Bill receives a symbolic Royal Assent and becomes an Act of Parliament, followed by a closing press conference and the Closing Ceremony. No participant is eliminated, so everyone takes part for the full event. Assessment rests on the quality of argument, the clarity of amendments and the ability to persuade. Every participant receives a certificate, and outstanding performers are recognised with awards.

details_text: Overview: This is a special market prediction challenge where all participants compete on the same 5 Nifty 50 stocks. After clicking through from Unstop to IndiaStox, you’ll first make your 5 predictions. Predict whether each stock will close Up or Down and set your confidence level from 1% to 100% in a single step for each trading day. For same-day participation, submit all 5 predictions before 1:00 PM IST. Entries after 1:00 PM IST will move to the next available window. Week 40 Format: November 23 - 27, 2026 Same 5 companies for everyone. 5 daily predictions. 25 total calls in 5 days. Rankings based on participation and accuracy. No long-form submission is required. No popularity bias. Rankings are based on your market judgment and performance. Rewards & Benefits: Winner - 1st Rank: 1:1 mentorship with VC founders Internship pathway with IndiaStox Ambassador program Top Performers - Top 3: Achievement certificate Internship pathway with IndiaStox Platform reputation boost Full Completion: Participation certificate Base points reward For users who vote on all trading days How It Works: The challenge runs from November 23 - 27, 2026 The same 5 Nifty 50 companies remain fixed throughout the challenge. Every day, participants answer Yes or No for each company. Participants also set their confidence level from 1% to 100%. Submit before 1:00 PM IST to predict that same day’s close. Predictions are scored after market close. The leaderboard updates as results come in. Simple Timing Rule: If you vote before 1:00 PM IST, your prediction is for that day’s close and is scored against the previous trading day’s close. If you vote after 1:00 PM IST, your prediction moves to the next trading day’s close and is scored against the current trading day’s close. In short: Before 1:00 PM = today’s prediction. After 1:00 PM = next trading day’s prediction. title: Refsolve
description: Mrs. Anjali Rao, Head of the Refinery, returns from a meeting with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) and the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG) with a clear mandate: all petrol…
details_text: Mrs. Anjali Rao, Head of the Refinery, returns from a meeting with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) and the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG) with a clear mandate: all petrol (motor spirit) leaving the plant must meet the *Bharat Stage VI sulfur limit of 10 ppm*, with the new unit scheduled to be operational by late 2027. Currently, the refinery's FCC (cracked) naphtha, which contributes most of the sulfur to the petrol pool, contains approximately *800–1,000 ppm sulfur. The budget ceiling for desulfurisation is *₹1.9–3.2 per litre**. The CTO, Mr. Vikram Sethi, identifies the key challenge: cracked naphtha contains a high concentration of *olefins, which contribute to its high octane number. Conventional hydrotreating catalysts can remove sulfur but may also saturate these olefins, resulting in **octane loss and increased hydrogen consumption*. The refinery therefore needs a *selective catalytic system* capable of removing sulfur while preserving the essential properties of the fuel. *Your challenge is to design an in-house catalyst and define the operating window required to achieve deep desulfurisation of petrol.*

title: Operation Blackout
description: About: In the Multiverse of Matter, thousands of parallel worlds exist, and most of them get through their darkest night. Wormwood is not one of them. It is a universe frozen at 1:23 a.m. on 26 April 1986, the night…
details_text: About: In the Multiverse of Matter, thousands of parallel worlds exist, and most of them get through their darkest night. Wormwood is not one of them. It is a universe frozen at 1:23 a.m. on 26 April 1986, the night Chernobyl’s Reactor 4 failed, and its clocks will not move until someone sets things right. The only thing that can calm its core is the Prima Materia, a mythical substance said to rewrite matter itself. But a rogue scientist, once ignored when she warned of this very night, has stolen it and sealed it away. Time is running out in Wormwood, and it is now up to you. Operation Blackout is a high-stakes, timed puzzle chase where every answer you crack unlocks the next challenge. Four connected levels stand between your team and the final solution, and none of them can be skipped. There is no textbook shortcut here. You will have to think like an alchemist, a circuit designer, a signal engineer and a gene hunter, often within the same five minutes. The challenges draw on many branches of engineering, so you will need a team that can reason under pressure and stay calm while the clock counts down. One shared countdown of 90 minutes runs for the entire game, and wrong turns and hints cost you precious time, so only the fastest and most precise teams will make it to the end. Open to 2nd, 3rd and 4th-year students, this is an event for the curious, the competitive and anyone who loves a good mystery. So gather your team, trust each other and be ready for the moment the lights go out. Wormwood is waiting, and its clock has already started.

details_text: BuildAthon is an intensive 8-hour, one-day AI Hackathon hosted as part of Techvora '26 by the Department of Artificial Intelligence . Scheduled for November 24, 2026 , at CAR LAB , BuildAthon challenges student teams to turn a real-world problem linked to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into a working AI prototype within a single day . Rather than training models from scratch, teams build practical solutions using pretrained models, free-tier APIs, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), prompting, and rule-based logic . Guidelines & Eligibility Who Can Participate: Open to all registered students with working programming or app-development knowledge . Prior model-training experience is not required . Team Size & Composition: Team Size: Strictly 3 members per team (no solo participation is allowed) Team Matching: Students without a full team of 3 may contact the event coordinators before the registration deadline to be matched with other participants . Participation Cap & Fee: Up to 20 teams will be shortlisted across the problem statements . Registration Fee: ₹750 per team (payable upon shortlisting confirmation) . Each participant may belong to only one team and must carry a valid student ID card on the event day . Number of Problem Statements: 3 Problem Statements (teams select one; full problem statements are provided separately in the Problem Statements document) . Competition Process & Round Durations (8-Hour Event Schedule) Registration & Concept Note Submission (Deadline: November 23, 2026): Teams submit member details, skill sets, chosen problem statement, an originality declaration, and a 1-page concept note (covering the problem, approach, tools/models, and SDG target) . Organizers shortlist up to 20 teams, notify them via email, and share sample datasets . Round 1 — PPT Pitch (Morning of November 24, 2026): Duration: 5 minutes per team ( 3-minute pitch + 2-minute Q&A ) . All 20 teams pitch across two rooms covering the problem, affected users, SDG link, architecture, tools/models, and responsible AI considerations . Top 8 teams advance to Round 2 (announced before noon) . Non-finalists attend a guest talk, feedback session, and vote for the People's Choice Award . Round 2 — Prototype Build & Live Demo (Afternoon of November 24, 2026): Build Duration: 3 hours (ending at the 3:00 PM submission freeze ) . Organizers release 20–30 test inputs at the start of the build phase . Demo Duration: 8 minutes per finalist team ( 5-minute live demo + 3-minute Q&A before the jury) . Results & Awards: Announced in the evening on the same day, concluding the 8-hour hackathon . Rules & Regulations Allowed Tools & APIs: Only open-source libraries, pretrained models, and free-tier APIs / free credits are allowed . Paid APIs are strictly prohibited . Mandatory Disclosures: Teams must disclose all pretrained models, APIs, libraries, datasets, reused code, and AI coding assistants used during development . Originality & Pre-Event Setup: Pre-event setup (creating accounts, generating API keys, and setting up an empty project skeleton) is permitted if disclosed, but the core solution must be built on the event day (GitHub commit history may be audited) . Presenting an existing complete project as new is prohibited . Feature Transparency: Teams must clearly distinguish working features from simulated or planned features during their demo . Data Privacy & Ethics: Only public, synthetic, or anonymized data may be used . Entering private or sensitive personal data into any AI tool is forbidden . Solutions must address responsible AI practices, including handling wrong, uncertain, or harmful outputs . Mentor & Conduct Guidelines: Mentors may guide and clarify doubts but cannot write code, design solutions, or operate demos . Sharing code or ideas with competing teams during the event is prohibited . Submission Freeze & Hardware: All Round 2 deliverables (working prototype, backup demo video, GitHub link with README, test input outputs

description: Design an AI-powered Smog Response System that Delhi NCR’s civic bodies could actually implement and present it to the people who can. About The Competition: SustainX 2026 is a Delhi NCR inter-institutional hackathon…
details_text: Design an AI-powered Smog Response System that Delhi NCR’s civic bodies could actually implement and present it to the people who can. About The Competition: SustainX 2026 is a Delhi NCR inter-institutional hackathon hosted by the Centre of Excellence for Sustainable Development at Great Lakes Institute of Management, Gurgaon. The Centre works at the intersection of data, governance, and sustainable business, and SustainX is its solution-focused hackathon built for social impact: a platform that challenges students to take on real civic problems and design solutions that can actually be put to work. Track 2 takes on one of Delhi NCR’s most visible and recurring crises: winter air pollution. The Problem We’re Solving: Every winter, Delhi NCR’s air turns hazardous. This year, the Commission for Air Quality Management invoked GRAP Stage III across the region on 6 November. On the morning after Diwali, Delhi’s AQI stood at 368, with 15 monitoring stations in the ‘severe’ category. In the week before Diwali, Delhi’s average PM2.5 was 236 µg/m³, the highest in three years and nearly four times the national 24-hour standard. Stubble burning gets the headlines, but it isn’t the main cause. In the first week of November, farm fires accounted for about 14% of Delhi’s PM2.5. Over half came from other NCR districts, and a third from local sources, led by vehicles. SustainX Track 2 asks one focused question: Can you design an AI-powered system that tells civic bodies where air pollution will spike next, what is driving it, and what to do about it before it happens? Why Participate: The judging panel will include officials from civic and pollution-control bodies. Solutions that demonstrate genuine implementability — technically credible, operationally feasible, and grounded in how NCR’s civic bodies actually function — will be shared by Great Lakes Gurgaon with civic stakeholders as a policy brief. This is one of the few student competitions where your solution has a realistic path from a slide deck to a government briefing room. Who Should Participate: This problem sits at the intersection of data science, environmental science and engineering, urban planning, public health, public policy, and business strategy. We actively encourage interdisciplinary teams. You do not need to be from a business management background; you need to understand the problem and design something that works. Background & Context: The NCR Smog Response System — From Blanket GRAP Bans To Targeted, Ward-Level Action: Delhi NCR’s main response to bad air is the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP): region-wide restrictions switched on when the forecast AQI crosses a threshold. But pollution varies street by street and hour by hour, while the response is city-wide and reactive. The same restrictions apply to every ward. Water sprinklers and mechanised sweepers run fixed routes, and inspection teams find violations after the fact. As the Centre for Science and Environment has noted, continued reliance on emergency GRAP restrictions shows that routine pollution controls are failing. Monitoring is thin and fragile too. Gurugram relies on four monitoring stations, and 29 of Haryana’s 31 stations went offline for about five months in 2024–25 when maintenance contracts lapsed. Civic bodies have no system that tells them which wards will spike in the next 24–72 hours, what is driving it locally, and where their limited crews and inspectors would cut the most exposure. Problem Statement: Design an AI-powered system that forecasts ward-level air pollution 24–72 hours ahead, identifies the likely local sources, and turns that into a daily action plan for civic bodies — one that is operationally viable within their existing technical and administrative capacity. details_text: 1. Event Overview "Deal Den" is a live startup pitch competition that tests your business acumen, financial planning, marketing, and negotiation skills. Teams will pitch their startup ideas to a panel of "Sharks" (entrepreneurs and industry leaders) and a live student audience. 2. Team Composition & Eligibility Team Size: Every team must have 2–4 members. Reporting & ID: Arrive at least 30 minutes early and carry your valid college ID card at all times during the event. Behaviour & Discipline: Remain respectful, follow all coordinator instructions, and do not cheat or seek outside help. Violation of these rules will result in immediate disqualification. 3. Event Stages & Game Structure Stage 1: Idea Screening (Preliminary Round) Teams must submit a PPT according to the following guidelines: First-Come, First-Served: Submissions will be reviewed in the order they are received. Slide Limit: Your pitch deck must contain 4–5 slides. Deadline: Submit your PPT before the deadline. Late submissions will not be accepted. Original Work: Your idea and slides must be 100% original and free from plagiarism. Review & Feedback: Organisers will review every submission. If any changes or corrections are required, your team will be contacted directly. Key Topics to Cover: The PPT must explain the problem identified, proposed solution, target audience, unique concept, and market potential. File Name: [Unique Start Up Name_Your Name/Your Team Name] Stage 2: The Final Pitch (Live Stage Round) Date: 11-12-2026 Selected teams will pitch live on stage to the Sharks and the student audience. Slide Limit: Your pitch deck must contain 10 slides. Executive Summary: Each team must submit its Executive Summary (Word/PDF) to the event coordinators after arriving at IBS Pune. Key Topics to Cover: Clearly present your business model, problem identified, innovative solution, target audience, go-to-market strategy, operational feasibility, 5-year financial projections, and growth prospects. Funding Ask: Clearly state the investment amount required and the equity being offered (for example, ₹20 Lakhs for 10% equity ). 4. Evaluation Judging Criteria Points Problem Identification & Innovative Solution 25 Financial Model & 5-Year Projection 25 Go-To-Market Strategy 20 Pitch Delivery & Confidence 15 Q&A & Negotiation Handling 15 Total 100 Mock Currency & Investment Mechanics Shark Funds: Each Shark will receive mock money to evaluate pitches, negotiate equity deals, and fund the teams they find promising. Audience Funds: Each audience member/participating team will receive mock money to invest in the startups they find most convincing. Overall Scoring Weight: Final team scores and rankings will be determined using a composite weighting model: Judging Criteria: 70% Shark/Judges' Mock Investments: 25% Audience Fund Mock Investments: 5% 5. General Rules & Disclaimers Time Limits: Strictly adhere to the set time limits: 10 minutes for pitching, followed by Q&A and 5 minutes for deal talks. Slide Rules: Decks containing more than 10 slides may lose points at the organisers' discretion. Campus Property: Do not damage, remove, or tamper with college property, stage setups, or event items. Organiser Rights: Organisers reserve the right to update the rules or make necessary changes during the event. Final Decisions: All decisions made by the Sharks/judges and coordinators will be final. title: Drone Soccer
description: Registration: All teams must register on the official Techfest website (https://techfest.org/competitions/drone-soccer) and obtain a valid Team ID. Registration on Unstop alone does not complete the competition…
details_text: Registration: All teams must register on the official Techfest website (https://techfest.org/competitions/drone-soccer) and obtain a valid Team ID. Registration on Unstop alone does not complete the competition registration. All participants must carry valid institutional ID cards for verification. Get ready for an adrenaline-filled aerial showdown at Drone Soccer , presented at Techfest 2026-27! Combining drone piloting, precision, strategy and teamwork, this competition brings the excitement of football into the air. Two teams of three players compete inside a fully netted arena, manoeuvring their drones to score goals while defending their own. Each team fields one designated Attacker and two Defenders . The objective is to fly the Attacker drone completely through the opponent's hanging Goal Ring, from front to back, while the Defenders block opposing attacks and protect their own goal. All teams compete using drones of the same Class 200 specifications, ensuring that success depends on piloting skills, coordination and strategy rather than expensive or oversized hardware. Competition Structure Stage 1 – Online Qualifying Round Teams must submit a single entry containing: Team details, including pilots, substitutes, coach, institution and nominated Attacker. Technical specifications of each drone. Clear top and side photographs showing the drone and its protective cage. A continuous video of up to 3 minutes demonstrating weight verification, lighting, controlled flight, successful passage through a ring and recovery from light contact. Entries will be evaluated on technical compliance, safety, piloting skills, reliability and build quality. Stage 2 – On-Campus Finals Shortlisted teams will compete at Techfest, IIT Bombay, in a fully netted arena measuring 24 × 12 × 12 ft. Each match consists of two 3-minute rounds with a 3-minute repair break. Tied knockout matches proceed to a 3-minute overtime round, followed by a shootout with 10 seconds per attempt if required. Teams must coordinate their Attacker and Defenders effectively, with all drones required to return behind the Center Line after every goal before another goal can be scored. Drone Specifications Drone class: Class 200. Outer diameter: 20 cm ± 1 cm. Maximum ready-to-fly weight: 200 g. All drones must comply with the prescribed cage, motor, battery and lighting requirements. All participating drones must satisfy the technical and safety checks conducted by the organisers. Eligibility and Team Composition Open to students of recognised schools, colleges and universities. A team may have 3 flying players, up to 2 substitutes and 1 coach. Maximum team size: 6 members. At least 2 players, including the designated Attacker, must be present to play. Venue The on-campus finals will take place at Techfest, IIT Bombay , from 16–18 December 2026. Bring your best pilots, build your strategy and take control of the skies. May the best team score!

title: BIOFORGE 2026 – Interdisciplinary Healthcare Innovation Hackathon
organiser: Dayananda Sagar College of Engineering (DSCE), Bengaluru
description: About the Hackathon BioForge 2026 is a seven-day, on-campus interdisciplinary healthcare innovation hackathon bringing together undergraduate students from Biotechnology, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence,…
details_text: About the Hackathon BioForge 2026 is a seven-day, on-campus interdisciplinary healthcare innovation hackathon bringing together undergraduate students from Biotechnology, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Biomedical Engineering and allied health-science disciplines. The hackathon aims to transform real-world healthcare challenges into practical, technology-enabled solutions through interdisciplinary collaboration, innovation and industry mentorship. Participants will work on challenges involving scattered health records, missed patient follow-ups, preventive healthcare gaps and post-hospitalisation recovery. Teams will develop working prototypes, computational models or data-driven solutions addressing tangible challenges in healthcare delivery, diagnostics and public health. AssistHealth will contribute industry challenges, insights and mentorship throughout the hackathon. Challenge Tracks and Problem Statements Participants can choose one of the following five tracks: 1. AI-Assisted Personal Health Record Organisation Develop an AI-enabled tool that organises medical documents, prescriptions, laboratory reports and consultation summaries into a unified, structured digital health record. 2. Patient Follow-Up and Care Continuity Develop a digital system that identifies missed appointments, pending investigations and overdue follow-ups to help patients stay on track with their treatment. 3. Preventive Healthcare Assessment & Awareness Build a data-driven tool that recommends appropriate preventive health checks based on an individual's age, lifestyle and established clinical guidelines. 4. Post-Hospitalisation Recovery & Monitoring Develop a solution supporting patients after hospital discharge or surgery through follow-up schedules, medication reminders, rehabilitation coordination and recovery tracking. 5. Open-Health Innovation Track Propose an original problem statement addressing a validated gap in clinical workflows, diagnostics, bioinformatics or public health. Eligibility and Team Structure Open to all undergraduate engineering students across academic years. Inter-college teams and participants from external institutions are welcome. Each team must consist of 3–4 members. At least 2 members must belong to Biotechnology or allied streams, including Biomedical Engineering or Medical Electronics. The remaining 1–2 members may belong to Computer Science, AI/ML or allied engineering streams. Each student may register in only one team. Team rosters will be locked once registration closes. Registration Fees DSCE Internal Teams: ₹400 per team. Valid DSCE student ID required for all members. External College Teams: ₹500 per team. Valid college ID required for campus entry and verification. Registration Deadline: 23 November 2026. Exact cutoff time to be confirmed. Event Schedule 23 November 2026 – Registration Closes Final deadline for team registration. Team rosters are locked. 24 November 2026 – Kick-Off & Orientation Inauguration, event briefing, dataset orientation and problem statement finalisation. 24–29 November 2026 – Build Phase Teams develop their solutions with mentor check-ins and periodic progress reviews. 30 November 2026 – Final Presentations & Finale Live team demonstrations and pitch presentations to the judging panel, followed by results and prize distribution. Detailed session timings will be shared with registered teams. Final Submission Requirements Each participating team must submit: Presentation deck in PPT or PDF format. Working software/hardware prototype or live demonstration. Public or accessible GitHub repository link, where applicable. Comprehensive README file detailing project architecture, setup instructions and usage. Prizes and Recognition 1st Place – Winner ₹6,000 worth of gift vouchers + Certificates of Achievement. 1st Runner-Up ₹5,000 worth of gift vouchers + Certificates of Achievement. 2nd Runner-Up ₹4,000 worth of gift vouchers + Certificates of Achievement. Queries: Bhavi Mehta - 9426970041 Aashna Singh - 9004206126 Nivedita Ranawat - 8107872339 Round 1: Genre Twist Make up to 30 second jingle for your product, in a genre nobody would expect. Think of a detergent qawwali, a rap for cough syrup, or a lullaby for a bank. Say the product name in it and give it a tagline. Send it as an MP3 or WAV file. How it will be marked: Criteria Points How surprising the pairing is, and whether the genre says something about the product 30 Tagline and lyrics 30 How much it actually sounds like that genre 20 Whether the name and tagline stick after one listen 20 Total 100 Round 2: Time Machine Now make a 60-90 second video ad for the same product, set in a different time. If your product is modern (a smartphone, UPI, a food delivery app), take it back in time. It could be a 1950s radio spot, a song from a 60s black-and-white film, a 70s Bollywood scene or an 80s Doordarshan ad. If your product is old (a Chetak, Nirma, a landline, a Walkman), bring it forward and sell it to Gen Z as a reel, an unboxing video or a meme. Not sure if your product is old or modern? Pick the direction where it looks most out of place. Send it as an MP4. Any aspect ratio is fine. If you work your Round 1 jingle into the ad, redone in the style of that era, you can get up to 10 bonus points. How it will be marked: Criteria Points How convincingly it feels like that era (look, sound, language, voiceover) 30 How well the product being out of its time drives the story 25 Whether it still works as an ad for the product 25 Story, editing and sound 20 Total 100 Bonus: Round 1 jingle reworked in the era's style +10 Example Say your team picks a smartphone. In Round 1 you make a qawwali with the tagline "Haath se chhoote na." In Round 2 you shoot it like a 60s black-and-white film song, with the hero singing to his phone to the same qawwali tune. Reusing the tune gets you the bonus too. Final score Your final score is 30% of your Round 1 marks plus 70% of your Round 2 marks. No one is eliminated after Round 1, so every team submits both rounds. Using AI You can use AI tools, but the writing has to be yours. Your lyrics, tagline and script must be written by your team. AI is fine for things like music production, vocals, voiceovers, visuals, editing and subtitles. Don't use AI to copy an existing song, or to fake a real person's voice or face. When you submit, tell us which AI tools you used and what you used them for. If you use AI without telling us, or use it to write your lyrics, tagline or script, your entry may be disqualified. Rules Everything must be original. No existing songs, tunes or copyrighted beats. Real brands are fine, but the jingle and tagline must be new. Don't make fun of any religion, community, region or gender. Any language is fine. If it isn't Hindi or English, add English subtitles. title: The First Job Reality Check 2026 | Are You Ready to Get Hired?
description: The First Job Reality Check 2026 Are You Ready to Get Hired? Thousands of students graduate every year. But how many are truly ready for their first job? You've attended classes, completed assignments, earned your…
details_text: The First Job Reality Check 2026 Are You Ready to Get Hired? Thousands of students graduate every year. But how many are truly ready for their first job? You've attended classes, completed assignments, earned your degree, and perhaps even built a resume. But here's the question that matters: If you had a job interview tomorrow, would you know how to stand out? Welcome to The First Job Reality Check 2026 , a national-level career-readiness challenge presented by Elevate Careers India . This isn't another academic quiz. It's an opportunity to test how you think, make decisions, and approach real-world situations that fresh graduates encounter while preparing for their first job. What's the Challenge? A 10-question, scenario-based challenge designed to test your practical career readiness across four important areas: Career Direction: How clearly do you understand your career choices? Profile Strength: Can you demonstrate your skills and position yourself effectively? Interview Readiness: How would you handle realistic interview situations? Job Search Strategy: Do you know how to approach opportunities and improve your chances? Every question encourages you to think beyond textbooks and apply practical judgment. Why Should You Participate? Because having a degree and being job-ready aren't always the same thing. This challenge will help you: Test your career readiness through realistic situations. Identify areas where your approach might need improvement. Challenge common misconceptions about getting hired. Reflect on how prepared you are for your first professional opportunity. Take an informed next step toward your career goals. Challenge Details Format: Online, scenario-based multiple-choice quiz Questions: 10 Estimated Duration: 10 minutes Participation: Individual Registration Fee: FREE Mode: Online via Unstop Who Can Participate? Final-year undergraduate and postgraduate students Recent graduates Freshers preparing for their first job Students from any academic discipline No previous work experience is required. Are You Really Job-Ready? You may have the qualifications. You may have the ambition. But do you have the readiness to turn an opportunity into your first job? 10 Questions. Real-World Scenarios. One Reality Check. Take the challenge and discover how prepared you really are. Register Now — It's Completely Free! Organized by Elevate Careers India — Helping students move from education to career readiness. Important: This is an educational career-readiness challenge. Participation does not guarantee employment, interviews, internships, or placement opportunities.

title: PRoelio 12.0
organiser: Symbiosis Institute of Business Management (SIBM), Pune
description: PRoelio 12.0 The Information Systems and Media Relations Team (iSMaRT), the official PR Team of SIBM Pune, presents PRoelio 12.0, the nation’s leading PR-based case study competition for college students, where teams of…
details_text: PRoelio 12.0 The Information Systems and Media Relations Team (iSMaRT), the official PR Team of SIBM Pune, presents PRoelio 12.0, the nation’s leading PR-based case study competition for college students, where teams of 1 to 3 participants are challenged to tackle real-world public relations crises through strategic and creative solutions. With sustainability becoming an increasingly important part of the corporate narrative, PRoelio 12.0 explores the evolving challenges of greenwashing and the fine line between responsible communication and misleading environmental claims. Building on a legacy of excellence, this edition provides a platform to test participants’ ability to navigate reputational challenges, uphold corporate credibility and craft communication strategies in an era where transparency and accountability matter more than ever. About PRoelio 12.0 is a dynamic experiential competition that places participants at the centre of a high-stakes public relations crisis rooted in greenwashing. Acting as senior decision-makers, teams must navigate situations involving misleading sustainability claims, environmental controversies and questions surrounding corporate accountability. They are required to develop and implement effective communication strategies to manage public perception, restore stakeholder trust and minimise reputational damage under intense media scrutiny. The most impressive teams advance to the national finale at the Symbiosis Institute of Business Management, Pune, where they present their crisis response plans to a distinguished panel of judges. The event tests participants’ ability to think on their feet, address difficult questions and defend their communication strategies in the face of challenging media scrutiny. Through this immersive experience, PRoelio 12.0 offers aspiring PR professionals an opportunity to demonstrate strategic thinking, ethical judgement, creativity and crisis management skills while navigating one of the most pressing challenges in contemporary corporate communication. Why should you participate? In an era where sustainability is no longer just a corporate choice but an expectation, organisations are increasingly being held accountable for their environmental claims. With consumers, investors and stakeholders demanding greater transparency, even a seemingly harmless sustainability claim can turn into a significant reputational crisis when it fails to reflect reality. PRoelio 12.0 offers an unparalleled platform to explore the complexities of greenwashing, sharpen your strategic communication skills and understand the role of public relations in building and protecting corporate credibility. It challenges participants to look beyond carefully crafted narratives, question the authenticity of environmental claims and develop communication strategies that balance transparency, accountability and stakeholder expectations. When sustainability claims come under scrutiny, can you separate perception from reality, navigate the backlash and rebuild trust? Step into the shoes of communication leaders with PRoelio 12.0 and prove that you can turn a greenwashing controversy into an opportunity for responsible communication. Rules All team members must belong to the same college. Teams can include members from different specialisations. Teams comprising students from different academic years are allowed. Each team must consist of 1 to 3 members. All members must register and form their teams before the deadline. All teams must attempt the quiz before the deadline. Team modifications will not be allowed after the registration deadline. A participant can be part of only one team. Each team must register with a unique team name. From Stage 2 onwards, submissions will be evaluated based on the originality of ideas, clarity of reasoning and strength of supporting data. Competition Stages Stage 1: Teams will have 20 minutes to complete the quiz, which can be attempted at any time within a 24-hour

All times are India Standard Time (IST). Each day has one task: a short lesson, 3 questions (with an explanation after each answer) and one optional real-life action. The optional action is a tick-box and earns no points. Day 30 is the finale quiz. It is open all day and has no late window. 4. Points Each correct answer earns 10 points. A wrong answer earns 0. You can retry a question, but each retry earns fewer points than the try before. A task done within 36 hours of its start earns full points. After that it earns 50% until that week’s Sunday cut-off, and nothing after. The finale quiz is worth 60 points. There is no daily or weekly cap on points. 5. Streaks and resets A day counts towards your streak if you finish it by 12:00 noon IST the next day. Streak bonuses: +10 at 7 days, +20 at 14 days, +30 at 21 days and +40 at 30 days. Everyone starts with 2 resets. One reset repairs one missed day and restores your streak. A task done late after a reset earns 50% of its points. One extra reset goes to each weekly top-3 finisher, and to everyone who completes every task in a leaderboard week. Unused resets expire at the end of 30 Dec. 6. Referrals Everyone gets a personal invite link. You earn 10 points for each friend who joins with your link, finishes Day 3 and passes a quick check. This counts for up to 20 friends. You can’t refer yourself, and each person can be referred only once. 7. Leaderboards There are 5 weekly leaderboards: Week 1 (1–6 Dec), Week 2 (7–13 Dec), Week 3 (14–20 Dec), Week 4 (21–27 Dec) and the Final stretch (28–30 Dec). Each weekly board closes on Sunday night, and winners are announced on Monday. A final leaderboard adds up all 30 days and closes at the end of 30 Dec. Ties are broken by higher score first, then by more tasks done on time, then by who reached that score first. If people are still tied, the prize is split equally. 8. Prizes WinterArc has total rewards worth ₹25,000, comprising ₹10,000 in cash prizes and ₹15,000 worth of brand-sponsored rewards. Cash prizes and in-kind rewards will be distributed among eligible winners based on the published prize structure. The full prize distribution, including the nature of brand-sponsored rewards, will be published before 1 December. Cash prizes will be paid through UPI to verified winners. Any tax due on winnings is the winner's responsibility. If a winner doesn't respond within 48 hours, the prize may pass to the next eligible person. 9. Fair play Every winner is verified before a prize is paid. FinEd may disqualify an account or withhold a prize for: more than one account per person, fake or self-referrals, automated or scripted entries, or any other attempt to game the challenge. FinEd’s decision is final. 10. Certificate Complete at least 21 of the 30 days to get a FinEd certificate of completion after the challenge ends. Every certificate can be verified. It is not an accredited qualification, and it doesn’t affect your score, rank or prizes. The certificate is optional and paid; the price will be confirmed when it goes on sale. 11. Your data We collect your name, email, college (optional) and how you heard about WinterArc, only to run the challenge and contact you about it. UPI details are collected only from winners, with their consent, only to pay prizes. 12. Changes Point values, streak bonuses and referral rules may still change. Get ready to take control of the field at RoboSoccer , a 2 vs 2 wireless robot football championship presented at Techfest 2026-27, under Bot League by BotMakers Pvt. Ltd. Teams will design, build and operate two robots — an Attacker and a Defender (goalkeeper) — to compete in an exciting football showdown. title: Anveshak: Open-World Object Detection for Remote Sensing
description: About Anveshak: Open-World Object Detection for Remote Sensing is a national computer vision competition by Techfest, IIT Bombay. Earth-observation systems support disaster response, maritime and defence surveillance,…
details_text: About Anveshak: Open-World Object Detection for Remote Sensing is a national computer vision competition by Techfest, IIT Bombay. Earth-observation systems support disaster response, maritime and defence surveillance, urban planning, agriculture, and climate monitoring, yet three problems limit them in practice: imagery always contains unknown objects the taxonomy does not cover, new classes arrive gradually with only a few examples, and learning new categories can quietly degrade performance on old ones. Teams build one remote sensing detector that handles all three while keeping the same model throughout, trained entirely from random initialisation with no pretrained weights of any kind. Take on the challenge at Techfest, IIT Bombay, Asia's largest science and technology festival. Structure The competition has an online Round 1, an on-site Round 2, and an on-site Finale at Techfest, IIT Bombay. Eligibility: Open to all students with a valid ID from their educational institution. Cross-institutional teams are encouraged. Team size: Maximum 4 members per team. The Challenge: Design and train one remote sensing detector that learns in two rounds and keeps the same model throughout. It must detect 40 known classes in Round 1, flag unknown objects as unknown rather than forcing them into known classes, learn 10 new classes from a small number of images each without forgetting the base classes, and then learn 10 fresh classes in Round 2 while still flagging unknowns. Key constraints: Every model is trained from random initialisation, with no ImageNet, COCO, self-supervised (e.g. DINOv2), remote sensing, or other pretrained weights. Open-source detection frameworks are allowed with pretrained-weight loading switched off; open-vocabulary models are not permitted as the detector. The model must remain one lineage: train on Set A, continue on Set B, then continue into Round 2, with the same architecture and no retraining from scratch or replacement. Round 1 - Online Teams receive Dataset A, Dataset B, unlabelled Round 1 test images, the class list, and a validator script. They train on Dataset A first, then continue on Dataset B with the same model; training images may contain unlabelled objects of unknown classes. Teams submit one Google Drive folder containing a predictions CSV for the Round 1 test images, the Round 1 checkpoint (weights after Set A then Set B), training and inference code with a README, and a 5-7 slide methodology PPT (problem understanding, methodology, first implementation, Round 2 plan, and team roles). Screening is on the OE-Score, computed on the full Round 1 test set, plus checkpoint reproduction: organisers re-run the checkpoint on the Round 1 test images and its predictions must match the submitted CSV within tolerance. The PPT is also checked for completeness. Round 2 - On-site, 16th December 2026 Held at Techfest, IIT Bombay. The Round 2 dataset and unlabelled test images are released at the start of the Round 2 window. Teams learn 10 fresh classes from a small number of images, starting from their verified Round 1 checkpoint (no other starting weights are permitted), without forgetting earlier classes and while still flagging unknowns. Round 2 training images may contain unlabelled objects of base, few-shot, and unknown classes. Teams train on the Round 2 dataset plus data released in earlier rounds only. The window closes at a fixed time to be announced on the day; teams may submit at any point within the window. The deliverable is a predictions CSV for the Round 2 test images. Outcome: shortlisting for the Finale. Finale - On-site, 17th December 2026 Organisers re-run inference for each shortlisted team on the Round 2 test images. Shortlisted teams submit code, weights, and a two-page technical note, present their approach to the panel, and answer questions. Outcome: final ranking. Scoring Primary score is the OE-Score = 100 x 2 x mAP_K x U-F1 / (mAP_K + U-F1), built from known-class detection (mAP_K)

title: Resonate: An Audio Filmmaking Competition
description: Overview Resonate is an audio filmmaking competition conducted under Eons, a student-led initiative at IIT Madras, as part of Shaastra 2027 . Eons is dedicated to preserving India's culture and heritage by integrating…
details_text: Overview Resonate is an audio filmmaking competition conducted under Eons, a student-led initiative at IIT Madras, as part of Shaastra 2027 . Eons is dedicated to preserving India's culture and heritage by integrating them with modern technology. Resonate is our tribute to the art of sound design and the breathtaking soundscape of India. This competition challenges participants to tell compelling stories using only sound, while designing high-quality spatial audio that artistically captures the soundscape of any aspect of Indian culture and life. What is this competition about? Participants will convey a story using only sound. We are looking for a sound that represents India in its rawest state. From the chirping sparrows, roaring waves, hawking vendors, Ilayaraja on the radio on a Chennai morning, to the soft winds, crunching snow, and the rustling of pine trees on a Kashmiri night, from seemingly ordinary sounds like tinkles of bangles to hypnotic Hindustani music. Using clips like these, sourced from the internet or recorded by themselves, the participants should be able to transport the listener into the setting of their story, without the assistance of visuals. Competition Structure Round 1: Preliminary online round (Deadline: 19/12/2026) Finals: Offline presentation at IIT Madras (03/01/2027) Team Composition No limit on team size (Maximum of 3 people present during finals) One person is allowed to join only one team Individual participation is allowed Why Participate? All participants get a one-month license to sound mixing software by Sonarworks Exciting prizes and merch for winners Opportunity to create high-quality spatial audio representing India’s culture Meet expert judges in the Indian film and sound industries Finalists present their submissions at IIT Madras Visit to the newly inaugurated Maestro Ilaiyaraaja Centre Guidelines: Inter-college teams and professionals are allowed. Inter-specialization team members allowed or not. There are two rounds: an online submission followed by finals at IIT Madras. Submissions must be a zip file containing: Final Project (Accepted formats explained in the resource document) DAW Project file along with all clips used (Project files are used only to verify originality and resolve technical issues. They are not part of the judging and will not be shared publicly.) A document containing: An explanation of your creative process and working (1 page at most) List of sources of all audio clips. List of team members and credits. Optional: A behind the scenes video explaining the creative process behind your project. Rules: The submission must at most 5 minutes long, and must be submitted before 11:59 PM 19 th December, 2026. Submissions will be accepted in two categories (explained in the resource document): Stereo and 5.1. All participants are strongly discouraged from using generative AI for any aspect of the creation of this project, from writing, to mixing, and creation of audio clips, and teams will be penalised for the same. Join the WhatsApp group linked in the participant guidebook to clear any queries and stay up to date with any updates in the competition.

title: Finnova

details_text: About: FINNOVA is a flagship competition under Adhikosh that explores the evolving role of Artificial Intelligence in Banking and Financial Services. As AI continues to transform the banking landscape, the challenge is to determine what should be automated and where human intelligence remains irreplaceable. The competition brings together students to test their knowledge, analytical abilities and innovative thinking through real-world banking challenges. Objective: To explore the intersection of Banking, Finance and AI while encouraging participants to develop practical, technology-driven solutions that balance automation with human judgment. Team Structure: 2–3 members per team. All team members must belong to the same college. Round 1 – Screening Quiz (Elimination Round) An online screening quiz testing participants across Banking & Finance fundamentals, AI applications in banking, current affairs and applied reasoning. Format: 40 MCQs | 15 Minutes | Online on Unstop Round 2 – Department Under Pressure (On-Campus) Shortlisted teams will be assigned a banking department facing a real-world operational challenge. They must analyse the problem and develop an AI-integration strategy, identifying what can be automated and where human intervention remains essential. Departments may include Loans & Credit, KYC & Compliance, Fraud & Risk Management, Relationship Banking, Wealth Management, Operations and Treasury & ALM. Deliverable: A practical AI-integration solution covering problem identification, AI–human balance, implementation feasibility and expected business impact. Preparation: 1.5–2 Hours | Live PPT Presentation: 10–15 Minutes Judging Criteria: Problem Understanding – 20% AI–Human Balance – 20% Feasibility – 20% Business Impact – 20% Presentation & Clarity – 20% The Challenge: AI can process information, automate decisions and optimise operations. But can it replace human judgment where it matters most? Step up, challenge conventional thinking and demonstrate how you would shape the future of banking.

details_text: Protatva’26 is the 4th National-Level Inter-College Project Exhibition and Competition. It gives students from colleges across the country a platform to showcase innovative projects, from technology prototypes and intelligent systems to sustainable innovations, science models, and socially impactful solutions. Process Register and form your team Phase 1 (26 Nov, online): PPT presentation Shortlisting by the evaluation panel Phase 2 (3 Dec, offline): poster display and prototype demonstration Phase 1 Format: Presentation (Online) Each team prepares a PowerPoint presentation covering: Project title and team details Problem statement Objectives Existing system and limitations Proposed solution Methodology / system architecture Innovation and novelty Expected outcomes and applications Technologies / tools used Conclusion Diagrams, architecture, flowcharts, screenshots, and prototype images may be included. details_text: Overview Beyond Margins is an editorial venture under the Economics Department of Sophia College for Women (Autonomous), Mumbai. title: CarbonQuest : The Decarbonization Challenge
organiser: National Institute of Bank Management (NIBM), Pune

details_text: CarbonQuest is a flagship sustainability-focused competition under Adhikosh, where teams act as sustainability consultants for carbon-intensive industries. The challenge encourages participants to identify emission hotspots and propose innovative, data-driven decarbonization strategies — supported by a comprehensive financial cost-benefit model. Objective: To promote climate innovation by engaging students in real-world carbon reduction challenges while enhancing analytical, technical, and financial modeling skills. Team Structure 1–4 members per team Cross-disciplinary teams encouraged (Finance, Operations, Sustainability, Engineering, etc.) What Participants Need to Do: Each team must: Round 1:- Choose a Carbon-Intensive Sector or 5 Companies from such sectors Examples: Cement, Steel, Aviation, Oil & Gas, Transportation, Textiles, FMCG, Energy, or Agriculture. Identify Emission Sources Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions. Propose a Decarbonization Strategy, including: Problem Identification: Quantify current emission footprint using available data. Innovative Idea or Intervention: Suggest new technology, process redesign, or renewable energy solution. Implementation Strategy: Include stages, partners, timelines, and key enablers (policy, finance, etc.). description: DATAVERSE: Shaastra, IIT Madras Where data meets decisions. Every boardroom decision today starts with a dataset. Dataverse is the data analytics case competition at Shaastra, IIT Madras . It asks you to do what top…
details_text: DATAVERSE: Shaastra, IIT Madras Where data meets decisions. Every boardroom decision today starts with a dataset. Dataverse is the data analytics case competition at Shaastra, IIT Madras . It asks you to do what top analysts and consultants do every day: take messy, real-world business data, find the story in it, and turn that story into a recommendation leaders would act on. This is not just a coding contest or a slide-making contest. It tests the full analytics stack: statistical thinking, data wrangling, business judgment and persuasive communication . Whether you’re an engineer who loves Python or an MBA who thinks in frameworks, Dataverse is built so both can win, and the best teams usually have both. Why participate? Prize pool of ₹40,000 for the winning teams Solve a business problem built on a realistic, industry-style dataset Pitch live to a jury of industry professionals / IIT Madras faculty at IIT Madras Get exposure at one of India’s largest student-run technical festivals Certificates for winners, finalists and participants Eligibility Open to students currently enrolled in undergraduate programmes (B.Tech/B.E./B.Sc./BBA/B.Com etc.) or MBA/PGDM programmes at any recognised institute in India Teams of 2–4 members Inter-college teams are allowed. Members can be from different institutes. Inter-specialization teams are allowed. Mixing engineering, management, economics and science backgrounds is encouraged, and undergraduate and MBA students can be on the same team. One participant can be part of only one team Every member must be able to show a valid college ID if asked Competition Structure Round 1: Analytics Aptitude Quiz (Online, Elimination) Topics: statistics and probability, data interpretation, Excel/SQL logic, basic ML concepts and business analytics reasoning Mode: online, on Unstop. The team leader makes one attempt on behalf of the team. Ties are broken by the time taken to finish. The top 40 teams move on to Round 2 Round 2: Case Submission (Online) Shortlisted teams get 1 business problem statement with an accompanying dataset Duration: 5 days from when the case is released Deliverables: a solution deck of up to 10 slides (PDF), plus the supporting analysis file (Excel / Python notebook / R script) Judged on problem structuring, depth and accuracy of analysis, quality of insights, feasibility of recommendations and clarity of presentation The top 8 teams qualify for the Grand Finale Round 3: Grand Finale (Offline, at IIT Madras during Shaastra) Finalists present their solution to the jury 10 minutes presentation + 5 minutes Q&A At least 2 members of each finalist team must present in person Certificates Winners: hard-copy certificates, presented at the Grand Finale Finalists: soft-copy (e-certificates) Participants: soft-copy (e-certificates) for all teams that [attempt Round 1] Rules Each team must register on Unstop before registrations close. Registration is free . Team members cannot be changed after registrations close. Each team gets only one quiz attempt. Multiple logins or attempts lead to disqualification. Any tool or language may be used for analysis (Excel, Python, R, SQL, Tableau, Power BI etc.), but all work must be the team’s own. Use of generative AI tools must be disclosed in the final slide . Undisclosed AI-generated content may be penalised. Plagiarism, sharing datasets or solutions between teams, or copying from public sources without credit leads to immediate disqualification. Submissions must follow the given format and slide limit. Late submissions will not be accepted. The Round 2 dataset is for competition use only and must not be shared or published. Travel and accommodation for finalists: to be confirmed A team with any member who does not meet the eligibility criteria will be disqualified. The judges’ decision is final and binding. The organizing team may change the schedule or rules. Any change will be communicated to all registered participants through Unstop.

details_text: About WealthNest WealthNest is your family’s personalized wealth manager. It’s a SEBI-registered investment advisory platform that brings a family’s Investments, Insurance, Income Tax and Inheritance onto one screen. This challenge gives students a real, live product to solve for, not a textbook case. Tracks Management & Growth Strategy Open to MBA, BBA and students from any stream The problem: Drive 1,00,000 high-intent downloads of the WealthNest app with a minimal marketing budget. WealthNest is built for India’s emerging affluent: families with ₹50L–₹10Cr in investable assets. Traditional wealth managers overlook them, and single-person robo-advisors don’t cover the whole family. Your submission should cover: Competitor teardown: how existing Indian wealthtech platforms acquire users, and where they fall short for families Target user: who the high-intent user is, and what makes them download and stay Channel mix: a low-cost channel mix with budget split and expected cost per install Growth loop: a referral or viral loop built around the product’s core moment, the whole family’s net worth on one screen Metrics: how you’d measure success, with the funnel numbers that get you to 1,00,000 Product Engineering & AI Open to TE/BE students in CS, IT, AI/ML and Data Science Pick one sub-track, explore the live WealthNest app, and solve one real problem in depth. - Frontend / UX Find a confusing flow, slow screen or hard-to-read data view in the app, for example family-level portfolio concentration on a small mobile screen. Redesign it. Submit: problem analysis, wireframes or a Figma prototype, and the reasoning behind your choices. - Backend Engineering WealthNest pulls bank accounts, mutual funds, demat holdings, FDs and insurance for multiple family members into one view. Spot a reliability, security or scalability bottleneck in how that data could be ingested, normalised or refreshed. Propose a fix. Submit: architecture diagram, design trade-offs, and a PoC or pseudo-code where it helps. - Artificial Intelligence Choose one: Make financial statement (PDF) parsing more accurate, and catch extraction errors automatically. Design a RAG and evaluation workflow so AI: ChatBot answers questions like “How much tax will I save if I move this FD?” without making up numbers. Submit: approach, evaluation method and metrics, plus a GitHub link to a PoC if you build one. Eligibility Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students across India. Team size: 1–2 members. Members can come from different colleges and different specializations. A team can enter both tracks, with a separate submission for each. Rounds - Round 1: Case Submission (21 Nov – 6 Dec 2026, 11:59 PM) Download the brief for your track, explore the WealthNest app, and submit your solution here on Unstop. - Round 2: Final Presentation (10 Dec 2026) Shortlisted teams present their solution to the WealthNest panel online: 30 minutes of presentation plus 30 minutes of Q&A. Submission Format Management track: one PDF deck, maximum 15 slides. Tech track: one PDF deck, maximum 15 slides, plus links to GitHub, Figma or a working PoC where relevant. File name: TeamName_Track.pdf Rewards PPI + internship at WealthNest for the top 2 teams in each track (4 teams in total). A Certificate of Completion for every team that submits a complete, original entry. Participation is free. Evaluation Criteria Insight grounded in a real audit of the WealthNest app Quality and depth of the solution Feasibility and measurable impact Clarity of presentation Rules Submissions must be original. Plagiarized or copied work will be disqualified. You can use AI tools, but generic, unedited AI output will be filtered out at screening. title: Call for Articles: 'The Impatient Consumer'
description: Overview This edition explores "The Impatient Consumer", looking at how quick commerce is changing the way India shops. Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now have made 10-minute delivery feel…
details_text: Overview This edition explores "The Impatient Consumer", looking at how quick commerce is changing the way India shops. Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now have made 10-minute delivery feel normal, and consumers now expect convenience instantly. But this speed has costs. Shoppers are becoming less patient, impulse purchases are rising, and neighbourhood kiranas and smaller brands are coming under pressure. This edition explores the psychology of instant gratification, how quick commerce is designed to make us buy more, and who really wins when patience goes out of fashion. Themes: Speed as the Product: Is 10-minute delivery a lasting competitive advantage or just the new normal? Explore how quick commerce has changed consumer expectations across categories, from groceries to electronics. Discuss whether speed alone can build long-term brand loyalty once every platform offers it. Impulse by Design: Why do we always end up adding "just one more item"? Examine how dark stores, app layouts, smart nudges and low-order thresholds encourage impulse buying. Discuss whether quick commerce is creating new demand or simply capturing purchases that would have happened anyway. Kiranas, D2C & the Battle for the Doorstep: Who wins and who gets squeezed in the 10-minute economy? Explore how quick commerce affects neighbourhood kiranas, distributors and D2C brands. Discuss whether these platforms help smaller brands reach new customers or concentrate power in the hands of a few players through deep discounting and visibility control. In a market where every minute counts, the real question is whether quick commerce is building genuine customer value or simply training consumers to expect everything instantly. We invite you to look at the trade-off between convenience and sustainability, and to question what businesses, communities and consumers give up in the race to the doorstep. Share your insights. Shape the conversation. details_text: About The Event REFRACT 1.0 marks the inaugural edition of a 30-hour national-level hackathon. AI & Intelligent Systems: Deploy ultra-low latency neural architectures, autonomous multi-agent workflows, computer vision algorithms, real-time sensor intelligence, and local edge inference models. Robotics & IoT (Hardware Track): Bring hardware to life. Build autonomous robots, smart gadgets, automated control systems, and connected IoT devices using microcontrollers, sensors, and actuators. App & Game Development: Create high-performance mobile applications, immersive web platforms, interactive game mechanics, real-time 3D rendering engines, and next-generation digital experiences. Space Technology: Create solutions inspired by the cosmos. Work on satellite systems, orbital tracking, space data processing, CubeSat hardware, or astronomy-related applications. Open Innovation: Ideas beyond boundaries. Defy traditional tech silos with unconstrained multidisciplinary inventions, wildcard solutions, and unconventional prototypes solving high-impact problems. title: Second Serving – A Business Revival Case Competition
description: Second Serving is a business revival case competition presented by the Infra, IT & Dorm Affairs Committee of the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Guwahati . Developed in collaboration with knowledge partner Skilled…
details_text: Second Serving is a business revival case competition presented by the Infra, IT & Dorm Affairs Committee of the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Guwahati . Developed in collaboration with knowledge partner Skilled Sapiens , the event challenges participants with a central theme: "Same Business. Same Problem. Different Response." . We’ve partnered with Skilled Sapiens , a leading consulting firm with a strategic focus on the education and business consulting spaces. In the education space, Skilled Sapiens works towards bridging the gap between academia and industry through experiential learning, industry-led mentorship, and professional capability development. In the business consulting space, the firm supports startups and emerging businesses through strategic advisory, market research, business strategy, market penetration, growth planning, and investor readiness. With a strong focus on innovation, structured problem-solving, and practical business exposure, Skilled Sapiens aims to empower individuals and organizations to navigate complex business challenges and achieve sustainable growth. Core Principle: Revive, Don't Replace The overarching goal is not to build an entirely new business, but to revive the existing one . Teams must preserve the selected business's original identity, fundamental value proposition, and core business model . The circumstances and problems that caused the original failure must be treated as given and confronted directly . Transforming the company into an unrelated venture or eliminating the original problem by altering circumstances violates the non-negotiable rules of the competition . Competition Structure Round 1: Diagnose & Reimagine Teams must identify the root causes of the selected business's decline and determine the critical intervention point . The submission requires a 3-slide PDF deck (excluding cover, thank-you, and optional appendix slides) . Slide 1 must cover the Executive Summary, Slide 2 must analyze "Why Did It Fail?", and Slide 3 must propose "What Could Have Been Done Differently?" . Round 2: Build the Revival Strategy Shortlisted teams must build a commercially viable revival strategy demonstrating implementation and sustainability . Teams must submit an approximately 6-slide deck covering Strategic Direction, Market & Customer, Business Model, Marketing & Growth, Competition, Operations, Financial Viability, and an Implementation Roadmap . Round 3: Revival in the Real World Finalists will present their comprehensive revival strategy before a panel of judges . Teams will have 5 minutes to present, followed by a 2-minute Q&A session where they must defend their assumptions, choices, and feasibility . Rewards & Recognition Cash Prize: There is a total prize pool of ₹10,000 for the winning teams . Live Project: The top 3 teams will earn a free-of-cost opportunity to work on a live project with Skilled Sapiens . Submission Guidelines & Rules All submissions must be in PDF format . Files must be named using the format: TeamName_Round()_SecondServing . Only one member per team is allowed to submit the solution via Unstop . Decks should be strictly grounded in the business context, avoiding broad, unrelated analyses . The use of Generative AI for creating the case deck is discouraged . Sources must be clearly cited, and any plagiarism will result in immediate disqualification . No deadlines will be extended, and failure to submit on time will lead to the cancellation of the team's participation . The organizing team's decisions are final and binding on all participants .

details_text: Overview Jaipuria Institute of Management, Jaipur, is excited to present E-Week 2026, themed "Local to Global." This event is dedicated to fostering innovation and entrepreneurship, with a strong emphasis on identifying local opportunities, nurturing indigenous ideas, and transforming them into globally competitive business solutions. The theme encourages participants to explore the potential of local products, traditional industries, regional resources, and community-driven innovations and envision how these can create an impact beyond geographical boundaries. Participants will be challenged to think creatively, identify opportunities within their surroundings, and develop entrepreneurial solutions with global relevance. The event includes multiple rounds of evaluations and presentations, providing students with an excellent platform to showcase their entrepreneurial skills and innovative ideas. Rules and Guidelines Shortlisting will be done on the basis of creativity, information, and clarity of solutions. Tasks must be completed within the specified timelines; late submissions will not be accepted. Unfair practices are prohibited and will result in disqualification. Submissions should be made in PDF format. Teams must remain vigilant and regularly check their email and phone for updates. Team size: 1-4 members. Theme Reveal: Local to Global The theme "Local to Global" invites participants to explore how ideas rooted in local communities, cultures, resources, and markets can evolve into scalable business opportunities with national and international recognition. India is home to countless traditional businesses, indigenous products, regional art forms, local innovations, and untapped entrepreneurial potential. The challenge lies in identifying these opportunities and transforming them through innovation, technology, branding, and strategic business models to compete in the global marketplace. This year, E-Week will revolve around the central theme of "Local to Global," encouraging students to think beyond geographical limitations and explore how local strengths can become global success stories. All prototypes and idea pitches during the event will revolve around this theme. Participants will be encouraged to: Identify local products, services, traditional practices, or community-based businesses that have the potential to reach national and international markets. Develop innovative business ideas that transform regional resources, indigenous knowledge, and traditional industries into scalable ventures. Explore how technology, digital platforms, marketing, and branding can help local businesses expand their reach globally. Showcase how sustainable and inclusive business models can create economic opportunities for local communities while establishing a global presence. Develop strategies to overcome challenges related to scalability, international competition, logistics, quality standards, and global customer preferences. The aim is to inspire students to recognise the entrepreneurial potential within their immediate surroundings and develop innovative business solutions that can make a difference on a larger scale. The focus will be on building ventures that preserve local identity while embracing global standards, opportunities, and aspirations. By adopting this theme, E-Week 2026 will celebrate the spirit of entrepreneurship by connecting local potential with global possibilities, encouraging future business leaders to think globally while staying rooted in local strengths. Real-Life Examples Jaipur Rugs (India) Transformed Rajasthan's traditional carpet weaving and local craftsmanship into a globally recognised brand. Connected rural artisans with international markets through innovation, design, and ethical business practices. Paper Boat - Food & Beverages Revived traditional Indian drinks and regional flavours through modern packaging and branding. Demonstrates how local tastes and cultural heritage can be transformed
