description: FINVENT 2027 – The Finance & Valuation Challenge In a financial landscape shaped by rapid technological disruption, capital market volatility, and complex deal-making, the ability to bridge quantitative rigor with sound…
details_text: FINVENT 2027 – The Finance & Valuation Challenge In a financial landscape shaped by rapid technological disruption, capital market volatility, and complex deal-making, the ability to bridge quantitative rigor with sound valuation is more valuable than ever. Shaastra 2027, IIT Madras, presents Finvent , a national-level pure-finance competition that brings together aspiring investment bankers, equity researchers, quantitative analysts, and problem-solvers from across the country. Moving beyond conventional management and strategy cases, Finvent is designed to test participants' financial acumen, mathematical precision, and analytical depth across high-growth, emerging technology sectors. Participants will be challenged to look past surface-level narratives, dissect complex financial data, and defend rigorous, data-driven valuations in a high-stakes boardroom environment. Competition Format: The competition will be conducted in three elimination rounds: Round 1 – Finance Aptitude Challenge (Online): The opening round will be a 15-minute timed online quiz on Unstop covering quantitative aptitude, probability, core corporate finance, valuation fundamentals, and analytical reasoning. Teams will be shortlisted based on their performance. Round 2 – Financial Thesis Submission (Online): The top 30–40 shortlisted teams will be presented with a real-world financial problem statement requiring them to build an investment or valuation thesis, perform core calculations, and establish key assumptions. Teams will submit a concise 2–3 slide pitch deck in the prescribed format, with the top 10 teams (along with 2–3 reserve teams) advancing to the final round. Round 3 – Grand Finale (On-Campus Final): The final round will be an on-campus finance challenge at IIT Madras. Qualifying teams will present their comprehensive final valuation decks before an expert panel of judges. (Note: This is a pure presentation round). Eligibility and Team Guidelines: Open to undergraduate (engineering, sciences, commerce, economics, etc.) and postgraduate/MBA students from recognised colleges and universities across India. Students from all academic streams and specialisations with an interest in quantitative analysis, corporate finance, and financial markets are eligible. Teams must consist of 1–3 members . All members of a team must belong to the same institute. Inter-specialisation and cross-year teams within the same institute are permitted. A student may register as part of only one team. Each team may submit only one entry for the competition. General Guidelines: Participants must register with accurate details and ensure that all team members meet the eligibility requirements. All submissions must be original and prepared by the registered team members. Case briefs and datasets shared during the competition are strictly for competition use and must not be distributed publicly. Participants are expected to maintain professional conduct throughout the competition. Further instructions, submission requirements, and round-specific guidelines will be communicated to shortlisted teams by the organising committee. The final round will be conducted on campus at IIT Madras. Finalists will be required to obtain a valid Shaastra pass through the official Shaastra website. The organising committee reserves the right to make necessary changes to the competition schedule or format. Decisions of the organising committee and judges will be final. Model rigorously. details_text: About Kurukshetra Kurukshetra is the flagship annual cultural, sports and management fest of FLAME University, Pune. Now in its 19th edition , it brings together students from across India to compete, create and lead. The management fest is its arena for ideas, strategy and sharp thinking. About Chakravyuh Chakravyuh is the national case competition of Kurukshetra '27. It brings together ambitious students to tackle complex, real-world business challenges. Teams analyse the problem, build strategic and innovative solutions, and defend their recommendations before a panel of industry experts. More than a competition, it is a test of analytical thinking, creativity, business acumen and decision-making under pressure. Teams compete with peers from across the country, gain industry exposure and show they can turn ideas into action. The best teams share a ₹30,000 prize pool . OBJECTIVES Encourage the practical application of theoretical knowledge to real business situations. Promote a structured, problem-solving approach and critical thinking. Eligibility & Teams Open to all undergraduate and postgraduate students enrolled in any recognised college or university in India. Participation is strictly in teams of 2 . Individual entries are not allowed. A student may be part of only one team . Team members cannot be changed after registration closes. Registration is only through the Unstop event page, and is free. Both members must register with accurate details. Certificates are issued with the names given at registration. The organising committee may ask for a valid college ID at any stage to verify eligibility ROUND 1 · ONLINE QUIZ Window: 23 December 2026, 12:05 AM to 24 December 2026, 11:59 PM IST, on Unstop. Format: A timed multiple-choice quiz on business awareness, current affairs and reasoning. The team attempts it once, within the window. Any form of unfair means, including sharing questions or using multiple devices or accounts, leads to disqualification. Shortlist: The top-scoring teams are announced on 25 December 2026 and move to Round 2. Ties are broken by the time taken. Round 2 · Case Submission The case is released to shortlisted teams on Unstop on 25 December 2026 . Teams analyse it and submit their solution by 30 December 2026, 11:59 PM IST . Format: PPT or PDF, uploaded on the Unstop event page. Length: A maximum of 3 content slides . The title slide and the reference slide are extra and do not count. Language: English only. File name: TeamName_CollegeName_CaseComp Anything beyond the slide limit will not be evaluated. Cite all data and sources on the reference slide. Finalists: The top teams from Round 2 are announced as finalists on Unstop and by email on or before 6 Jan 2027 . Originality, Plagiarism & AI Policy Plagiarism limit: Every submission is checked with plagiarism-detection software. A similarity score above 20% leads to immediate disqualification. AI-generated content: The analysis and recommendations must be the team's own. Content generated with AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude or Copilot above 20% leads to immediate disqualification. Cite your sources: Data, frameworks and ideas taken from others must be credited. Uncited copying counts as plagiarism even if it falls under the limit. Verification: Judges may question any team on its numbers, sources and assumptions during the finale. A team that cannot explain its own work may be disqualified. The committee's decision on plagiarism and AI use is final. Round 3 · Grand Finale The finalist teams travel to FLAME University, Pune on 23 January 2027 to present their case solution to a panel of industry experts. Time: Each team gets 7 minutes to present, followed by 3 minutes of Q&A with the panel. Teams are stopped when time runs out. Deck: Teams present the deck submitted in Round 2. Any changes must be sent to the organisers by the deadline they announce. Both members must be present, and both are expected to take part in the presentation and Q&

details_text: Overview CTF CICADA 2026 – Capture The Flag Organised by IEEE Student Branch & IET On Campus, BIT Mesra Get ready to enter the world of cryptic clues, hidden messages, ciphers, and challenging puzzles! CTF CICADA 2026 brings back our Capture The Flag competition with an entirely new experience inspired by Cicada 3301 , the mysterious internet puzzle phenomenon that captivated thousands of people worldwide. This year, we are moving beyond the traditional Jeopardy-style CTF format and introducing an Alternate Reality Game (ARG)-style experience . Participants will navigate through 30 levels, each presenting a trail of clues that must be deciphered to unlock the next stage. Whether you enjoy cryptography, cybersecurity, logical reasoning, digital investigation, or solving unconventional puzzles, CICADA is your opportunity to put your skills to the test. Event Format Competition: Capture The Flag (CTF) Format: ARG-style, fully online Total Levels: 30 Team Size: 1–3 members Participation: Open across India Duration: 10 December 2026 – 10 January 2027 What Makes CICADA Different? Unlike conventional CTF competitions that present standalone challenges on a leaderboard, CICADA follows a progressive puzzle-solving journey. 30 Progressive Levels: Every level contains a trail of clues. Solve one to unlock the next. ARG-Inspired Challenges: Explore clues involving images, ciphers, websites, and hidden information. Staged Releases: Levels will open in stages and remain accessible until the competition ends. Hints Along the Way: Hints will be released to help participants progress. No Elimination: Participants can continue solving challenges throughout the competition period. Who Can Participate? CICADA 2026 welcomes curious, analytical, and technically inclined participants from across India. You can participate: Individually, or In a team of 2–3 members. Bring your friends together, form a team, and take on the challenge. Prizes and Recognition Exciting prizes for the winning teams. E-certificates for every participant. Recognition for outstanding performance. About the Organisers IEEE Student Branch and IET On Campus at Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra, Ranchi, are student-run campus chapters of two leading engineering societies. Since 2019, we have been organising Capture The Flag competitions, technical events, and hands-on workshops covering Linux, Git, Python, web development, and more. With CICADA 2026, we aim to bring an engaging, month-long puzzle-solving experience to participants across India. Important Dates Competition Starts: 10 December 2026 Competition Ends: 10 January 2027 Mode: Completely Online Get ready to decode, investigate, collaborate, and uncover what lies beyond the next clue. Organised by: IEEE Student Branch & IET On Campus Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra, Ranchi The trail is waiting. Will you follow it? CTF CICADA 2026 – Every clue leads somewhere.

details_text: Overview Logic Sprint is a 30-minute online logical reasoning race on Mind Race. There are no teams and no waiting: press Start and solve as many reasoning puzzles as you can before the clock runs out. The questions adapt to you . Format and rules Saturday, 28 November 2026, 8:00 to 8:30 PM IST (online, on phone or laptop) Solo and live. The questions adapt to how you're doing. Each question has its own timer, and running out counts as wrong. Skips: you can skip at most 1 question in every 3. No negative marking. Minimum attempts: try at least 30 questions to appear on the leaderboard. Stay on the screen. Switching to another app or tab for more than 2 seconds counts the question as wrong and pauses you. Late start: Start closes 10 minutes before the end, so join by 8:20 PM . Fair play: results are checked for fair play before winners are confirmed. Rewards Certificates for the top 3 (winner and runners-up) Your Mind Race rating moves after the event Who can join: everyone. It's free. How to join Open MindRace (event code CMUT4E). Sign up free (Google takes one tap) and tap Join. Come back on Saturday at 8:00 PM and press Start. Warm up before Saturday: practise reasoning free on Mind Race in Practice and 1v1 matches.

description: 24 hours. One real farm problem. One room full of people trying to solve it. Most hackathons ask you to build another app for people like you. This one asks you to build for the people who feed the country. Drones that…
details_text: 24 hours. One real farm problem. One room full of people trying to solve it. Most hackathons ask you to build another app for people like you. This one asks you to build for the people who feed the country. Drones that spot-crop stress. Rovers that spray with precision. A voice assistant that answers a farmer in their own language. If you can build it, there is probably a field that needs it. Agri-Tech Hackathon is a national-level, 24-hour offline sprint hosted by K. J. Somaiya School of Engineering, Mumbai, and organised by e-CESA. Software and hardware builds are both welcome. Last edition, in numbers and names 1,772 registrations on Unstop ₹2,00,000 prize pool First place: Team Snack Overflow, D. J. Sanghvi College of Engineering, for an automated tractor-mounted sprinkler system Partners included BKT, LIC, NABARD, Festo, KIAAR, Red Bull and Domino's Why register The prize pool is now ₹3,50,000, up from ₹2,00,000 last edition. Registering is free, and Round 1 is just an abstract and a short pitch video you can record from anywhere. You don't need an agriculture background or prior AI, IoT or blockchain experience. Round 1 is about how you think: write your abstract on any of the five themes. For the sprint, problem statements go live 3 to 4 days before the event on our website, grouped by tech bucket. Mentors stay with you during the sprint, and the organisers provide food and snacks. You pitch your build to a panel of industry and academic judges. Eligibility Undergraduate and postgraduate students, any discipline Teams of 3 to 4 members; cross-college and cross-specialisation teams allowed Themes Next-Gen Agri-Tech: robotics, drones, computer vision, IoT, AI and predictive analytics Agri-Market Access: direct marketplaces, demand forecasting, blockchain traceability, smart storage and quality grading Farmer Empowerment: multilingual AI, offline-first tools, hyperlocal advisories and AR/VR training Green Growth: soil regeneration, water conservation, carbon monitoring and climate intelligence Open Innovation (Round 1 only): your idea, your solution, as long as it serves agriculture Rounds Round 1: Abstract Submission (online) Submit a 5 to 6 page abstract (maximum) as a PDF, proposing your own solution under any of the five themes, along with an unlisted YouTube video link (5 to 7 minutes) explaining your solution in simple terms, as if pitching to a farmer who has never seen it before. This checks your oratory and pitching skills, since your solution ultimately has to be understood by farmers on the ground. Teams are shortlisted for Round 2 based on the abstract and the video. Deadline: 27 December 2026, 11:59 PM IST. Shortlist announcement: 7 January 2027. Round 2: The 24-Hour Sprint (offline, at KJSSE) Shortlisted teams from Round 1 move directly into Round 2, no separate registration needed. Dates: 28 to 29 January 2027 (Thursday to Friday). Prizes Total prize pool: ₹3,50,000 Winner: ₹1,50,000 + certificate First Runner Up: ₹1,20,000 + certificate Second Runner Up: ₹80,000 + certificate Rules Projects must be built for this hackathon. Pre-existing projects are not allowed. Each team submits one abstract. Team members cannot be changed after registration is finalised. Participants bring their own laptops, hardware, tools and development environments. The organisers' decision is final. Partners, sponsors, prizes, dates and other details mentioned here are subject to change; the latest confirmed information will always be on this page and our official website.

title: Mantrastra
organiser: Madan Mohan Malaviya University of Technology
description: About the Competition MANTRASTRA is a three-round AI Engineering Competition designed to evaluate participants' ability to understand, debug, develop, and optimise software using AI tools. The competition focuses on…
details_text: About the Competition MANTRASTRA is a three-round AI Engineering Competition designed to evaluate participants' ability to understand, debug, develop, and optimise software using AI tools. The competition focuses on AI-assisted software engineering, code comprehension, and agentic development. Eligibility & Team Formation Open to students of all academic years from all colleges and universities. Team size: 2–4 members. Inter-college teams are allowed. Inter-specialisation and interdisciplinary teams are allowed. Each participant can register as a member of only one team. Registration is free and can be completed on Unstop. Competition Format The competition will consist of three rounds: Round 1: Build with AI Interested students will have the opportunity to attend an offline workshop covering Prompt Engineering, Git & GitHub, and Agentic AI tools, followed by a quiz. Students who do not opt for the workshop will directly participate in an online quiz conducted through Unstop. The quiz will evaluate fundamental knowledge of AI, programming, software development, and related concepts. Use of AI tools or external AI assistance is strictly prohibited during the quiz. Participants must attempt the quiz independently. Round 2: AI Code Comprehension Challenge (In-person) Shortlisted teams will be provided with an unfamiliar codebase. Teams must analyse the codebase, understand its architecture and execution flow, and identify and fix bugs. Participants will evaluate AI-generated suggestions and explain their technical decisions. Use of AI tools is permitted and encouraged in this round. Evaluation will focus on code comprehension, debugging, critical thinking, and the ability to validate AI-generated outputs. Round 3: Agentic Engineering Challenge (In-person) Finalist teams will be required to build, test, and optimise a working application. Participants can use AI assistants and autonomous AI agents throughout the development process. Teams must demonstrate their working application before the judges. Evaluation will focus on functionality, implementation, optimisation, effective AI utilisation, and the quality of the final demonstration. AI Usage Policy Round 1: AI tools are strictly prohibited during the quiz. Round 2: AI tools are permitted for code analysis, debugging, and evaluating solutions. Round 3: AI assistants and agents are permitted for application development, testing, and optimisation. Participants must understand and be able to explain the solutions and code they submit. Misuse of AI tools, plagiarism, or misrepresentation of work may result in disqualification. Important Dates & Venue Registration Deadline: 20 December 2026 Round 1 & Workshop: 22 December 2026 Round 2 & Round 3: 25–27 December 2026 Venue: MMMUT Campus, Gorakhpur. Prizes & Recognition Total Prize Pool: ₹12,000+ Certificates and further details will be communicated through the official channels of MMMUT RESO. General Rules & Regulations All participants must complete registration through either of the official registration platforms. Each team must have 2–4 members. Team composition cannot be changed after registration without approval from the organising committee. Participants must follow the instructions and time limits announced for each round. Teams must submit their solutions within the prescribed deadlines. Plagiarism, copying another team's work, or any form of unfair practice is strictly prohibited. Participants must not share confidential problem statements or solutions with other teams. Teams must ensure that they can explain and justify their submitted work. The organising committee reserves the right to disqualify teams violating competition rules. The decisions of the judges and organising committee will be final and binding. Important Instructions Participants should bring their own laptops and chargers for the in-person rounds. Carry a valid college ID card. Participants are advised to follow the official social media channels of MMMUT

title: Risk Ladder
organiser: National Institute of Bank Management (NIBM), Pune
description: Overview: Climb the Market is a gamified, team-based board game tournament that introduces students to the fundamentals of financial risk management through an engaging and competitive experience. Inspired by the…
details_text: Overview: Climb the Market is a gamified, team-based board game tournament that introduces students to the fundamentals of financial risk management through an engaging and competitive experience. Inspired by the classic Snakes & Ladders format, the game transforms market developments and financial decisions into interactive challenges. Each move on the board presents an opportunity to apply financial concepts, assess risk and make decisions in a simulated market environment. The event is designed to assess participants’ financial awareness, analytical thinking and ability to identify and respond to different categories of risk, including market, credit, liquidity, operational, legal and compliance risk. Participants will also experience the challenges of managing a simulated virtual portfolio under time and decision-making pressure. No prior finance background is required; the event is open to students from all academic disciplines. Eligibility Teams will consist of minimum of three and maximum four students. All participants must be currently pursuing a degree; students from any discipline may participate. Round Structure Round 1: Online Quiz The first round will be conducted online through a proctored quiz designed to evaluate participants’ basic financial knowledge, financial awareness and analytical aptitude. Only one member from each registered team is permitted to attempt the quiz. Each team will be allowed only one attempt. The quiz will serve as the elimination round for shortlisting teams for the offline round. 30 questions in 15 minutes. Round 2: Offline Board Game Tournament The second round will be conducted on campus. Shortlisted teams will compete in Risk Ladder, a financial risk-management board game in which each team manages a simulated virtual portfolio of ₹10,00,000 while progressing across a 100-square board. The board incorporates ladders representing sound decisions or favourable market developments, and snakes representing poor decisions or adverse market events. As teams move across the board, they will encounter different types of cards: Question Cards: Test participants’ understanding of financial and risk-management concepts. Opportunity Cards: Present favourable situations or potential opportunities that require informed decisions. Risk Cards: Introduce risk-related situations that require teams to assess possible consequences and respond appropriately. Market Event Cards: Simulate real-world market developments and their potential impact on financial positions. Teams will take turns rolling a die and moving across the board. The square on which a team lands will determine the question, card or scenario it must address. Teams’ decisions and responses will influence their progress and/or simulated portfolio, as applicable to the game mechanics. Winning Criteria The winner will be determined by either of the following outcomes: A team is the first to reach Square 100; or If no team reaches Square 100 within 20 rounds, the team with the highest portfolio value at the end of the 20th round will be declared the winner. In the event of a tie, the team that has answered the highest number of questions correctly will be declared the winner.

description: About: AIB is a competition which is inspired by MUN (Model United Nations) where we will be allotting different teams with different Banks instead of countries unlike in MUN to discuss the recent 2 agendas that are…
details_text: About: AIB is a competition which is inspired by MUN (Model United Nations) where we will be allotting different teams with different Banks instead of countries unlike in MUN to discuss the recent 2 agendas that are going on in the Banking Industry e.g.- Global Recession, Future of new banking in India by integrating Artificial intelligence, tighter Norms by RBI on Personal loan sector. The event will be headed by individuals (NIBM Students) representing the RBI Governor and Deputy Governor who will provide motions (reasons/solutions for the agendas) and the team will be speaking on it. There will also be 2 moderators (faculty/guests/alumni) who will be judging the whole competition. There will be 3 prizes for this event. Procedure: An online screening, in the form of a quiz, will be conducted before the event on the same website. The interested teams consisting of 2-3 members in each team, must register themselves on Unstop. Participants should be from the same college. No member can be a part of more than one team. There will be no negative markings in the online quiz. Based on the results, 6 teams will be shortlisted and will be given their respective banks (banks based on the time of the event will be decided) and a common agenda which will be communicated through an email. On the event day, the shortlisted team will be given a platform where the second round or discussion round wherein every team shall break into a full-fledged discussion on the agenda, putting forward their views, taking a stand, and challenging their fellow teams through interjections (counter). Results will be announced on the same day. Round 1 - Quiz (Elimination Round): An online quiz based on banking and financial services will be conducted on the Unstop platform. 40 questions must be answered in 30 minutes. There will be no negative markings in the online quiz. Only team leaders will be allowed to play the quiz. The top 6 teams will qualify for the second round. Round 2 - Discussion Round (Final Round): AIB is a MUN-inspired competition wherein 6 teams consisting of 2-3 students. Qualified teams will be representing a bank from a host of banks to discuss and put forth their views on a recent agenda relevant to the Banking Industry. This is followed by the discussion round. In this, every team shall break into a full-fledged discussion on the agenda, putting forward their views, taking a stand, and challenging their fellow teams through interjections (counter). The limit per team is 1.5 minutes - 2 minutes followed by a Real-Time News Segment wherein the house shall be presented with real-time news that shall take the event ahead with discussion on the same. The event will be headed by a NIBM Student representing the RBI Governor who will provide motions (reasons/solutions for the agenda) on which the house shall speak. The agenda shall be notified beforehand and shall run for an hour. There will also be a moderator to chair the session. Results shall be announced at the end of the event. Further details will be shared with the teams who will qualify for this round. Timeline: Quiz date - 21st December 2026 Date for the Final round – 29 th Jan 2027 (Final round will be on campus)

title: Shark Tank : An On-the-Spot Product Innovation Challenge
description: Think. Innovate. Pitch . Can you create a breakthrough product when the clock is ticking? Imagine being handed a real-world crisis or problem with zero preparation. Your task is to rapidly conceive an original product…
details_text: Think. Innovate. Pitch . Can you create a breakthrough product when the clock is ticking? Imagine being handed a real-world crisis or problem with zero preparation. Your task is to rapidly conceive an original product that addresses the problem, develop a viable pitch on the spot, and convince the sharks. Welcome to SHARK TANK, a high-intensity pitch competition where you turn unexpected challenges into market-ready innovations. How Does It Work? The Pitch Battle (Single Round Format – Only One Round) A problem statement is revealed to a cohort of 5 students. Each student must individually conceptualize an original product to tackle the given problem. Speaking order is determined through random selection. The first student picked gets 5 minutes to develop an original product concept and prepare their pitch. Each participant receives 3 minutes to pitch their product individually to the panel. The second student pitches immediately after the first, continuing sequentially across all five participants. Once a cohort completes its presentations, a fresh problem statement is issued to the next cohort of 5 students. What Will You Need ? メールに送信された確認コードを入力してください。届かない場合は、迷惑メールフォルダを確認してください。 パスワードを設定し、指示があれば CAPTCHA を完了させてください。 AWS Builder ID を作成してください。初回サインイン時に、エイリアスの選択を求められます。 すでに AWS Builder ID をお持ちですか？ 以前にAWS Skill Builder をご利用になったことがある場合は、既存の認証情報でサインインしてください。新たにアカウントを作成する必要はありません。 エイリアスはどこで確認できますか？ Builder Center にサインインし、上部ナビゲーションにある自分の名前をクリックして、「プロフィールの管理」を選択してください。 プロフィールへのリンクは、次のような形式になります： builder.aws.com/community/@youralias ステップ 2: 学生資格を確認する 学生ステータスの確認は、AWS の認証パートナーであるSheerIDを通じて、現在の在籍状況を確認するためのものです。 在籍状況の確認方法 AWS Builder Center にサインインします。 プロフィールの編集 (Edit Profile) → 学生情報 (Student Details) を開きます。 [確認を開始] をクリックします。 SheerIDの指示に従い、所属機関名と在籍情報を入力してください。 必要に応じて、証明書類をアップロードしてください。 学生資格の確認でお困りですか？ 通常：数分程度です。 追加書類が必要な場合：通常24 ～48 時間かかります。 学生認証がうまくいかない場合 本人確認が却下された場合は、より鮮明な書類、または最新の在籍証明書類を提出して、再度お試しください。さらにサポートが必要な場合は、 SheerID の学生向けサポートをご利用ください。 学習内容： ブートキャンプのライブウェビナーで、興味深いテーマについて学びましょう： セッション：生成AI アプリケーションの構築とデプロイ 生成 AI 報酬と賞品： 高得点者および紹介者：高得点者と紹介者には、プレミアムAWSグッズキットまたはAmazonギフト券が贈られます。 セッションに参加し、積極的に取り組み、クイズに全力で挑みましょう！ 注：報酬は、該当するクイズの得点および選考基準に基づいて決定されます。 AIへの挑戦はここから始まります。AWS で学び、構築し、競い合い、勝利をつかみ取りましょう！

details_text: 6 Hours. One Challenge. Infinite Possibilities. Get ready to turn your engineering imagination into reality! Suryodaya College of Engineering & Technology (SCET), Nagpur, in association with Suryodaya Technology Business Incubation Foundation (STBIF) , proudly presents CENTRAL INDIA CADATHON 2.0 , the second edition of its multidisciplinary CAD Designing Competition, organized under the Youth Tech Connect (YTC) initiative . With an exciting overall prize pool of ₹25,000 , Central India CADATHON provides a platform where engineering meets creativity, innovation meets precision, and ideas transform into practical designs. This six-hour design challenge invites students from Mechanical, Electrical, and Civil Engineering backgrounds to showcase their technical knowledge, creativity, and problem-solving abilities through Computer-Aided Design (CAD). Participants will be presented with real-world engineering problem statements and challenged to develop innovative, technically sound, and practically feasible designs within the given time limit. Whether it's designing a mechanical system, developing an electrical layout, or creating an innovative civil infrastructure solution, this competition will challenge you to think beyond conventional boundaries. What awaits you? A challenging six-hour CAD design competition. Real-world engineering problem statements. An opportunity to showcase your CAD modelling and designing skills. A total prize pool of ₹25,000. Evaluation by an expert jury. Exciting prizes, awards, and recognition for outstanding designs. Internship opportunities and participation certificates. Participating Departments Mechanical Engineering Electrical Engineering Civil Engineering Students from all other engineering and related disciplines are also welcome to participate! Guidelines Maximum 2 participants per team. Individual participation is also permitted. Participants must develop their designs within the competition duration. Each team must submit its final CAD design along with the required deliverables. Challenge your engineering knowledge, explore innovative design approaches, compete with talented minds, and transform your ideas into practical digital engineering solutions. This is your opportunity to put your designing skills to the test, demonstrate your technical expertise, and gain recognition for your creativity and innovation. Your imagination is the limit. Your design is your identity. THINK. DESIGN. INNOVATE. Join CENTRAL INDIA CADATHON 2.0 on 22 January 2027 and be a part of an exciting engineering design challenge. Bring your ideas. Build your designs. Create an impact!

title: Gyantrix
description: Overview THE ULTIMATE BATTLE OF MINDS Think Beyond. Challenge Everything. A National-Level Online Knowledge & Intelligence Competition Organised by CATALYST CREW DEV COMMUNITY About Gyantrix Knowledge is powerful, but…
details_text: Overview THE ULTIMATE BATTLE OF MINDS Think Beyond. Challenge Everything. A National-Level Online Knowledge & Intelligence Competition Organised by CATALYST CREW DEV COMMUNITY About Gyantrix Knowledge is powerful, but the ability to apply it under pressure is what makes the difference. Welcome to GYANTRIX 2026, an exciting national-level online quiz competition designed to challenge your knowledge, logical reasoning, analytical abilities, and intellectual curiosity. GYANTRIX brings together five diverse domains — Technology, Logical Reasoning, Riddles, Fun Trivia & Everyday Science, and General Awareness — into one engaging competitive experience. This competition is designed for students who love exploring new ideas, solving challenging problems, testing their knowledge, and competing with brilliant minds from across the country. Whether you are a technology enthusiast, a logical thinker, a general knowledge enthusiast, or simply someone who enjoys challenging their brain, GYANTRIX offers an opportunity to put your abilities to the test. You don't need to be a coding expert or have specialised technical knowledge. What matters is your curiosity, accuracy, awareness, and ability to think smartly. One Competition. Five Domains. One Leaderboard. Countless Possibilities. Are you ready to prove your potential? Objectives of Gyantrix GYANTRIX aims to: Encourage intellectual curiosity and continuous learning among students. Promote healthy competition across colleges and universities in India. Evaluate logical reasoning, analytical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. Test awareness of technology, science, and the world around us. Provide an inclusive competitive platform for technical and non-technical students. Recognise individuals who demonstrate strong knowledge, accuracy, and quick thinking. Competition Format GYANTRIX 2026 will follow a single-round online quiz format. Participants will attempt a set of multiple-choice questions covering five different knowledge domains. Competition Structure Competition Type: Online Quiz Participation: Individual Total Rounds: 1 Total Questions: 30 Question Format: Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) Total Duration: 25 Minutes Difficulty Level: Easy to Moderate Maximum Score: 120 Marks Platform: Unstop All participants will attempt the same quiz under the same assessment conditions. There will be no team participation, coding round, or presentation round. Quiz Domains & Syllabus The competition is divided into five carefully selected categories to ensure a balanced assessment of technical knowledge, reasoning, creativity, and general awareness. 01. Technology & Computer Fundamentals 8 Questions | 26.7% Test your understanding of the digital and technological world. Topics include: Programming Fundamentals Computer Fundamentals Database Management Concepts Computer Networks Cybersecurity Basics Artificial Intelligence Fundamentals Internet and Digital Technologies 02. details_text: Sharpen your skills, test your vision, and lead like entrepreneurs. Inventopreneur is a startup arena for participants to present a business idea, demonstrate its market potential, and defend its commercial viability. The event puts entrepreneurial thinking, communication, and financial awareness to the test. Opportunity Rounds: Round 1 – Bizz Quiz (Online): The team leader completes a 30-question quiz covering entrepreneurship and related concepts. The quiz acts as an elimination stage for teams progressing to the next round. Round 2 – The Marketer’s Pitch (Offline): Teams present their idea with a focus on the product or service, value proposition, target market, USP, business model, market-entry strategy, and basic financial projections. The presentation is followed by a judges’ Q&A. Round 3 – The Investor’s Pitch (Offline): Finalist teams pitch their business to a panel and fellow participants acting as investors. The pitch focuses on financials, scalability, feasibility, and investment potential. Teams also allocate a virtual ₹50 lakh investment budget among other teams and submit their portfolio.

details_text: Every empire leaves fingerprints. Legacy Files is a business-detective challenge in which teams investigate a hidden company by solving puzzles, interpreting evidence, and uncovering its Foundation, Pivot, and Frontier. The strongest teams then defend the company as its board of directors. Opportunity Rounds Online Screening & Team Leader Interview If registrations exceed the stated threshold, teams take a screening quiz. Qualifying team leaders proceed to a one-on-one online interview. Round 1 – The Legacy Vault (Offline, Day 1) Teams solve an opening evidence puzzle and move through four stations. Each station tests skills such as pattern recognition, business data interpretation, logic, and spotting inconsistencies. Clues are combined to identify the hidden company; the top eight teams advance. Round 2 – Boardroom Under Fire (Offline, Day 2) Teams act as the identified company’s board and respond to questions from judges and journalists. Crisis, market, legacy, and surprise prompts test their judgement, communication, and ability to defend decisions under pressure

details_text: Analyse the market. Make the call. Manage your portfolio. Financial Forward is a two-day stock market simulation and analysis competition. Opportunity Rounds: Online Screening Quiz: The online qualifying quiz tests stock market and finance fundamentals and selects teams for the on-campus event. Short selling is prohibited; teams are evaluated on how effectively they manage their portfolio. details_text: In the world of business, one deal can change everything. But knowing which deal to make and how to make it, is what sets great strategists apart. THE ACQUISITION ARENA brings you into the world of mergers and acquisitions, where businesses look for opportunities to grow, gain an edge, and create value. Put yourself in the decision-maker's seat, evaluate the opportunities in front of you, and think through the challenges that come with making a deal. It's about looking beyond the numbers, understanding what makes a business valuable, and deciding whether an opportunity is worth pursuing. Bring your business sense, think on your feet, and show us how you'd approach a deal when the stakes are high. Every deal has two sides. Can you make the right move? Participants must adhere to the prescribed format and submission deadlines for each round. Judges will evaluate participants on strategic thinking, financial analysis, valuation, negotiation, and presentation skills. The organisers reserve the right to make necessary changes to the event schedule or rules. The judges' decisions regarding evaluation and final rankings will be final and binding.

title: Reverse Tank
description: Where Founders Become Investors. Where Investors Have to Earn the Deal. Most competitions ask you to build a startup and pitch it. Reverse Tank asks you to do both sides of the deal. Every team enters with one Founder…
details_text: Where Founders Become Investors. Where Investors Have to Earn the Deal. Most competitions ask you to build a startup and pitch it. Reverse Tank asks you to do both sides of the deal. Every team enters with one Founder and two Investors. You will build and pitch a startup, defend your business under questioning, evaluate other teams’ startups, conduct due diligence, negotiate terms, deploy a limited fund, and ultimately defend your investment decisions before a panel of industry experts. There are no external case packs. No outside startups. No pre-written deals. The participants create the deal flow. The strongest founders from one round become the startups that investors compete to back in the next. The sharpest investors earn their place in the Finals, where they must prove not just what they invested in, but why they were the right investor to make that decision. Welcome to Reverse Tank, Strategia’s flagship finance track. The Core Concept Reverse Tank is designed around one central question: can you think like a founder, invest like a VC, and negotiate like a dealmaker? Every team consists of: 1 Founder , responsible for building and defending the startup. 2 Investors , responsible for evaluating opportunities, negotiating deals and managing the team’s fund. The Founder and Investors operate as one team, but their objectives are deliberately different. The Founder wants to secure the best possible deal. The Investors want to deploy capital only when the risk-adjusted opportunity makes sense. Across the competition, you will experience both sides of the venture capital ecosystem: raising capital and deploying it. How the Competition Works The competition has four rounds: two online and two offline. Round 1: Online Qualifier (Due Diligence Test), 28 Jan 2026 Teams get access to a simulated data room (financial statements, cap table, revenue and operating metrics, transaction information, company background, and planted red flags). The test is 10 minutes long, with one attempt per team. It tests your ability to identify risks, interpret financial information and assess valuation. Round 2: Founder Video Round Your Founder submits a 2.5-minute pitch video of your most investible idea. Alongside it, your team files a public Diligence Sheet (sector, stage, one-liner, headline numbers, public ask) and a private Terms Sheet (minimum cheque, maximum equity, optional strategic-fit clause) that is never shown to investors. The Founder must make the opportunity investible. Round 3: The Offline Deal Floor, 15 Feb 2027 (11:00 AM – 6:00 PM) All teams which qualified for R2 compete live on campus at Loyola College, Chennai. They are divided into 10 panels of 5 seats, operating across 3 concurrent rooms. Before the event, your Investors file an Investor Form and receive a Persona Card and a fixed notional fund. Panel N invests while Panels N+1 and N+2 pitch, wrapping around after Panel 10. Every panel invests once and pitches twice. Teams alternate between: Investing: evaluate fellow participants, conduct rapid diligence, challenge assumptions, negotiate terms, and decide whether to close or pass. Pitching: enter the room and pitch your startup to competing investor seats with limited capital and multiple opportunities competing for their attention. Round 4: Grand Finale (Defend the Deal), 16 Feb 2027 The top 10 teams, ranked by investing performance, defend “Why this deal?” (diligence, valuation, portfolio logic) and “Why you?” (strategic fit) before partner VCs and founders. The Live Deal Format Every deal in Round 3 follows a strict 6-minute format: 2 minutes, Pitch: the Founder presents the problem, solution, business model, market opportunity, traction and assumptions, competitive positioning, funding requirement, and why the investor should care. 3 minutes, Grill & Negotiate: the investors take control. details_text: RAIT-CTF 2.0– National Level Capture The Flag Competition Get ready to test your cybersecurity skills, challenge your limits, and compete against some of the brightest minds in cybersecurity! RAIT-CTF is a national-level Capture The Flag (CTF) competition organized by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at Ramrao Adik Institute of Technology (RAIT) . It provides a competitive platform for cybersecurity enthusiasts to showcase their technical expertise, analytical thinking, and problem-solving abilities through hands-on cybersecurity challenges. As far the Prizepool in concerned, Do not worry, we have some exciting cash prizes and stuff!! Competition Structure The competition will be conducted in two rounds: Round 1 – Online Qualifier Mode: Online Duration: 12 Hours Participants will compete in challenging cybersecurity problems across multiple domains. Top 50 qualifying teams will advance to the offline finale. Round 2 – Offline Grand Finale Mode: Offline Duration: 24 Hours Shortlisted teams will compete in an intensive CTF competition, testing their technical expertise, teamwork, and ability to solve complex security challenges. CTF Domains The competition will feature challenges across seven cybersecurity domains: Web: Discover and exploit vulnerabilities in web applications. Cloud: Investigate cloud infrastructure, configurations, and security vulnerabilities. Reversing: Analyse compiled binaries and reverse-engineer software to uncover hidden functionality. Forensics: Investigate digital evidence, analyse files, and uncover hidden information. Cryptography: Solve encryption-based challenges and uncover weaknesses in cryptographic implementations. OSINT: Gather intelligence and extract valuable information from publicly available sources. Miscellaneous: Tackle unconventional challenges that test creativity, technical knowledge, and problem-solving abilities. Eligibility Criteria Open exclusively to college students currently pursuing undergraduate (UG) or postgraduate (PG) degree programmes . Participants must be enrolled in a recognized college or university. Students from all academic disciplines are welcome, provided they have an interest in cybersecurity. Why Participate? Compete at a national level against talented cybersecurity enthusiasts. Test your practical cybersecurity and ethical hacking skills. Experience challenging, real-world-inspired security scenarios. Network with like-minded individuals and cybersecurity enthusiasts. Showcase your skills and gain recognition in the cybersecurity community. Are You Ready? The challenges are set. The competition awaits. Only the sharpest minds will make it to the finale. Capture. Compete. Conquer

title: ELU Build
description: About ELUBuild ELUBuild is the flagship solo product-building challenge by EduLinkUp . Over the course of the buildathon, individual builders pitch innovative software ideas, and once approved, build, document, and ship…
details_text: About ELUBuild ELUBuild is the flagship solo product-building challenge by EduLinkUp . Over the course of the buildathon, individual builders pitch innovative software ideas, and once approved, build, document, and ship real-world SaaS applications from the ground up. The mission of ELUBuild is to discover and empower solo builders to create sustainable, user-ready digital products. Exceptional projects will be selected for integration into the ELU Store platform, with opportunities for direct deployment, hosting, and potential publishing on the Google Play Store on behalf of EduLinkUp. The Complete Event Flow ELUBuild runs across clear, structured phases: Registration & Track Exploration: Register via the EduLinkUp mobile app. Review the announced tracks and loose problem statement suggestions provided by EduLinkUp. These serve as inspiration-participants are completely free to think beyond these suggestions and tackle any authentic, high-impact problem within the domain. Use this phase to brainstorm, validate needs, and prepare your pitch before the idea portal opens. Idea Submission Phase: When the idea window opens, submit your idea proposal (project name, problem statement, target users, proposed solution, anticipated tech stack, solo buildability feasibility, and an explanatory video link). You can submit anytime while the window is active. Continuous Review & Approval: The EduLinkUp team reviews submissions on a rolling basis. Ideas can be approved at any time while the window is open. Share Your Vision: Once your idea is approved, you can (and are encouraged to) publish your explanatory pitch video on social media. Social Media Engagement Leaderboard (Active in Idea & Build Phases): A dedicated engagement leaderboard tracks reach, quality, and engagement of participants' social media posts across both the Idea Phase and the Building Phase . Compelling explanations, progress updates, and demos that resonate with the community rank higher. Idea Phase Closure, Review & Stage 1 Certification: The idea submission portal closes at 11:59 PM IST on the deadline day. The final review round is completed, and results are officially released to all participants. Stage 1 Certification: All builders whose ideas are approved receive official Stage 1 ELUBuild recognition and advance to the building phase. Building Phase (Next.js + Supabase): Building takes place inside the edulinkup-interns GitHub organisation. Shortlisted builders create their public repository under edulinkup-interns . Mandatory Tech Stack: Projects must be built using Next.js and Supabase , with authentication integrated via EduLinkUp OAuth ( @edulinkup/auth SDK). Detailed step by step instructions/guide of connecting your site with EduLinkUp OAuth will be shared before the building phase. Weekly Social Updates: Builders must share at least one weekly progress update on social media (e.g., #buildinpublic , feature demos, architecture highlights, or lessons learned). Engaging, authentic content helps you climb the Social Leaderboard. Repository Commits & Commit Quality Leaderboard: Steady, consistent development through the build window is tracked on a dedicated Commit Leaderboard . Quality & Consistency Over Raw Volume: Scoring evaluates steady engineering rhythm, meaningful commit messages, and genuine code evolution-not artificial commit spamming or scripts. Manual Audits: Code and repository activity will be regularly inspected manually. Use of commit bots, artificial commit scripts, or bulk dumping pre-existing code on the final day will lead to immediate disqualification . Final Submission & Judging: Submit your GitHub repository (under edulinkup-interns ), a deployed live demo URL, and a comprehensive product walkthrough video. Independent evaluations determine top ranks (Winner / Top 1, Top 3, Top 5, Top 7, and All participants). Event Conclusion, Rewards & ELU Store Integration: Winners and top builders receive trophies, official swags kits, domain vouchers

title: Vincenza 13.0 - The International Business Plan Competition
description: “It’s not about ideas. It’s about making ideas happen.” Every enduring enterprise begins as a single idea and the conviction to pursue it. Vincenza exists to honour that conviction and to put it to the test. Vincenza is…
details_text: “It’s not about ideas. It’s about making ideas happen.” Every enduring enterprise begins as a single idea and the conviction to pursue it. Vincenza exists to honour that conviction and to put it to the test. Vincenza is the international Business Plan Competition of Delphique , the National Management Convention of MDI Gurgaon. Over the years it has grown into a stage where ambition meets capital and where the next generation of entrepreneurs present their vision to the people who back the future. This year, Vincenza 13.0 is presented in collaboration with Auxano Capital and Eximius Ventures , bringing participants face to face with leading venture capital firms that actively back the next wave of Indian start-ups. Vincenza invites student founders of early-stage start-ups and aspiring entrepreneurs to present business ideas they are building today or plan to build tomorrow. Whether the business idea is a well-researched concept or a start-up already finding its first customers, Vincenza offers a platform to validate it, sharpen it and showcase it at a national level. Every business idea will be assessed on its scalability, feasibility and potential to transform its industry. Over three progressively demanding rounds, teams will move from a crisp opening pitch to a comprehensive business plan, refining their strategy at every stage. The journey culminates in the Grand Finale on the MDI Gurgaon campus, where the finalists take the stage and pitch their business ideas live before a distinguished panel of Venture Capitalists from Auxano Capital and Eximius Ventures . The top three teams will share cash prizes worth ₹1,00,000 , a prestigious recognition of innovation, practicality and entrepreneurial vision. Why Participate Investor exposure: Present your business ideas directly to Venture Capitalists Expert evaluation: Receive the scrutiny of seasoned investors on your business model, financials and growth strategy A national stage: Compete with the brightest entrepreneurial minds from campuses across India Recognition and rewards: Earn cash prizes, goodies and certificates that mark your entrepreneurial journey Eligibility Criteria Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students across India, including student founders of early-stage start-ups Team size: 3 to 4 members Teams may include members from different colleges and specialisations Multiple teams from the same college are allowed Prizes and Rewards Winner: ₹60,000 1st Runner-Up: ₹25,000 2nd Runner-Up: ₹15,000 Beyond the cash prizes, participants can look forward to: Exclusive gift vouchers and goodies Other attractive non-cash benefits Certificates of Participation for all participants

title: The Algo Trading Innovation Challenge
description: Complete Regsiteration and Submission at: https://techfest.org/competitions/Algo It is mandatory to register on Techfest Website . further details will be updated on the Website only . About The Algo Trading Innovation…
details_text: Complete Regsiteration and Submission at: https://techfest.org/competitions/Algo It is mandatory to register on Techfest Website . further details will be updated on the Website only . About The Algo Trading Innovation Challenge is a national fintech competition by Delta Exchange and Techfest, IIT Bombay, built around a stark fact: SEBI found that 87.7% of individual equity-derivatives traders made net losses in FY26. Teams study Delta Exchange's AlgoHub, its ecosystem of six algorithmic trading features, identify a significant gap that Futures and Options traders face, and design an original, AI-assisted capability that goes beyond what the platform offers today. The top 50 teams turn their ideas into working prototypes at an on-campus hackathon at Techfest, IIT Bombay, Asia's largest science and technology festival. Structure The competition runs in two rounds, with Round 2 as an on-campus hackathon at Techfest, IIT Bombay. Eligibility: Open to all students with a valid ID from their educational institution. Cross-institutional teams are encouraged. Team size: Maximum 4 members per team. The Challenge: Teams select one or two (maximum two) of the six AlgoHub features, Algo Marketplace, Algo Builder, API Copilot, Trading Bot, APIs, or Trade Data, identify a significant product gap or unmet need that F&O traders face within them, and design an innovative, AI-assisted capability that adds meaningful functionality beyond what exists today. Teams may propose an independent innovation per feature or one unified solution covering both. Delta Exchange is already working on natural-language strategy creation, backtesting, and trading intelligence, so teams are encouraged not to build their proposal primarily around those capabilities. Round 1 - Online Submission (Screening) A conceptual round; no working prototype is required and teams do not need to deploy live strategies or trade with real capital. Teams submit a presentation of no more than 6 slides (PPT/PPTX or PDF export) covering: Selected Feature(s) & Product Understanding Problem Identification & Product Gap Proposed AI-Assisted Innovation Real-World Trading Use Case Technical Approach & Feasibility Expected Impact & Value Only the Team Leader may submit. The 50 highest-scoring teams qualify for Round 2; ties at the cutoff are broken by the higher score in Innovation & AI Application, then Problem Identification & Trader Relevance, then Technical Feasibility. Round 2 - On-Campus Hackathon at IIT Bombay The top 50 teams develop their proposed innovations into working prototypes and demonstrate them at Techfest, IIT Bombay. Detailed format and judging guidelines will be shared with shortlisted teams. Timeline Registration closes - 30th November 2026 Round 1 submission deadline - 30th November 2026 Shortlist announcement - 5th December 2026 Finals (on-campus hackathon at IIT Bombay) - 15th-18th December 2026 Rewards and Prizes INR 50,000 for the top 3 winners. Certificates for all participants who qualify for Round 2.

details_text: About LightHouse: LightHouse is an international, online hackathon for builders of agentic AI. Team size: 2 to 5 members. Inter-college and inter-specialization teams are allowed. Each participant can be part of only one team. Basic knowledge of programming and AI/LLM concepts is recommended. title: Manager of the Year
description: Description- Every brand eventually faces a moment when its old story stops working. A product loses relevance, a name picks up the wrong meaning, or a competitor changes what customers expect. The marketers who stand…
details_text: Description- Every brand eventually faces a moment when its old story stops working. A product loses relevance, a name picks up the wrong meaning, or a competitor changes what customers expect. The marketers who stand out in these moments are the ones who can find the real problem quickly and build a plan that holds up in the market. Manager of the Year, the management competition of Passion’26 at IMT Ghaziabad, puts teams in that position. Teams begin with a quiz on marketing fundamentals, move on to a case built around a real brand problem, and finish by presenting their recommendation to a panel of industry leaders. The competition rewards sound diagnosis, evidence and practical thinking over decoration. Round Structure- Online Quiz - Format: Online quiz hosted on Unstop with 30 multiple-choice questions to be completed in 15 minutes. Marking Scheme: Each correct answer carries 1 marks, each incorrect answer carries no negative marks, and unanswered questions carry no marks. Evaluation: About 35 participants will qualify for the on-campus rounds based on their quiz score. In case of a tie, the participant with fewer incorrect answers will rank higher. If the tie remains, the participant who took less time to complete the quiz will rank higher. Strategy Board Review- Format: On-campus round in groups of 5, with a case pack and a 3-minute individual recommendation to an investment committee. Objective: Each participant acts as a strategy head and recommends whether to acquire, merge, divest or grow organically. Evaluation: Individual scores on valuation logic, fit assessment, quality of challenge and clarity, normalised across rooms. The top 10 advance. The Deal Room- Format: On-campus negotiation between 5 pairs of participants, each pair negotiating the same case from opposite sides. Objective: Participants must reach an agreement, or walk away, using a confidential brief. Evaluation: Deal outcome (40), value creation (20), process (30) and ethics and honesty (10). The top 5 advance. Crisis Leadership Briefing- Format: On-campus finale for 5 finalists, with a 2-minute opening statement and a 5-minute media panel Q&A. Objective: Finalists lead the company response to a realistic crisis. Evaluation: Messaging, transparency, composure and damage control. The finalist with the highest score will be declared the winner. Note: Teams are not allowed to mention the name of their institution, or use its logo, anywhere in their submissions or during the presentation. General Rules & Regulations: All rounds will be held online. Multiple registrations by the same participant will lead to disqualification. In case of any dispute, the decision of judges and the organizing committee at IMT Ghaziabad will be final.

title: Finnacle : Read Past The Hype

details_text: Description- An Initial Public Offering (IPO) is more than a single-day fundraising event. It is a process through which a privately held company transitions into public ownership, with its valuation and investor expectations evolving across several stages. The analysts who stand out are the ones who follow the whole journey, from the last private funding round to the first quarterly results after listing. Finnacle, the finance competition of Passion’26 at IMT Ghaziabad, puts teams in that position. Teams begin with a quiz on IPOs and equity markets, move on to Listing Lens, where each team is assigned a recently listed Indian company and they have to trace its IPO journey. Round Details- Allotment Quiz- Format: Online quiz of 20 multiple-choice questions to be completed in 10 minutes. Only the team leader can attempt the quiz. Objective: The quiz assesses the IPO ecosystem, equity markets and the fundamentals of valuation. Marking Scheme: Each correct answer carries 1 mark and each incorrect answer carries no negative marks. Evaluation: Teams will be shortlisted on their quiz score. In case of a tie, the team that took lesser time will be ranked higher. Listing Lens- Format: Presentation (PPTX/PDF) and Excel workbook (XLSX) submitted by the Team Leader on Unstop. Shortlisted teams present for 10 minutes, followed by 5–7 minutes of Q&A. Objective: Qualifying teams will receive a case study centred on a recently listed Indian company. This round tests participants’ ability to analyse the company’s IPO journey across multiple stages, assess its valuation and market performance, and develop an evidence-backed investment recommendation. Task: The presentation should have up to 5-8 content slides, including the title and appendix slides. The first content slide must be an executive summary. Evaluation: Submissions will be judged on the depth of the problem diagnosis, the strength of the analysis and evidence, the clarity of the recommendation and the feasibility of its implementation. Original insight will be given credit. Final Bell- Format: Shortlisted teams present their recommendation in online mode to a panel of senior industry leaders. Objective: Participants must defend their recommendation under questioning. Task: Shortlisted teams from Round 2 will deliver a case presentation to a panel of industry experts, followed by a Q&A in which the judges will test their assumptions, analysis, and proposed solutions. Evaluation: Teams will be judged on how they handle questions, their commercial judgement, the clarity of their narrative, their command of the case and its numbers, and their delivery. The team with the highest average score from the panel will be declared the winner. Note: Teams are not allowed to mention the name of their institution, or use its logo, anywhere in their submissions or during the presentation. General Rules & Regulations: All rounds will be held online. Multiple registrations by the same participant will lead to disqualification. In case of any dispute, the decision of judges and the organizing committee at IMT Ghaziabad will be final.

title: Recast: Rewriting Brand Narratives
description: Description- Some products do not fail because they stop working. They fade because people stop seeing a reason to care about them. Bringing such a product back takes more than attention. It needs a clear idea of who…
details_text: Description- Some products do not fail because they stop working. They fade because people stop seeing a reason to care about them. Bringing such a product back takes more than attention. It needs a clear idea of who the product is for, why it matters to them and how the brand can earn their trust. Branding, the brand strategy competition of Passion’26 at IMT Ghaziabad, asks teams to take on that challenge. Teams begin with a quiz on branding and marketing fundamentals, move on to a case in which they must relaunch a forgotten product through an unlikely personality partnership, and finish by presenting their campaign to a panel of industry leaders. The competition rewards clear positioning, sound judgement and ideas that can work in the market. Rounds Structure- The Brand Sprint- Format: Online quiz hosted on Unstop with 15 multiple-choice questions to be completed in 10 minutes. Only the team leader will be allowed to take the quiz. Objective: The quiz will assess participants’ knowledge of branding, advertising, consumer behaviour and positioning, and their ability to apply these ideas to real brand situations. This round serves as the preliminary filter. Marking Scheme: Each correct answer carries 1 marks. There is no negative marking, and unanswered questions carry no marks. Evaluation: The teams will be shortlisted by score to qualify for the next round. In case of a tie, the team that took less time to complete the quiz will rank higher. The Unlikely Alliance- Format: Online case deck submission (PPTX/PDF). Objective: Teams that qualify will receive a case on relaunching a forgotten product for India’s Gen Z audience through a personality partnership, and must submit a brand identity and integrated campaign that is credible, memorable and commercially viable. Task: The presentation should have 5-8 slides, including the title and appendix slides. The first content slide must be an executive summary, and the deck must include a justification of up to 150 words for the chosen pairing. Evaluation: Submissions will be judged on the clarity of the brand positioning, the strength of the personality and brand fit, the relevance of the brand identity and campaign idea, and the feasibility of the budget and distribution plan. Original ideas will be given credit when they suit the audience. The Pitch Room- Format: Shortlisted teams present their campaign live in online mode to a panel of senior industry leaders. Objective: Participants must defend their campaign under questioning. Task: Shortlisted teams from Round 2 will deliver a case presentation, followed by a Q&A in which the judges will test their assumptions, budget and proposed campaign. Evaluation: Teams will be judged on how they handle questions, their commercial judgement, the clarity of their narrative, their command of the brand and its numbers, and their delivery. The team with the highest average score from the panel will be declared the winner. Note: Teams are not allowed to mention the name of their institution, or use its logo, anywhere in their submissions or during the presentation. General Rules & Regulations: All rounds will be held online. Multiple registrations by the same participant will lead to disqualification. In case of any dispute, the decision of judges and the organizing committee at IMT Ghaziabad will be final.

title: Vantage: Transforming Vision Into Enterprise

details_text: Description- Most new ventures do not struggle for lack of a good product. They struggle because customers do not see its value, the numbers do not add up, or growth moves faster than the team can manage. The founders who succeed are the ones who spot these problems early and make clear choices with limited money and time. Entrepreneurship, the venture competition of Passion’26 at IMT Ghaziabad, asks teams to think like founders. Teams begin with a quiz on entrepreneurship and business fundamentals, move on to a case built around a growing social enterprise, and finish by presenting their plan to a panel of judges acting as the venture’s board. Objective: The quiz will assess participants’ knowledge of entrepreneurship and business fundamentals, including business models, startup funding, unit economics and growth. This round serves as the preliminary filter. Marking Scheme: Each correct answer carries 1 marks. There is no negative marking, and unanswered questions carry no marks. Evaluation: The teams will be shortlisted by score to qualify for the next round. In case of a tie, the team that took less time to complete the quiz will rank higher. The Blueprint- Format: Online case solution submission (PDF/PPTX). Objective: Teams that qualify will receive a case study on a growing social enterprise and must submit a practical, evidence-backed plan covering perception, sales, growth and funding. Task: The presentation should have 5-8 slides, including the title and appendix slides. The first content slide must be an executive summary. Evaluation: Submissions will be judged on the depth of the problem diagnosis, the strength of the analysis and financials, the clarity of the plan and the feasibility of its implementation. Original insight will be given credit. The Boardroom- Format: Shortlisted teams present their plan in online mode to a panel of judges acting as the venture’s board. Objective: Participants must defend their plan under questioning. Task: Shortlisted teams from Round 2 will deliver a case presentation, followed by a Q&A in which the judges will test their assumptions, numbers and proposed solutions. Evaluation: Teams will be judged on how they handle questions, their business judgement, the clarity of their narrative, their command of the case and its numbers, and their delivery. The team with the highest average score from the panel will be declared the winner. Note: Teams are not allowed to mention the name of their institution, or use its logo, anywhere in their submissions or during the presentation. details_text: Overview PromptEd 2026 is an international competition on generative AI in business and management education. The Centre for Software and Information Technology Management (CSITM), IIM Bangalore, is running it in collaboration with Memoric AI. Students, faculty members, postdoctoral researchers and industry professionals are invited to use generative AI creatively to build original teaching artefacts that make business and management education more engaging and interactive. Shortlisted participants will show their work at IIM Bangalore. Winners will be announced and prizes given out during Teaching the Tech Generation: Rethinking Teaching and Learning in the Age of Technology, a two-day event organised by CSITM on 27–28 January 2027. What if the next great business classroom experience were built by you, with AI? The Challenge Use Gen-AI to build an original teaching artefact for business or management education. It could be: An educational game or simulation An interactive learning experience A teaching tool or web application Any other creative learning resource Tracks and Eligibility Student Track: students in business, management or related disciplines Professional Track: faculty members, postdoctoral researchers and industry professionals Enter on your own or in a team of up to 3 members Teams must consist of students from the same institution. Inter-college or mixed-institution teams are not permitted. Each participant can be part of one or a maximum of two teams. Mixing student and professional members within the same team is not permitted. Competition Structure Round 1: Online Submission Each participant or team submits a teaching artefact built with generative AI, with a teaching artefact, short demo video, a concept note, a teaching note and a prompt log. Entries are judged on the evaluation criteria below, and the top entries in each track go through to the finale. Upload the artefact file, such as a video or slide deck. For a web app, game or simulation, share the link and upload the source files in a ZIP folder. Demo Video (up to three minutes): A short video demonstrating how the artefact works. If the artefact itself is a video, a separate demo is not required. Concept Note (PDF, up to two pages): Describe the problem addressed, target learners, idea behind the artefact, AI tools used, how the artefact was developed, and any feedback received from users who tested it. Teaching Note (PDF, up to two pages): Include the learning objectives, instructions for using the artefact in a classroom session, suggested discussion questions, and its limitations. Prompt Log (Word document): Include the key prompts used, the models used, and how the outputs were refined. Evaluation Criteria Pedagogical Value and Learning Objectives Originality and Creativity Effective and Thoughtful Use of Gen-AI Classroom Usability and Feasibility Quality of Documentation (Concept Note, Teaching Note, Prompt Log) Presentation and Demo Registration Process Register for PromptEd 2026 through Unstop. title: Operationale : Delivering Calm In Chaos
description: Description- Every supply chain eventually meets the week it was not built for. A promotion lifts demand, a supplier under-delivers, the rain arrives and a freezer fails. The operations managers who stand out in these…
details_text: Description- Every supply chain eventually meets the week it was not built for. A promotion lifts demand, a supplier under-delivers, the rain arrives and a freezer fails. The operations managers who stand out in these moments are the ones who can separate the symptom from the cause and fix it within the limits they have been given. Operationale, the operations competition of Passion’26 at IMT Ghaziabad, puts teams in that position. Teams begin with a quiz on operations fundamentals, move on to a case built around a quick-commerce supply chain under pressure, and finish by turning their solution into a decision-ready deck. The competition rewards sound diagnosis, clear numbers and practical thinking over decoration. Rounds Structure- Stock Check- Format: Online quiz of 15 multiple-choice questions to be completed in 10 minutes. Only the team leader can attempt the quiz. Objective: The quiz assesses demand forecasting, inventory control, fulfilment metrics, warehousing and cold chain, and supplier reliability. Marking Scheme: Each correct answer scores 1 mark and each incorrect answer carries no negative marks. Evaluation: Teams will be shortlisted on their quiz score. In case of a tie, the team that took lesser time will be ranked higher. The COO’s Desk- Format: One-page PDF of up to 400 words, submitted by the Team Leader, with calculations in an XLSX file. Objective: Teams diagnose a live operations problem, separate symptoms from root causes, weigh options against hard limits and propose a fix the company can afford. Task: Identify every problem in the case, give the reasoning and a solution with rationale for each, and show the calculations. Evaluation: Submissions will be evaluated on how thoroughly teams identify problems and separate root causes from symptoms, the feasibility and affordability of their proposed solutions, the accuracy of their supporting calculations, and the clarity and conciseness of the write-up. Control Tower- Format: Pitch deck submitted on Unstop (PDF/PPTX). Objective: Teams turn their caselet solution into a clear, decision-ready deck in which the diagnosis, the fix and the trade-offs are visible on screen. Task: 5 to 8 content slides, excluding the Introduction and Thank You slides, covering every problem, its solution, the calculations and a source citation for any outside information. Evaluation: Decks will be evaluated on how thoroughly they diagnose the problems in the case, the practicality of the solutions and how clearly their trade-offs are shown, the accuracy of the supporting calculations, and the clarity and decision-readiness of the deck, including adherence to the slide limit and proper citation of sources. Note: Teams are not allowed to mention the name of their institution, or use its logo, anywhere in their submissions or during the presentation. General Rules & Regulations: All rounds will be held online. Multiple registrations by the same participant will lead to disqualification. In case of any dispute, the decision of judges and the organizing committee at IMT Ghaziabad will be final.

title: WealthWise : Let Goals Guide Growth

details_text: Description- Most people do not need more investment products. details_text: Overview Welcome to VIVAAD, the ultimate battleground of ideas, arguments, and perspectives, organised as part of Avartan 2026 at IIM Mumbai. VIVAAD is designed to challenge participants to think critically, question assumptions, construct compelling arguments, and defend their perspectives with confidence. Whether it is presenting a convincing argument or countering an opposing viewpoint, this competition will put participants’ debating and analytical abilities to the test. The competition will unfold across two rounds, beginning with an unconventional intra-team debate and culminating in an offline debate showdown at the IIM Mumbai campus. Competition Structure Round 1: Intra-Team Debate - Video Submission Each team must consist of exactly 2 members. One member will argue in favour of the given topic (Proposition), while the other will argue against the topic (Opposition). The debate topic will be revealed during Round 1 itself. Each team must submit a 3-minute video featuring the debate between the two members. Both members must actively participate, presenting their arguments, critical thinking and communication skills. Based on the evaluation of video submissions, selected teams will qualify for the final round Round 2: The Grand Finale - Offline Debate Shortlisted teams will be invited to the IIM Mumbai campus. The final round will be conducted in an offline debate format. Teams will compete against each other in a live debating environment. Further details regarding the debate topics, format, and speaking sequence will be communicated to the shortlisted teams. This round will test participants’ ability to think on their feet, build logical arguments, counter opposing viewpoints, and persuade the audience and judges.

details_text: Overview 48 HOURS. ONE UNKNOWN BRAND. MAKE BENGALURU NOTICE. Think you've got what it takes to make a local business famous? Compete for officially announced rewards. Get a chance to see your creative on a real advertising screen. Teams retain ownership of their submissions. OORO will seek separate permission for promotional reuse and screen publication. Your creativity. A real business. An entire city waiting to discover it. Presented by OORO. Final rules, eligibility, prizes, dates, social account handles, and participation terms will be published before registrations open.
