title: The Mandate Redline: Live Global Policy Drafting Lab (Co-Author a Published Policy Brief)
description: Overview No suits. No passive lectures. Just real-time policy drafting under live crisis pressure. The Mandate Redline is a first-of-its-kind Adversarial Policy Drafting & Consultation Lab hosted by Global Youth…
details_text: Overview No suits. No passive lectures. Just real-time policy drafting under live crisis pressure. The Mandate Redline is a first-of-its-kind Adversarial Policy Drafting & Consultation Lab hosted by Global Youth Mandate—a youth-led global policy organization with 500+ members across borders. Instead of repeating generic speeches that vanish after a conference ends, participants act as Policy Architects and Adversaries tasked with tearing apart, amending, and rewriting a flawed global policy bill on Artificial Intelligence, Digital Governance, and Youth Labor Rights. Why Participate? Get Published as a Co-Author: Every participant who completes the lab is officially credited as a Contributing Policy Fellow in the final published policy brief released by the Global Youth Mandate Research & Publication Division. Live Stress-Testing: Defend your clauses against sudden "Black Swan" crisis injections and live critiques from real policy and legal practitioners. Portfolio & CV Gold: Walk away with a verifiable publication link on globalyouthmandate.org, a Co-Author Press Kit for LinkedIn, and a Certificate of Policy Authorship. Competition Format & Process Stage 1: The Broken Draft Release (48 Hours Prior) All registered participants receive an intentionally flawed, realistic policy bill (The 2027 Global AI & Youth Workforce Protection Protocol) along with faction assignments (Tech Regulators, Youth Rights Advocates, Corporate Counsel, Developing Economies). Stage 2: Round 1 — The Live Redline Teardown (90 Minutes) Working in live collaborative documents, participants submit line-by-line "Redline Amendments" to expose loopholes, fix weak clauses, and negotiate consensus across opposing factions. Stage 3: Round 2 — Black Swan Crisis Injections (60 Minutes) Mid-session, the Secretariat drops real-time geopolitical and technological shockwaves, forcing teams to rewrite surviving clauses before the clock runs out. Stage 4: The Expert Stress-Test & Publication (45 Minutes + Post-Event) Top drafted clauses are grilled live by our guest policy/legal panel. Within 72 hours, surviving clauses are compiled into an official Global Youth Mandate Policy Brief published on our website. Rules & Guidelines Participation: Open to individual delegates (you will be placed into balanced policy factions) or teams of up to 10. Originality: All live amendments and policy justifications must be drafted originally during the live rounds. Conduct: Debate the clause, never the person. Diplomatic, evidence-backed reasoning scores highest on the live Policy Viability Scoreboard. Eligibility Open to School Students, Undergraduate & Postgraduate College Students, Freshers, and Young Professionals from any academic background (Law, Policy, Engineering, Economics, Humanities, Business). No prior MUN or policy experience is required.

title: Rabinjathon: Prime 1
description: Overview RABINJATHON is a student-led, online-first innovation and project-building event organized by RABINJA SQUAD. The event is designed for participants who want to take an idea beyond a presentation — develop a…
details_text: Overview RABINJATHON is a student-led, online-first innovation and project-building event organized by RABINJA SQUAD. The event is designed for participants who want to take an idea beyond a presentation — develop a concept, build a working prototype or demonstrable solution, explain how it works, and present it before a panel of judges. The event will begin in an online format. Depending on the event schedule and feasibility, selected/final-stage activities may be conducted in a hybrid format. Any confirmed hybrid requirements, venue details, or physical participation information will be communicated to eligible participants in advance. Event Approach Participants are expected to develop their own original idea, product, prototype, or solution. There is no single fixed problem statement that every team must solve. Participants may work across different areas such as software, web development, hardware, robotics, open innovation, and other technology-oriented concepts. The focus is on creativity, development, demonstration, communication, and practical thinking. Participants are encouraged to build and demonstrate a functional prototype wherever reasonably possible. Teams should be able to explain what their solution does, how it works, and what problem it is intended to address. Eligibility & Team Format Participation is open to students and eligible learners as specified in the registration requirements. Solo participation is allowed. Teams may consist of 1–4 participants. Inter-college teams are allowed. Participants from different academic specializations/branches may form a team. Team members do not need to belong to the same college, course, or specialization. Each participant should provide accurate information during registration. Participants may be required to provide additional details or proof of eligibility if requested by the organizers. A team can therefore be formed around the idea and skills required for the project rather than being restricted to one institution or specialization. Event Format RABINJATHON: PRIME 1 will progress through multiple stages. The rounds are designed to evaluate not only the idea itself, but also how participants develop, demonstrate, communicate, and defend their solution. Round 1 — Product Introduction / Ad-Style Video Participants will create a short video of approximately 2 minutes introducing their product, project, or solution. The video should be presented in an engaging, attention-grabbing format similar to a professional product advertisement or launch introduction. The video should communicate: Product/project name Product logo or visual identity, where applicable The problem or need being addressed A concise introduction to the solution Key value or purpose of the product Why someone would be interested in the solution An engaging introduction that captures the viewer's attention Participants may use creative storytelling, demonstrations, visuals, mock advertisements, animations, or other suitable presentation techniques. Where a participant uses an officially sponsored/partnered product, service, API, platform, or tool, the relevant sponsor/partner branding may be required to be displayed or acknowledged according to the applicable usage guidelines and permissions. Participants must not imply sponsorship, endorsement, partnership, or affiliation with any company unless such relationship has been officially confirmed and authorized. Detailed Round 1 submission instructions, technical requirements, submission procedure, deadlines, and any applicable branding requirements will be shared with registered participants approximately one week before the round. Round 2 — Project Showcase / Working Explainer Participants progressing to Round 2 will create a video of up to 5 minutes explaining their project in greater depth. This round is intended to demonstrate that the concept is not only an idea, but something that has been developed, prototyped, tested, or otherwise demonstrated

title: Chanakyaneeti 2027 - The Consulting Event
description: CHANAKYANEETI 2027 – The Consulting Challenge In a business environment shaped by changing markets, competitive pressures and complex decisions, the ability to think strategically and solve problems is more valuable…
details_text: CHANAKYANEETI 2027 – The Consulting Challenge In a business environment shaped by changing markets, competitive pressures and complex decisions, the ability to think strategically and solve problems is more valuable than ever. Shaastra 2027, IIT Madras, presents Chanakyaneeti, a consulting and business strategy competition that brings together aspiring consultants, strategists and problem-solvers from across the country. The competition aims to test participants' business acumen, analytical abilities and strategic thinking through a series of business-oriented challenges. Participants will be encouraged to look beyond conventional solutions, interpret information critically and develop practical recommendations to address real-world business problems. Competition Format: The competition will be conducted in three rounds: Round 1 – Business Aptitude Quiz (Online): The opening round will be an online quiz comprising 50 multiple-choice questions covering business awareness, quantitative aptitude, analytical reasoning, finance, marketing, strategy and consulting fundamentals. Teams will be shortlisted based on their performance. Round 2 – Case Study Submission (Online): Shortlisted teams will be presented with a business case requiring them to identify key challenges, analyse the available information and propose suitable recommendations. Teams will submit their solutions in the prescribed format, with the strongest submissions advancing to the final round. Round 3 – The Consulting War Room (On-campus Final): The final round will be an on-campus consulting challenge at IIT Madras. Qualifying teams will be presented with a business problem and will be expected to analyse the situation, develop strategic recommendations and present their approach before a panel of judges. The round will test participants' ability to think critically, make informed decisions and adapt their strategies when faced with changing business circumstances. Eligibility and Team Guidelines: Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from recognised colleges and universities across India. Students from all academic streams and specialisations are eligible. Teams must consist of 2–4 members. All members of a team must belong to the same institute. Inter-specialisation teams within the same institute are permitted. A student may register as part of only one team. Each team may submit only one entry for the competition. General Guidelines: Participants must register with accurate details and ensure that all team members meet the eligibility requirements. All submissions must be original and prepared by the registered team members. Participants are expected to maintain professional conduct throughout the competition. Further instructions, submission requirements and round-specific guidelines will be communicated to shortlisted teams by the organising committee. The final round will be conducted on campus at IIT Madras. Finalists will be required to obtain a valid Shaastra pass through the official Shaastra website. The organising committee reserves the right to make necessary changes to the competition schedule or format. Decisions of the organising committee and judges will be final. Think strategically. Analyse critically. Make your strategy count. Are you ready to take on Chanakyaneeti 2027?

details_text: Opportunity Details – Shaastra Ideathon: Operation Resilience – The Supply Chain Control Tower Competition Overview: Shaastra Ideathon is a three-round operations and supply chain case competition based on a real-world business scenario in the consumer electronics manufacturing industry. Participants will take on the role of a Supply Chain Advisory Team for Vistara Climate Systems Pvt. Ltd., a fictional Indian manufacturer facing supply chain disruptions due to delayed imports, rising demand, currency depreciation and limited domestic supplier capacity. The objective is to develop a practical, commercially viable strategy that ensures customer fulfilment while controlling procurement, inventory and logistics costs. Competition Structure: Round 1 – Unstop Q&A Participants will answer questions related to supply chain management. The round will test fundamental knowledge and understanding of supply chain concepts. Detailed question count, duration and evaluation criteria will be communicated by the organizers. Round 2 – Executive Summary Challenge Problem Statement: The Supply Chain Under Pressure. Teams must analyze the given business case and develop a practical response for managing the company's supply chain disruption over the next 30 days. Participants must address three key questions: What should the company do immediately? Recommend procurement, inventory and production decisions. How should scarce products be allocated across the three regions? Why is the proposed solution commercially sound? Explain the cost-service trade-off and profitability implications. Submission Format: PDF. Length: Maximum 2 A4 pages. Presentation: Not required. Recommended Team Size: 2–4 members. Evaluation Criteria: Practicality of proposed solution – 35% Quality of reasoning and trade-offs – 30% Understanding of operational constraints – 20% Clarity of executive summary – 15% Round 3 – Final Case Presentation Shortlisted teams will present their complete solution to a panel of industry experts. The presentation must cover five key deliverables: Recommended Strategy. Operational Action Plan. Business and Financial Impact. Risk Mitigation and Contingency. Implementation Roadmap and KPIs. Format: PPT presentation followed by panel Q&A. Presentation Duration: 10 minutes. Q&A Duration: 5 minutes. Suggested PPT Length: 5–7 substantive slides, excluding the title slide. All calculations and assumptions must be clearly explained. All teams must use the same case data and constraints provided by the organizers. Evaluation Criteria: Quality of strategy and decision-making – 25% Operational feasibility – 25% Financial reasoning – 20% Risk management – 15% Presentation and panel defence – 15% Eligibility and Team Guidelines: Recommended team size: 2–4 members. Inter-college team participation: Not specified in the competition document; subject to organizer approval. Inter-specialization team participation: Not specified in the competition document; subject to organizer approval. Detailed eligibility requirements will be communicated by the organizing team. Competition Rules: Teams must adhere to the case information, assumptions and operational constraints provided by the organizers. Recommendations must be practical, feasible and commercially justified. Teams must consider the company's production capacity, supplier constraints, inventory availability and customer service commitments. Round 2 submissions must not exceed two A4 pages and must be submitted in PDF format. Only shortlisted teams will proceed to the final presentation round. Final presentations must be followed by a panel Q&A session. All financial calculations, assumptions and proposed operational decisions must be clearly explained. The winning team will be selected based on the practicality and economic justification of its solution, rather than simply minimizing costs or maximizing service levels. details_text: HackKumbh 2026 | Honouring a Legacy, Innovating the Future Theme — Tech for Humanity: Innovating for Health, Education and Rural Empowerment What would you build to make healthcare easier to access, help students learn with limited connectivity, or solve a problem facing a rural community? HackKumbh 2026 is a national-level hackathon organised by Yeshwantrao Chavan College of Engineering (YCCE), Nagpur. Held in memory of Late Shri Datta Meghe Ji, it invites college students from across India to turn ideas for health, education and rural empowerment into working prototypes. Use AI, IoT, data analytics, robotics or digital platforms where they fit. Start with a specific problem and the people who face it. Then show how your solution could work in practice and be affordable and accessible to the people it serves. Who can participate? Open to college students across India Teams of 2–5 members Round 1 Problem Statements Choose one of the 15 problem statements for your PPT submission. Healthcare — Clinic appointments and queues, personal medical records and prescriptions, medicine and diagnostic price comparison, medication reminders and dose tracking, or multilingual health awareness and symptom guidance. Education — Internship matching and progress tracking, offline learning, peer learning and doubt resolution, an AI tutor based on teacher-approved material, or multilingual learning support. Social Issues — Urban sanitation and waste reporting, rural and semi-urban skills and job matching, digital literacy and fraud awareness for senior citizens, water scarcity and groundwater monitoring, or help finding and applying for government welfare schemes. Download the PPT Round Problem Statements PDF attached below for the full briefs, core features, expected prototypes and PPT guidelines. Read your chosen brief before preparing your submission. Stages and format Stage 1 — Online Idea Submission on Unstop Submit a presentation outlining the problem, who it affects, your proposed solution, how you plan to build it and its expected impact. Submissions will be reviewed for the problem addressed, the proposed solution, technical approach, feasibility and expected impact. The top 50 teams will advance to the on-campus finale. Stage 2 — 24-Hour On-Campus Build Shortlisted teams will develop a working prototype at YCCE, Nagpur. Teams will receive feedback during mentoring and review sessions and use it to refine their prototypes before the final submission. Stage 3 — Live Demo and Final Presentation Present your prototype to the jury. Show what it does, explain how it addresses the problem and describe what it would take to put it into use. Proposed prizes and recognition Winner — ₹1,00,000 First runner-up — ₹75,000 Second runner-up — ₹50,000 Total cash prize pool — ₹2,25,000 Five teams may receive special mentions, and two promising startup ideas may be considered for incubation or mentoring. Event details Proposed finale dates — 18–19 December 2026 Venue — Yeshwantrao Chavan College of Engineering (YCCE), Nagpur Proposed finale fee — ₹2,000 per shortlisted team Form your team, pick a problem worth solving and submit your idea on Unstop.

details_text: Overview VerilogVerse is an exciting hardware description and embedded design competition organized as part of Shaastra Elecfest, the annual tech fest vertical of IIT Madras. Designed for undergraduate students across Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, and related disciplines, the event challenges participants to design, implement, test, and optimize real-world digital systems directly on FPGA hardware. Description: VerilogVerse is an embedded programming and hardware design competition conducted by Elecfest at Shaastra, IIT Madras. The competition evaluates participants' core competence in digital logic, hardware description languages, and efficient system implementation on FPGA development boards. Shortlisted participants advance from an online screening round to a high-intensity offline hardware implementation challenge. Get certified by an ISO 9001:2015-certified organization and showcase your RTL design skills at one of India's premier technical festivals. Event Structure: The competition comprises two rounds: an online theoretical and coding assessment followed by a hands-on offline FPGA design challenge. Round 1: A 90-minute online assessment comprising MCQs and numerical-answer questions, designed to evaluate participants' understanding of digital design and Verilog fundamentals. Round 2: A 3-hour offline hardware implementation round where shortlisted teams implement Verilog modules on FPGA development boards to solve complex problem statements. Solutions are evaluated on functional correctness, hardware area utilization, and speed optimization. Topics Covered: Verilog / SystemVerilog (HDL) Combinational and Sequential Logic Design Finite State Machines (FSMs) RTL Design & Architecture Static Timing Analysis FPGA Hardware Implementation & Area Optimization Note that the above list is not exhaustive. The list of topics is meant to give an idea of what to expect from the event and the areas it will focus on. Guidelines: Intercollegiate and interdisciplinary team members are permitted. Teams can consist of 1 or 2 participants for Round 1. A participant cannot be part of multiple teams. Individual participants who qualify from Round 1 are permitted to pair up with other qualified individuals before Round 2. Rules and Regulations: Participants must strictly adhere to all instructions provided by the event coordinators. A laptop is mandatory for both rounds and ensure a stable internet connection for Round 1. Calculators are permitted for both rounds. Tab switching, communication, or use of external assistance and AI tools will result in immediate disqualification Professional etiquette and proper communication protocols must be maintained at all times. In any situation involving disputes over solutions, submissions, or evaluations, the decision of the event coordinators shall be final. Participants are advised to regularly check the official Unstop page for schedules, updates, and announcements. Further instructions and logistical details will be communicated via dedicated participant groups established after registration.

description: Overview Optima, the Annual Economic Outlook of the Department of Economics at Daulat Ram College, University of Delhi, stands as a beacon of knowledge and inspiration in the realms of finance and economics. Renowned…
details_text: Overview Optima, the Annual Economic Outlook of the Department of Economics at Daulat Ram College, University of Delhi, stands as a beacon of knowledge and inspiration in the realms of finance and economics. Renowned for its impactful articles, research papers, newsletters, and the annual E-Magazine, Optima has consistently provided valuable insights to individuals passionate in domains. As we gear up for the upcoming edition, we invite students from across India to contribute their fresh perspectives, original ideas, and compelling narratives and get them published in our Annual Magazine. Theme for the 14th Edition: The Quantum Economy About the Theme: A note on intellectual honesty: Quantum economics is a young and contested idea. Our strongest version of the argument says digital economies are best modelled as quantum-like information systems, using quantum probability as a mathematical tool. Critics reasonably ask what the framework predicts that behavioural economics, network theory, or Bayesian models cannot. In this edition, we choose to believe & test it- For most of the last two centuries, economics has borrowed its imagination from classical physics. Markets were pictured as machines: stable, predictable, and tending toward equilibrium. Prices reflected intrinsic value and scarcity, agents acted independently with fixed preferences, and small changes in one place produced small, proportionate effects elsewhere. That picture served the industrial age well. It serves the twenty-first century far less well. Today’s markets are dominated by intangible assets such as data, software, and brands. Algorithms trade in microseconds, a handful of platforms shape whole industries, and value often comes from who is connected to whom rather than from what is produced. Quantum economics is a proposed paradigm for making sense of this world. It borrows the mathematical and conceptual language of quantum theory. To be clear, it does not claim that markets are made of subatomic particles. It proposes that digital economies share the features quantum theory was built to describe: irreducible uncertainty, context-dependence, deep interdependence, and outcomes that only become definite when something interacts with the system. We'd like to clarify that we are an independent body and open to all opinions as well as interpretations of our theme. Submission Guidelines: Submissions can be made in any one of the following forms: Research paper, research article, caricatures, policy analysis report, opinion piece, comparative essays, review article, or expository essay. All submissions should be made in Word Document format (.doc or .docx). The word limit of submissions is given as follows: Research Articles/Opinion Pieces: 1500-2000 words (excluding reference list, tables, and figures) Research Papers: 2500-3000 words Caricatures (a one-line caption would be recommended) All images used along with the plagiarism percentage report should also be shared in the same mail with titles as per the following convention: Organisation Name_Title of the Article_Name of the Author(s)_serial number of Image used. Authors must submit a 200-250 word abstract for their writing pieces by 3rd January 2027, and mail it (not required for caricatures). The Submission deadline for the Final Submission of write-ups is 17th January 2027. Kindly find the Detailed Guidelines and Suggested Topics attached below for your reference. Writing Guidelines: Font to be used is Times New Roman. Font size of the Heading is 12 and the Font size of the Body is 10. Alignment should be justified. details_text: Adaption Dataset Challenge Organised by Hackyard, in collaboration with Adaption. Fully online. What you will do Build an AI assistant for an underserved language or topic, starting with its data. Create or improve an instruction-tuning dataset with Adaption (Invent a Dataset and/or Adaptive Data) and evaluate it before and after to show how much it improved. Training a model with AutoScientist is optional. Start from a seed dataset you have the right to use and adapt. You pick the use case. Some ideas: A question-answering assistant for an underserved language. An assistant that explains a specialised topic or service in simple language. An assistant for a clearly defined group of users. How to join Register once, on Unstop or Hackyard. Do not register on both. Create your Adaption account at https://adaptionlabs.ai/app using the same email you registered with. You can do this right away. If you already have an Adaption account, keep using it. After creating your account, submit a screenshot of it through the Google Form. The form link will be shared with registered participants. Join the WhatsApp group for updates: https://chat.whatsapp.com/DyiXXOZ4ATJ7xVRUpxyKn8?s=cl&p=a&mlu=4&ilr=4 Attend the onboarding session with Adaption on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, at 7:30 PM IST (9:00 AM EST). It covers account setup, dataset preparation, Invent a Dataset, Adaptive Data and AutoScientist. The session is private. The recording will be shared with registered participants only. Start with the Adaption documentation: https://docs.adaptionlabs.ai/ What to submit Submit once, by December 6, 2026, 11:59 PM IST, on one platform only: here on Unstop, or on your team page in the Hackyard app at https://app.hackyard.org/e/adaption-labs . Share one link that includes: Your dataset created or improved on Adaption. Optional: details of a model you trained with AutoScientist, if you did. Your use case and who it is for. How you used Adaption. Your evaluation results. A README covering your approach, data source and licence, results, limitations and team members. A demo of the assistant. You keep ownership of what you build. Your submission is shared with Hackyard and Adaption for judging. Dataset rules Use instruction/response or chat-style data in a format Adaption supports. Use only data you have the right to use. Name the source and licence. No personal, confidential or unsafe content. Who can join Participants must be at least 18 years old. Open worldwide, subject to applicable laws and Adaption's platform terms. Solo or teams of up to four, as listed on Unstop. Judging Hackyard runs judging, and a judge from Adaption's team joins the final round. Projects are scored on: Dataset quality and fit for the use case. Measurable improvement in the dataset before and after. A clear problem, users and practical value. A clear write-up of your decisions, results and limits. Prizes 1st place: $100 cash for the team, two VIP swag boxes and an extra $1,000 in Adaption credits per member. 2nd and 3rd place: swag boxes and an extra $1,000 in Adaption credits per member. Certificates: certificates of submission for builders who submit a project, and winner certificates for the top 3 teams. Only projects that use Adaption are eligible for the cash prize. Credits have no cash value and cannot be transferred or sold. All amounts are in US dollars. Winners will be asked for their name, address and phone number to ship swag. details_text: All that you need to know about Agentic AI in BFSI: Hackathon 2026 by IIT Bombay Complete Regsiteration and Submission at: https://techfest.org/competitions/Agentic-AI It is mandatory to register on Techfest Website . further details will be updated on the Website only . About Agentic AI in BFSI: Hackathon 2026 is a national hackathon by Perfios, one of India's largest SaaS TechFin companies serving over 1,000 financial institutions globally, in association with Techfest, IIT Bombay. Under the theme AI Native Applications for BFSI, teams prototype AI-backed systems that can perceive, reason, decide and act across real-world financial workflows. Participants pick one of two banking domains, Debt Collections or Fraud Detection & Prevention, and its problem statement, and are judged on the rigor of their technical plan in Round 1 and on a working prototype at the finals at Techfest, IIT Bombay, Asia's largest science and technology festival. No prior BFSI experience is needed. Structure Eligibility: Open to all students with a valid ID from their educational institution. No prior BFSI experience is needed. Cross-institutional teams are encouraged. Team size: Maximum 4 members per team. The competition runs in two rounds, with Round 2 as an in-person prototype demo at Techfest, IIT Bombay. Domains & problems: Teams choose one domain and its problem statement. Theme 1, Debt Collections, has Problem 1: Paralinguistic State Detection from Voice, Not Transcript, where teams build an acoustic model that estimates borrower emotional state (arousal, valence, discrete states, commitment credibility) from speech alone, plus a decision layer that guarantees distressed borrowers are handed to a human and never pressured. Theme 2, Fraud Detection & Prevention, has Problem 2: Know Your Agent (KYA), where teams build a real-time system that detects whether a non-human agent is involved in a banking session, produces an explainable Agent Trust Score, and recommends allow, step-up authentication, hold, or block. Round 1 - Ideation Round (Online Abstract) Teams submit a 600-900 word abstract (plus an optional 1-page architecture diagram) covering the problem chosen, understanding of the challenge, proposed approach and agent architecture, how it maps to the Minimum Viable scope, stretch ambitions, expected impact, novelty, evaluation plan, responsible design (fairness, privacy, explainability, safety), and feasibility and risks. No code or prototype is required at this stage; only the Team Leader may submit, and multiple submissions are not accepted. Perfios evaluates submissions and shortlists the most promising ideas based on creativity, feasibility, and relevance. Round 2 - Prototype & Demo (Finals) Shortlisted teams build a working prototype covering the Minimum Viable scope of their problem (and any stretch goals attempted) and present it at IIT Bombay to a panel of Perfios judges. Each team gets 20 minutes for presentation and live demo, followed by 5 minutes of Q&A. Finalists submit a code repository with README, a technical report (max 6 pages), a results summary table against every success metric, and a demo video (max 3 minutes) as a backup. Winners are selected on innovation, technical depth, prototype quality, and real-world applicability. Timeline Submission link opens - 15th November 2026 Registration closes - 25th November 2026 Round 1 submission deadline - 30th November 2026 Shortlist announcement - 4th December 2026 Finals at IIT Bombay - 15th-18th December 2026 Rewards And Prizes INR 1,00,000 for the top 3 winners. Certificates for all participants who qualify for Round 2.

details_text: About the Hackathon - agentwarehack.com Agentware is a 72-hour online AI agent engineering hackathon built around one challenge: build an autonomous AI agent that can perform real work independently, operate reliably, and know when to stop. Everyone has a demo of an AI agent. Almost nobody has one they would leave running overnight. Agentware challenges participants to build agents that go beyond conversational interfaces and actually execute complete workflows using real tools, systems, and external inputs. The hackathon covers six tracks: Inbox & Calendar, Life Admin, Research & Study, Browser Agent, Developer Workflow, and an Open Track. Each track focuses on a different category of real-world automation, from managing emails and schedules to conducting research, navigating websites, reviewing code, and handling complex workflows. This is not a hackathon where you build a chatbot that simply responds to prompts. Your agent must take meaningful actions, complete tasks from trigger to result, and operate without continuous human intervention. Participants can use any AI model, framework, programming language, or development stack, including hosted APIs, local models, MCP, function calling, browser automation, shell commands, and custom tools. However, autonomy alone is not enough. Your agent must also demonstrate reliability, appropriate permissions, safety guardrails, monitoring, and a mechanism to stop execution when necessary. Participants can compete across six tracks, qualify for individual awards, and earn additional safety bonus points by implementing guardrails, live monitoring, a kill switch, and a complete audit trail. Build an agent you can walk away from. Stay Updated All event announcements, track specifications, rule clarifications, Trap Pack releases, scoring updates, judging information, submission instructions, FAQs, and participant support are provided through the official Hackathon Raptors community channels. Discord Server Invite: https://discord.gg/xfYPDZYqeh Why Participate Most AI hackathons focus on building applications that demonstrate what AI can do. Agentware takes a different approach: the challenge is to build autonomous systems that can perform real work reliably, handle unexpected situations, and operate safely without someone constantly monitoring them. Participants will get to: Build autonomous AI agents that perform real-world tasks instead of simply answering questions. Develop agents that interact with emails, calendars, documents, websites, APIs, and external systems. Implement multi-step workflows involving planning, tool calling, execution, and verification. Explore different approaches to agent architecture, orchestration, and tool integration. Build inbox and calendar automation systems that handle scheduling, replies, and follow-ups. Develop life administration agents for bills, renewals, paperwork, travel planning, and groceries. Create research agents that monitor publications, organize reference libraries, and track deadlines. Implement browser agents capable of navigating websites, extracting information, and filling forms. Build developer workflow agents for pull request reviews, failed-build diagnosis, and on-call assistance. Experiment with voice agents, back-office automation, and other applications through the Open Track. Implement safety mechanisms against prompt injection, conflicting instructions, and malicious inputs. Explore permission scoping, confirmation gates, audit logging, and real-time agent monitoring. Test autonomous systems against a dedicated Trap Pack containing hostile inputs and deliberately broken data. Compete against other builders using a common judging rubric focused on autonomy, usefulness, reliability, and engineering quality. Demonstrate practical AI engineering skills through working software and reproducible execution traces. AI coding assistants are allowed and expected, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and local models. AI-

details_text: OVERCLOCK 2027 | 24-Hour National-Level Hardware Hackathon BUILD. INNOVATE. ENGINEER THE FUTURE. OVERCLOCK 2027 is a 24-hour national-level hardware hackathon organized by the Department of Electrical Engineering, Fr. C. Rodrigues Institute of Technology (FCRIT), Vashi, Navi Mumbai , in association with IEEE FCRIT Student Branch (STB 61121), EESA and ISLE FCRIT . The hackathon challenges undergraduate students to identify real-world engineering problems and develop practical, innovative hardware solutions. From energy and industrial automation to healthcare and defence, turn your ideas into working physical prototypes. Important Dates 06 November 2026: Registrations Open 10 November 2026: Round 1 Problem Statements Released 15 December 2026: Round 1 Submission Deadline (11:59 PM IST) 22 December 2026: Shortlist Announcement (Top 30 Teams + 5 Waitlisted) 22 January 2027: Finale Problem Statements Released 29–30 January 2027: 24-Hour On-Campus Hackathon at FCRIT, Vashi, Navi Mumbai Hackathon Structure Round 1 – Online Proposal Screening 100% Free – No Registration Fee Register your team and select a problem statement. Submit your proposed solution using the official PPT template. Explain your problem understanding, proposed approach, hardware architecture, components and technical feasibility. No physical prototype is required during this round. All teams can participate in Round 1 without any payment. Round 2 – 24-Hour On-Campus Finale ₹1,500 + 18% GST = ₹1,770 PER TEAM The top 30 teams will qualify, with 5 additional teams on the waitlist. Only shortlisted teams will be required to pay the Round 2 participation fee. Finalists will receive fresh problem statements one week before the event. Teams will design, assemble, program and demonstrate a functional hardware prototype within 24 hours. All final assembly, soldering, wiring and firmware development must take place during the event. Completed prototypes and pre-assembled final circuits are not permitted. Payment Information: Round 2 participation fees will be collected separately through the official FCRIT institutional payment portal after shortlisting and confirmation. No payment is required through Unstop for Round 1 registration or submission. title: Robo Sumo
description: All that you need to know about Robo Sumo RoboSumo Competition – Rules & Guidelines Overview: RoboSumo is a robot combat competition where manually controlled robots compete to push their opponent out of the designated…
details_text: All that you need to know about Robo Sumo RoboSumo Competition – Rules & Guidelines Overview: RoboSumo is a robot combat competition where manually controlled robots compete to push their opponent out of the designated arena while defending themselves. The team with the most points wins. In case of a tie, a special round will determine the winner. Gameplay: Round Duration: Two halves, each lasting 2 minutes (subject to change). Starting Positions: Robots start outside the arena. Objective: Push the opponent's robot out of the ring to score points. Post-Point Resumption: After scoring, robots return to their starting positions. Out-of-Bounds: A robot is considered out if more than 50% of its body crosses the arena boundary Technical Timeout: Each team can claim one technical timeout per round (maximum 2 minutes). Can only be used if the robot is damaged during the match. Scoring: 1 Point: Awarded when a robot pushes the opponent out of the ring. Simultaneous Elimination: Both teams receive 1 point if both robots go out together. Early Game End: If a team reaches a 7-0 lead, the game ends immediately. Tie: A special sudden-death round determines the winner. Robot Specifications: Dimensions: Maximum Length: 350 mm Maximum Width: 350 mm Maximum Height: 300 mm Maximum Weight: 5 kg Control: Can be wired or wireless. If wired, the cable must be at least 2 meters long. Battery: Only up to 4S LiPo batteries are allowed. Higher voltage batteries are strictly prohibited. Arena Specifications: Arena Size: 3m x 3m Playable Area: A central 1.5m diameter ring. Starting Positions: Robots begin outside the ring. Technical Timeout: Each team gets one technical timeout per round (max 2 minutes). Only allowed if the robot suffers damage during the match. Rules & Regulations: Timely Arrival: Late teams may be eliminated. Team Size: Maximum 4 members per team. Robot Handler: Only one team member controls the robot; others must stay outside the game zone. Match Format: Knockout format. Misbehavior: Any misconduct may lead to disqualification. Interference: Damaging other robots or the arena results in immediate disqualification. Final Decision: Judges and organizers have final say on all matters. Disqualification: Deliberate damage to robots or the arena. Violation of robot specifications or gameplay rules. Judges' Authority: Judges have final authority over all game matters. Their decisions cannot be contested. Special Round (Tie-Breaker): If the match ends in a tie, a sudden death round will determine the winner. The exact rules will be announced on the event day. Conclusion: The team that scores the most points wins the match. If a team reaches a 7-0 lead, they win instantly. The competition will be conducted fairly and competitively, and all final decisions rest with the Organizing Committee

details_text: All that you need to know about Maze Runner Maze Runner Challenge – Rules & Guidelines: Overview: The Maze Runner Challenge is a technical competition where participants navigate a small car through a maze. Eligibility: Open to all students. Teams can have 2 members. Only registered teams are allowed to participate. Car Specifications: The car must fit within 20cm (L) x 20 cm (W) x 8 cm (H). The car must be battery-operated. Autonomous navigation is allowed. Manual cars are not allowed. No harmful components such as sharp edges, explosives, or hazardous materials are allowed. Maze Overview: The maze will contain obstacles and dead turns to challenge participants. The exact layout and specifications will be revealed on the event day. General Guidelines: Participants must follow event coordinators’ instructions. Any damage to the maze or unfair play will lead to disqualification. The decision of the judges is final. Rules: Team Composition: Each team will have two members. Attempts: Each team gets two attempts per round. In the first attempt, one participant will drive the car. In the second attempt, the other participant must drive. A single participant cannot drive in both attempts. Rounds & Qualification: First Round: The top 10 teams with the best completion times will qualify for the second round. Second Round: Additional obstacles will be introduced. Each team gets two attempts, one per participant. The top 5 teams will qualify for the final round. Final Round: The top 2 teams with the best times will be declared winners. Conditional Time Limit: If participation is higher than expected, a time limit will be set for each round and attempt to ensure smooth progression of the competition. Scoring & Penalties: Fastest completion time wins. Touching the car: +5 seconds. Resetting at checkpoint: +10 seconds. Hitting maze wall: +5 seconds. Judging Criteria: The time taken to complete the maze. The number of penalties incurred in case of a tie. Final decision will be made by the judge. Winner: Fastest completion time with minimum penalties. Best Innovation: Most creative car design (if participants bring their own car). Safety Precautions: Ensure that the car adheres to the given safety standards. Avoid high-speed collisions to prevent damage to the maze and other components. Participants bringing their own cars must ensure no harmful materials or components are used.

Developers, beginners, innovators, and technology enthusiasts are welcome. Participants can register individually or in teams. Team size: 1–3 members. Inter-college teams are allowed. requirements: Robots must meet official technical specifications and participants must follow all safety and competition rules.
details_text: Get ready to put your robotics skills, creativity, and problem-solving abilities to the test at Robo Hurdle Race, an exciting technical competition organized as part of KAUSHALYA 2.0, the annual fest of CSVTU University Teaching Department, Bhilai. Robo Hurdle is a robotics challenge in which participants compete by navigating their robots through a specially designed obstacle course. The competition tests robotic control, precision, coordination, and the ability to overcome physical obstacles. Event Details Date: 27 November 2026 Time: 12:00 PM – 3:00 PM Category: Robotics Competition Overview Participants will be required to navigate their robots through an obstacle-based track. Performance will be evaluated during the competition according to the event's official judging criteria. GENERAL PARTICIPATION RULES Registration & eligibility 1. Registration: Teams must register before the deadline announced by the organizers. 2. Team size: 1–3 participants for Robo Hurdle. 3. Identification: Participants must carry valid college or student ID and show it on request at check-in. Robots & equipment 1. Own equipment: Each team must bring its own robot, controller, batteries, charger, and essential tools and spares. 2. Originality: Robots must be team-built or team-integrated. Organizers may inspect the robot and ask the team to demonstrate or explain it. 3. Robot safety: No sharp edges, flames, explosives, corrosive substances, hazardous projectiles or exposed dangerous wiring. 4. Power switch: Every robot must have an easily reachable main power switch so a referee can shut it down quickly. 5. Batteries: Batteries must be securely mounted and insulated. Charging is allowed only in the area designated by organizers; Li-Po packs must not be left charging unattended. Conduct & decisions 1. Competition area: Only registered team members may handle or operate the robot in the designated competition area. 2. Fair play: Unauthorized assistance, interference, tampering, intentional damage or unsportsmanlike conduct may lead to penalties or disqualification. 3. Final decisions: Referee and technical committee decisions are final, subject to any appeal process announced by the organizers. 4. Instructions: Participants must follow the instructions provided by the event coordinators. 5. Reporting time: Teams must report to the venue at the designated time. EVENT RULES A. Participation & Robot Team size: 1–3 members (KAUSHALYA 2.0 reference). Eligible participants: Undergraduate, postgraduate and engineering students, subject to organizer confirmation. Power: Robot must be self-powered. No external pushing, lifting or physical guidance during a run. Control mode: Wired or wireless manual control. Wired tethers must not drag or lift the robot. Maximum size: 30 cm × 30 cm × 30 cm at start (may expand during a run). Maximum weight: 5 kg. Maximum voltage: 12 V nominal on the robot. Final specifications: 30 × 30 × 30 cm. B. Track & Run Procedure Teams report for inspection and check-in before their scheduled slot. The referee explains the route, start and finish lines, obstacles, checkpoints and penalty zones. The robot starts only after the official signal. The robot must complete the course in the prescribed sequence. Shortcuts or skipping mandatory obstacles are not allowed. The timer starts at the signal (or at start movement, as announced) and stops when the robot fully crosses the finish line. If the robot stalls or gets stuck, the team may request judge-authorized recovery. Recovery penalties and attempt limits apply as announced. The referee records track contact, obstacle displacement, boundary departure and course damage. C. Attempts & Ranking Match type: Timed solo run. Official runs: Up to 2 attempts per team. Practice: One practice run if the schedule permits. Time limit per run: 3 minutes. Ranking (winner decided by): Best valid run time after penalties. Course completion: Mandatory. Incomplete runs rank below valid finishers. Tie-break

details_text: Embarko Student Challenge: Deploy With Embarko Build a project with AI. Put it live on Embarko. Win 250 prizes. How It Works Step 1: Build a Project Ask any AI to build you something beautiful. Not sure what to build? Start with the ideas at embarko.ai/challenge , such as: A portfolio that looks like a retro video game Your college fest's website A notes library for your class A cricket stats page for your gully team Step 2: Deploy It Paste the Embarko prompt from embarko.ai into your AI. Your project goes live at yourname.embarko.app . Say yes when your AI offers to keep it, or it will be deleted after 24 hours. If you get stuck, read the guides at embarko.ai/guides . Everyone after them receives Embarko goodies, including backpacks, bottles, and T-shirts. See Rewards and Recognition for the full list. How To Register Step 1: Register on Unstop. Step 2: Register for the Embarko Student Challenge at embarko.ai/challenge using the same email address and phone number. Your registration is complete only after both steps. details_text: Overview CRUX – Consulting & Research Undertaking Club at XLRI is proud to present Orion 2026, the flagship case study competition of Synergy 2026, XLRI’s annual fest. Designed to challenge aspiring consultants and future business leaders, Orion provides a platform to apply strategic thinking, analytical rigor, and creative problem-solving to real-world business challenges. About Orion 2026 Orion 2026 invites participants to step into the shoes of consultants, dissect complex business problems, and develop innovative, data-driven, and actionable solutions. The competition aims to test participants’ ability to structure ambiguous problems, formulate strategic recommendations, and translate ideas into practical business plans that deliver measurable impact. Competition Structure The competition will follow a three-round format, progressively testing participants’ knowledge, analytical abilities, and communication skills. Round 1: Business Quiz Teams will compete in a quiz designed to test their business acumen, analytical thinking, and understanding of business concepts. title: Sora Everyday: The Next Growth Equation
description: About the Case: Sora Everyday is a fictional Indian personal care brand that has grown into a recognised digital challenger across hair care, body care and everyday skin care. The brand sells through its own website and…
details_text: About the Case: Sora Everyday is a fictional Indian personal care brand that has grown into a recognised digital challenger across hair care, body care and everyday skin care. The brand sells through its own website and app, online marketplaces, and a growing offline retail network. However, growth is becoming increasingly expensive. Customer acquisition costs are rising, repeat purchases are declining, and management is questioning whether reported advertising returns are actually generating incremental sales. With a ₹57 crore H2 FY27 revenue forecast against a ₹67 crore target , the leadership team must find ₹10 crore of additional revenue without increasing the ₹14 crore marketing budget , while simultaneously improving profitability. The board's mandate is clear: growth must translate into profitable, sustainable value. Problem Statement: Participants step into the role of an independent strategy team advising Sora Everyday's CEO and Board . They must build a six-month growth strategy that balances: Customer acquisition and retention Marketing efficiency and incrementality Channel mix across D2C, marketplaces and offline Contribution margin improvement Practical execution within existing resources The current H2 forecast is ₹57 crore , while the board requires ₹67 crore in revenue and at least 13% contribution margin , with marketing expenditure capped at ₹14 crore . Participants must address four key decisions: 1. Close the ₹10 Crore Revenue Gap Build a credible, quantified bridge from ₹57 crore to ₹67 crore without double-counting revenue or assuming all attributed sales are incremental. 2. Redesign the Marketing Mix Reallocate the ₹14 crore H2 marketing budget across acquisition, brand, marketplaces, CRM and agency/production costs. 3. Improve Customer Economics Design 2–3 specific interventions to improve repeat purchase, retention and first-order economics. 4. Build a Measurement Framework Define experiments, KPIs and a 90-day decision framework to determine what is genuinely working and where investment should be scaled or stopped. Key Business Challenges: Rising Acquisition Costs The illustrative D2C first order generates ₹820 contribution before marketing , against an average ₹1,180 acquisition cost , resulting in a ₹360 first-order loss after acquisition . Declining Repeat Purchase Second-purchase rates within 90 days have fallen from 27% to 20% across recent acquisition cohorts. Attribution vs. Incrementality Different marketing platforms use different attribution windows, meaning reported platform sales are not additive and cannot automatically be treated as incremental revenue . Limited Resources Sora has one CRM manager, two in-house creative resources and an existing agency roster. Large technology implementations cannot be completed within the six-month period. Flow of Events: Round 1: Quiz — Online Assessment Participants will begin with an online quiz testing their business acumen, strategic thinking and understanding of growth and profitability concepts . Round 2: Strategic Deck — Online Submission Shortlisted teams will develop and submit a strategy deck addressing Sora Everyday’s growth challenge, including the revenue bridge, marketing allocation, customer retention strategy and 90-day action plan. Round 3: Live Pitch — On Campus Finals The top teams will present their recommendations live on campus to a panel of judges, defending their strategy, assumptions, calculations and key trade-offs through an interactive boardroom-style pitch. Evaluation Criteria — 100 Marks: Commercial Strategy & Growth Plan — 35 Marks Credibility of the ₹57 Cr → ₹67 Cr revenue bridge Quality of growth levers Avoidance of double-counting Strategic channel prioritisation Unit Economics & Marketing Efficiency — 30 Marks Improvement in contribution margin Quality of ₹14 Cr marketing allocation Understanding of CAC and first-order economics Incrementality vs. platform attribution Customer Retention & Execution — 25 Marks Strength

title: Gambit 2035: The Great Power Game
description: How the Game Works Leverage Points (LP) Leverage Points are the primary in-game currency. Each nation begins with a different level of power and has a different maximum possible LP score. Final performance is therefore…
details_text: How the Game Works Leverage Points (LP) Leverage Points are the primary in-game currency. Each nation begins with a different level of power and has a different maximum possible LP score. Final performance is therefore measured relative to each nation's own maximum potential, keeping the competition balanced across nations. Secret Agendas Every nation receives a confidential objective that can earn bonus LP. Your Secret Agenda may force you to pursue an objective that conflicts with your nation's obvious interests, creating an additional layer of strategic decision-making. Treaty Registry If it isn't registered, it isn't real. Only agreements submitted through the official Treaty Registry are enforceable. Promises made in private chats are cheap talk unless backed by a registered agreement. PNN: PiE News Network The PNN will deliver breaking developments throughout the game. Expect market shocks, diplomatic leaks, surprise events, rival moves and changing conditions through Discord and Solaris Instagram Stories. Day 1 Scoring Game Performance: 50% Diplomatic Cable: 50% Advancement: The winner of each world + the 4 highest-scoring runners-up advance. 12 teams advance to Day 2. Day 2 Scoring Game Performance + Secret Agenda: 40% Crisis Report: 60% Top 3 teams from each world advance. 6 finalists reach Day 3. Day 3 Scoring 2035 Accord: 30% Summit Address: 40% Press Conference: 30% Participation Team Size: 2 to 3 members Maximum Teams: 48 The 48 teams will be divided into 8 worlds, with 6 nations in each world. If registrations exceed the cap, participants will be shortlisted through a 20-minute entry quiz covering game theory and geoeconomics. WHY PARTICIPATE? GAMBIT 2035 isn't a conventional case competition. You won't receive a case and simply present a solution. You will create the case yourself through your decisions. You will have to: Make decisions with incomplete information Negotiate with competing interests Build and break alliances Understand incentives React to unexpected shocks Quantify economic consequences Read your rivals Apply game theory in real time Defend your decisions under pressure In GAMBIT 2035, there is no fixed solution. There is only the move you make and the world it creates. Enter the game. Shape the world.

details_text: About the Opportunity Case Union 4.0 presents Vyapar Sahayak × Jagriti , a case focused on building a digital companion for India's smallest businesses, starting in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Despite widespread adoption of UPI and WhatsApp, many small businesses continue to rely on paper bahi-khata , family advice, and CAs to manage their businesses. Vyapar Sahayak is a pre-build concept bundling bookkeeping, inventory, business services and access to expertise — but the challenge is deciding what it should actually be on Day One, who it should serve, and how it can sustain itself. Case Union 4.0 - Vyapar Sahayak… Case Union 4.0 - Vyapar Sahayak… The Challenge Teams must build a plan that Jagriti could start testing within 60 days , answering: Which customer segment should Vyapar Sahayak target? How should Jagriti acquire and retain its first 500 users ? What is the low-cost validation test that determines whether to build or kill the idea? Case Union 4.0 - Vyapar Sahayak… Case Union 4.0 - Vyapar Sahayak… Deliverables Round 2 submissions should cover: Segment Choice Diagnosis Product Wedge Path to Full Product Business Model & Unit Economics Go-to-Market in Eastern UP Validation Plan Case Union 4.0 - Vyapar Sahayak… Flow of Events Round 1: Quiz — Online Assessment Timed, proctored online quiz covering MSMEs, UPI, GST, ledger apps, udhaar , bahi-khata , Jagriti and the case. Case Union 4.0 - Vyapar Sahayak… Round 3: Finale — On Campus / Live with Jagriti Finalists present to Jagriti's leadership team and defend their recommendations and build-or-kill test under questioning. Case Union 4.0 - Vyapar Sahayak… What We're Looking For Strong solutions will demonstrate: Sharp customer and segment understanding A focused product wedge , not an everything-on-day-one solution A viable business model with a real payer Practical GTM through Jagriti's existing ecosystem A credible, low-cost validation plan Clear thinking grounded in the realities of small businesses in Purvanchal Case Union 4.0 - Vyapar Sahayak… Prizes Winners: Two seats on the Jagriti Yatra — a 15-day, 8,000 km journey across India. details_text: Description: The Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur, renowned for its academic excellence, is set to host the 33rd edition of Techkriti, Asia’s largest technical and entrepreneurial festival, from January 28 to January 31, 2027. Techkriti'27 will bring together top talent from across the country to compete, collaborate, and innovate in technology and entrepreneurship. The festival’s competitions, divided into Technical, Entrepreneurial, and Miscellaneous categories, include events like Robogames, Takeoff, Software Corner, ECDC, Business Events, Trading, and MUN. These competitions aim to foster creativity and technical expertise among participants while providing a platform for real-world problem-solving and skill development. Techkriti also features workshops led by industry experts, covering topics such as AI, ML, Ethical Hacking, Stock Investment, and Prompt Engineering (ChatGPT). These sessions will help students stay updated on the latest advancements in technology and entrepreneurship. In addition, the festival will host talks by renowned speakers, including Nobel laureates and industry leaders, along with exhibitions showcasing cutting-edge innovations. For those seeking entertainment, Techkriti offers a variety of fun events, including escape rooms, VR experiences, PS gaming, stand-up comedy, EDM nights, and live concerts. About: The Lok Sabha or House of the People is the lower house of the Parliament of India. Members of the Lok Sabha are elected by direct election under universal adult franchise. As of 2024, there have been eighteen Lok Sabhas elected by the people of India. The Constitution limits the Lok Sabha to a maximum of 552 members. This includes up to 530 members representing states and up to 20 members from Union Territories. Each Lok Sabha is formed for a five-year term. Normally, after five years, it is automatically dissolved. It can be extended by a proclamation of emergency. If this happens, the term may be extended for one year. It can be extended more than one time. The 18th and current Lok Sabha was formed in May 2014.

title: Drone Soccer | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: A drone soccer competition where teams pilot custom-built, caged drones through an obstacle-filled arena to score points by flying through a circular goal ring. Matches are conducted as timed sprints focusing on agility, defense, and scoring precision.
eligibility: Teams of 2 to 5 members; cross-college teams are allowed.
requirements: Custom-built or configured drones with protective cages (no standard RTF models) and the use of only one main drone model.
details_text: Rules & Guidelines: Team Structure: Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 5 members . Cross-college teams are allowed—participants from different institutions can team up. Model Regulations: Each team must use its own custom-built or custom-configured drone wrapped in a protective cage/exoskeleton; exchanging models or components between teams during match rounds is strictly prohibited. Standard RTF (Ready-To-Fly) commercial consumer drones are not allowed, though pre-programmed flight controllers and stabilization boards are permitted. Only one main drone model can be used throughout all competition rounds. Flight and Conduct Rules: No trial attempts are allowed in Round 1, but teams will receive a 2-minute warm-up/trial period before Round 2 matches. Lifting or repositioning the drone manually during active gameplay is strictly prohibited. A drone that crashes and is unable to take off within the allotted restart window immediately forfeits that specific attempt or round. The competition organizers and judges hold the final decision on all match rules, scoring disputes, and safety calls. Event Structure: Round 1: Drone Soccer Arena Showdown: Obstacle & Defender Navigation: Teams must pilot their caged drones through an active arena featuring physical obstacles and designated opponent defense zones. Goal Scoring Task: Teams must navigate their drone past defensive barricades and maneuver it cleanly through the elevated circular Goal Ring to score points. Each successful goal scored within the match time earns points based on precision and execution. If a goal attempt fails, misses, or bounces off the goal frame, no points are awarded, but no negative penalty is incurred. Teams can immediately reset and attempt another run. Match Execution: Matches are conducted in timed sprints where agility, mid-air defense, collision recovery, and scoring accuracy determine the final winners.

title: Multirotor | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: A two-round drone competition where teams navigate through rings and obstacles to complete a payload delivery task. Participants must fly custom-built drones to score points through precision maneuvering and QR code identification.
eligibility: Teams of 2 to 6 members; inter-college teams are permitted.
requirements: A custom-built drone (no RTF models) equipped with an onboard camera for QR scanning.
details_text: Rules: Team Structure: Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 6 members. Participants from different colleges can form a team. Model Regulations: Each team must have its own custom-built drone; exchanging models between teams is strictly prohibited. RTF (Ready-To-Fly) models are not allowed, but pre-programmed boards can be used. Only one model can be used throughout all competition rounds. Flight and Conduct Rules: No trial attempts are allowed in Round 1, but teams can have a 2-minute trial before Round 2. Lifting the drone manually to improve position during any round is not allowed. Any failed landing attempt that does not result in a score immediately ends the round. The competition organizers and judges hold the final decision on any disputes. Event Structure: Round 1: Teams must fly their drone through 5 circular rings placed at varying heights (between 1 meter to 2.5 meters). Each ring carries different points based on difficulty. Teams must avoid touching the rings to earn points. Skipping a ring results in no points but does not incur a penalty. Maximum time for completion: 8 minutes. Qualification Criteria: Teams with the highest scores will advance to Round 2. Round 2: Obstacle Navigation: Teams must maneuver through multiple obstacles, which will be disclosed on the spot. Payload Task: The onboard camera scans a QR code to identify a specific payload. If scanning fails, teams can receive the QR details manually but will lose detection points. The identified payload must be dropped into a designated area. No penalty for unsuccessful drops, but no points are awarded either.

title: Beat The Market | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: This two-round competition challenges participants to build a stock portfolio based on financial analysis and subsequently develop a machine learning model to predict the future prices of those selected stocks.
eligibility: UG and PG college students; teams of up to 5 members.
requirements: Team formation, portfolio construction with financial justification, and machine learning model development.
details_text: Event Structure: Online Round: Portfolio Building & Analysis: All registered teams will receive details of 20 virtual stocks, including their technical and fundamental analysis. Participants must study the stocks and create a portfolio of 8 stocks using a virtual fund of ₹20 lakh. Teams must present a rationale for their selection, supported by financial statements, news articles, or relevant market data. Bonus Challenge: Justify why the remaining 12 stocks were excluded from your portfolio. ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) factors may be incorporated into the portfolio for additional evaluation. Portfolios will be assessed based on stock performance two years into the future, assuming the investments were made in the current year. Offline Round: Machine Learning-Based Stock Price Prediction: Teams will create a Machine Learning model to predict stock prices for each of the 8 selected stocks in their portfolio. A time series model can be used to forecast future price movements. Historical stock data (till Dec 2024) will be provided for training the model. The model will be evaluated on stock prices from 2025-2026. The team with the best-performing model will win the competition. A bonus round will be held, with further details provided on campus. Guidelines: Team Composition & Registration: Each team can have up to 5 members (both UG and PG students are eligible). A participant cannot be part of multiple teams in the same event. The competition will challenge participants across areas such as penetration testing, reverse engineering, cryptography, and vulnerability exploitation , requiring them to choose the right tools and techniques to solve increasingly challenging problems. Winners will be determined based on their total score. In case of a tie, the participant/team with the faster submission time will be given preference. details_text: Overview Welcome to Singularity 2.0, the premier national-level hackathon where the conventional rules of technology break down! Born to cultivate a relentless building culture, Singularity 2.0 has evolved into a high-stakes arena for the brightest engineering minds across the country. This is an intensive, 18-hour offline sprint engineered to test your technical endurance, collaborative spirit, and execution. Forget basic tutorials and generic templates. At Singularity 2.0, you will step into a frictionless environment designed for one purpose: building disruptive, real-world solutions. What to Expect at Singularity 18-Hour Sprint: Build, test, and deploy under extreme time constraints. Elite Collaboration: Form cross-disciplinary teams to tackle real-world bottlenecks. Expert Mentorship: Get real-time guidance from industry experts. Production-Ready Builds: Transform ambitious concepts into fully functional prototypes. Participation Fee Singularity 2.0 is a paid hackathon . Shortlisted teams proceeding to the offline hackathon will be required to pay a ₹1,000 participation fee per team, irrespective of team size . Our Theme: The Technological Singularity In astrophysics, a singularity is a point of infinite density, often at the heart of a black hole, where the standard laws of physics completely cease to function. We have adopted this cosmic phenomenon to represent the rapidly accelerating frontier of the modern digital landscape. We are approaching a technological tipping point where artificial intelligence, automation, and interconnected networks are growing at an unstoppable, irreversible pace. This theme is a direct call to step across the event horizon. We challenge you to dismantle standard engineering paradigms and harness the raw power of our four core tracks: AI-Enabled Hardware, Health & Emergency Services, FinTech, and Environmental Technologies. Just as a physical singularity warps reality around it, this hackathon empowers you to warp the fabric of modern technology. At Singularity 2.0, you aren't just wiring hardware or writing lines of code; you are forging the architecture of tomorrow. Prepare to disrupt the status quo, engineer without constraints, and build the impossible.

The Second Runners-up will receive a cash reward of INR 75,000 and PPIs (Pre-Placement Interviews) at Eurogrip.

title: KAINOS

description: KAINOS 2026–27 – National Student Innovation & Entrepreneurship Challenge is a national-level initiative by the KIIT School of Innovation and Entrepreneurial Leadership (KSIEL), designed to bring together final-year…
details_text: KAINOS 2026–27 – National Student Innovation & Entrepreneurship Challenge is a national-level initiative by the KIIT School of Innovation and Entrepreneurial Leadership (KSIEL), designed to bring together final-year undergraduate students from across India to identify real-world challenges and develop innovative, impactful solutions. Moving beyond conventional hackathons and idea-generation competitions, KAINOS offers a structured, five-month journey that takes participants from identifying a problem and understanding user needs to validating solutions, developing prototypes, and pitching their ideas. The programme is organised across three progressive phases – SPARK, BUILD, and RISE – providing participants with opportunities to learn, collaborate, receive mentorship, and refine their ideas with guidance from industry experts, practitioners, and founders. Selected teams will progress through six zonal build labs and eventually compete at the national finale at KIIT, Bhubaneswar. Innovation Themes KAINOS follows an open-innovation approach, encouraging participants to identify and address challenges across diverse domains, including: Health, Life Sciences & Well-being AgriTech, Food Systems & Blue Economy Climate, Environment & Circular Economy AI, Digital Technologies & Cyber-enabled Solutions Education, Skills & Future of Work Mobility, Smart Cities & Infrastructure Financial Inclusion, Social Innovation & Community Solutions Open Innovation: Participants can also explore problems beyond the listed themes, provided they demonstrate the problem, users affected, and potential impact. Who Can Participate? KAINOS is open to final-year undergraduate students pursuing their degrees at colleges and universities across India, regardless of their academic discipline. Interdisciplinary collaboration is encouraged. Team size: 2–4 members. Each team must have one designated Team Lead. Team members can belong to one institution or a maximum of two institutions. Existing student projects, prototypes, and early-stage student-led startups are welcome, subject to disclosure. There is no registration fee at any stage . Programme Structure Phase I – SPARK: National Opportunity Hunt The first phase focuses on identifying real-world problems, understanding the people affected, gathering evidence, and developing an initial solution concept. Teams will submit a Problem Card along with a 90-second video pitch. Around 500 teams will be shortlisted for the next phase. Phase II – BUILD: Six Zonal Build Labs Shortlisted teams will participate in masterclasses, mentor clinics, and structured learning sessions focused on problem validation, value proposition, business models, MVP/PoC development, IP awareness, and impact. The phase concludes with zonal pitches, with 50 teams progressing to the national finale. Phase III – RISE: National Finale The top 50 teams will come together at KIIT, Bhubaneswar, for the national finale. The phase will feature venture clinics, interactions with founders and industry leaders, national pitches, and a rapid challenge based on a new problem. Rewards and Recognition With ₹5,00,000 in total prize money across 24 awards , KAINOS offers national recognition and opportunities for promising student innovators. National Champion – ₹1,20,000 National Runner-up – ₹80,000 National Second Runner-up – ₹40,000 Zonal Build Excellence Awards – 10 awards of ₹15,000 each Category Awards – 10 awards of ₹10,000 each Finalist / Impact Recognition Award – ₹10,000 Participants can also benefit from stage-wise certificates, structured mentorship, expert feedback, national exposure, and potential pathways towards validation, incubation, and further venture development through KIIT-NEST. One registration covers all three phases. Participants begin their journey with SPARK, and shortlisted teams progress to BUILD and RISE through the selection process. details_text: L’Oréal Brandstorm is a global innovation challenge by the L’Oréal Group. It gives young minds a platform to reimagine the future of beauty through technology and innovation. You’ll build your creativity, entrepreneurial mindset and problem-solving skills while tackling real business challenges. Brandstorm is about more than cracking an innovation. It’s about growing. You’ll work closely with teammates, open your mind to new perspectives and learn directly from the industry. You’ll challenge your assumptions as your ideas meet those of bright minds from around the world. Senior leaders, brand managers and HR mentor you through the domestic and international rounds. Beyond a competition, Brandstorm is built to develop your resilience, curiosity and ability to turn concepts into reality. Get ready to learn, innovate and grow, because in Brandstorm you don’t just compete; you create the future. Brandstorm mission – what we expect from you Today, over 2.2 billion people live with a skin condition, and 850 million people plan to undergo an aesthetic procedure. The need for dermatological expertise has never been greater. Your Brandstorm 2027 mission is to: PIONEER AI-POWERED SKIN HEALTH AND BEAUTY Shape the future of skin health and beauty by bridging AI, medical science and life-changing human impact. Join L’Oréal Brandstorm 2027, in partnership with the L’Oréal Luxe Beauty division, and choose your playing field: Playing Field 1: Pioneer life-changing solutions Develop breakthrough products and services that improve people’s everyday lives and pioneer skin health and beauty. These can span skincare, scalp care, supplements and products that complement aesthetic procedures. Explore how AI can shape the next generation of solutions, from conception and development to discovery, use and experience. Playing Field 2: Design personalised support & education Give healthcare professionals and consumers access to reliable dermatological knowledge through social media, AI and other advanced technologies. In a world full of misinformation, how can science become the universal source of truth again? Use medical authority, congresses, beauty tech and brand activations to make information personalised, accessible and easy to understand. Playing Field 3: Reinvent the doctor-patient relationship Rethink how patients and doctors relate now that AI, beauty apps and new services give patients more access to information. Explore how AI can improve the whole patient journey: Booking an appointment and preparing for the consultation Diagnosis support and explanations Follow-up care, including pharmacies, teleconsultations and points of sale Keep the medical edge at the core, from prescription to product discovery and purchase. Responsible AI note: All solutions should minimise bias and support inclusivity across skin tones (Fitzpatrick phototypes I–VI), ages and genders. They must also meet the highest standards of medical ethics, data privacy and human oversight. Join L’Oréal Brandstorm 2027 , in partnership with the L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty division , and bring your boldest ideas to life. description: The 5th International Conference on Global Trends in Engineering and Technological Advancement (ICGTETA’27), organized by the Department of Research and Development, Gojan School of Business and Technology, Chennai, is…
details_text: The 5th International Conference on Global Trends in Engineering and Technological Advancement (ICGTETA’27), organized by the Department of Research and Development, Gojan School of Business and Technology, Chennai, is a global platform for researchers, academicians, industry professionals, innovators, and students to present original research work, exchange innovative ideas, and discuss emerging trends in engineering and technological advancement.The conference aims to promote interdisciplinary collaboration, encourage research innovation, and address real-world challenges through sustainable technological solutions. Participants will have the opportunity to share their research findings, interact with experts, and explore advancements across engineering, management, business, and interdisciplinary sciences.The conference will be conducted in online mode on 20th January 2027.
